title: North Dakota State wins first game as FBS program
summary: The Fargodome was a-rockin'.
full_text: The Fargodome was a-rockin'. Jacksonville State shouldn't have gone a-knockin'. North Dakota State, a longtime FCS powerhouse, made the official jump to the FBS division on Saturday with an easy win over the Gamecocks, 33-7. (It didn't start so easy; the game was tied 7-7 at the half.) The $17.5 million to graduate to the Mountain West apparently was money well spent. And it sparked plenty of excitement at the Fargodome, which seemed to be a far better football environment on Saturday than the L.A. Coliseum. "I can't wait to go through this process of making this move up," NDSU coach Tim Polasek said after the game. " This is step No. 1 . I just think for Fargo, and for our university, this can be explosive, and we're excited about this season." The Bison outgained Jacksonville State 373-170 yards in the game. NDSU has produced plenty of NFL players over the years — including quarterback Carson Wentz (No. 2 overall in 2016), quarterback Trey Lance (No. 3 overall in 2021), tackle Grey Zabel (No. 18 overall in 2025), Packers receiver Christian Watson (second-round pick in 2022), and Buccaneers tackle Cody Mauch (second-round pick in 2023).
author: Mike Florio

title: Dolphins waive QB Cam Miller
summary: The Dolphins traded Quinn Ewers to the Jaguars on Saturday and they've parted ways with another backup quarterback on Sunday.
full_text: '' The Dolphins traded Quinn Ewers to the Jaguars on Saturday and they've parted ways with another backup quarterback on Sunday. According to multiple reports, they have waived Cam Miller as they move to set their initial 53-man roster. The move would leave undrafted rookie Mark Gronowski as the only quarterback behind Malik Willis, but there's been no indication that the team plans to hold onto Gronowski through the final cuts. Miller and/or Gronowski could return to the practice squad if they clear waivers, but it seems likely that the Dolphins have their eye on bringing in someone from another team to serve as the No. 2 behind Willis. Miller was a 2025 sixth-round pick by the Raiders and the Dolphins signed him off of their practice squad late last season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bills agree to trade C Sedrick Van Pran-Granger to Colts
summary: The Colts are adding an offensive lineman to the roster on Sunday.
full_text: The Colts are adding an offensive lineman to the roster on Sunday. Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports that the Bills have agreed to trade center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger to Indianapolis. The Bills will also trade a 2027 seventh-round pick with the Colts sending a 2027 sixth-rounder back to Buffalo. Van Pran-Granger was a 2024 fifth-round pick by the Bills and he played in 31 regular season games for the team. He started two of those contests and also appeared in three playoff games. Tanor Bortolini is the starting center for the Colts and Van-Pran Granger will likely be slotted into a backup role with his new team.
author: Josh Alper

title: ACC debuted FIFA-style ref cam on Saturday
summary: The NFL is lagging when it comes to innovation.
full_text: At a time when the SEC has made plenty of news for not wanting NFL players, the ACC has made a little news for something the NFL should want. During Saturday's game between North Carolina State and Virginia, the conference that introduced officiating transparency in 2025 added a FIFA-style ref cam . It's absolutely something the NFL should embrace . Regardless of its potential value in the review process, it looks great. It gives viewers another way of experiencing the game, with a viewpoint that is more immersive and first-person than any other available camera angles. The decision to let viewers see and hear the replay-review sausage being made, along with the new ref cam, makes the ACC not only the most innovative college football conference but also puts it ahead of the NFL. As Sean Keeley of Awful Announcing recently explained, the ACC plans to have even more officiating transparency in 2026. Last year, the ACC presented 27 games featuring full transparency. This year, it will have 27 such games in the first three weeks . At the professional level, the UFL has done the same thing. Former NFL senior V.P. of officiating Dean Blandino, who now works for both Fox and the UFL, has addressed both the value of transparency and the reasons why the NFL may be reluctant to go there . Broncos coach Sean Payton, a member of the NFL's Competition Committee, believes the league will nevertheless make the change within the next two or three years . The NFL should already be there. The fact that the UFL and the ACC have taken the lead on such an important issue in the age of bet! bet! bet! becomes a bad look for America's preeminent sports league. The more the NFL drags its feet, the more glaring it will become. Especially if other college conferences get on board with giving viewers the kind of access to officiating that will help the tinfoil-hat crowd realize that, when critical decisions are being made, the fix is absolutely not in. Frankly, the fact that lesser leagues and levels of the sport have fully embraced something the NFL continues to resist will serve only to increase suspicions as to whether something fishy may be going on when the process of reviewing plays slips behind a curtain to which no one on the outside has access.
author: Mike Florio

title: Colts WR Keenan Allen arrested for DWI
summary: Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen was arrested in Indianapolis early on Sunday morning.
full_text: ' Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen was arrested in Indianapolis early on Sunday morning. Per a police report obtained by multiple media outlets, Allen was arrested around 1 a.m. on charges of driving while intoxicated (DWI) and DWI endangering a person. Both charges are misdemeanors and Allen has not been formally charged at this point. The Colts released a statement about the matter on Sunday. “We are aware of the incident involving Keenan Allen last night," the statement said. "We are in the process of gathering more information and have no further comment at this time.” Allen signed with the Colts a couple of weeks ago and had one catch in Saturday's preseason game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bears to trade DT Gervon Dexter to Falcons for CB Clark Phillips and fifth-round pick
summary: Defensive tackle Gervon Dexter is on the move ahead of Sunday afternoon's deadline to set 53-man rosters around the league.
full_text: Defensive tackle Gervon Dexter is on the move ahead of Sunday afternoon's deadline to set 53-man rosters around the league. According to multiple reports, the Bears have agreed to trade Dexter to the Falcons. Cornerback Clark Phillips and a fifth-round pick will head back to Chicago. Dexter was a 2023 second-round pick by the Bears. He started all 19 games that the Bears played last season and had 48 tackles, six sacks and two fumble recoveries. Grady Jarrett, Neville Gallimore, Kentavius Street, James Lynch, and sixth-round pick Jordan van den Berg remain on the depth chart as options on the interior. The Falcons added Phillips as a 2023 fourth-rounder and he played in 27 games in his first two seasons, but he only played in one game last year due to a triceps injury. He was vying for a backup role in Atlanta.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dan Campbell "comfortable" with Jacob Saylors as Lions' No. 2 running back
summary: The Lions came into the summer with a plan for Isiah Pacheco to be their No. 2 running back behind Jahmyr Gibbs, but Pacheco has dealt with multiple injuries this month and that may lead them in a different direction.
full_text: The Lions came into the summer with a plan for Isiah Pacheco to be their No. 2 running back behind Jahmyr Gibbs, but Pacheco has dealt with multiple injuries this month and that may lead them in a different direction. Jacob Saylors ran 17 times for 100 yards in Saturday's preseason finale and he had 14 carries for 87 yards in the team's other two games. It is Year 2 for Saylors in Detroit, but he only played eight offensive snaps while seeing regular time on special teams in his 15 appearances. The offensive action may have been limited, but head coach Dan Campbell said on Saturday that Saylors's experience in the system leaves him comfortable about moving forward with him in the backup role. "I am," Campbell said, via Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press . "I’m comfortable with those guys. And I just like the thought of having a guy in our system, think that's important. Knows our terminology, knows our guys, knows the protections. Just kind of knows it all, man. Understands our quarterback and how he thinks. I just think that's important." Pacheco added a back injury to a sprained MCL recently and his status for Week 1 is up in the air. If he can't go, Saylors is in line for a chance to build on the positive impression he made in the preseason.
author: Josh Alper

title: 12 NFL teams did not play their starting quarterbacks in the preseason
summary: The growing trend of NFL teams keeping their quarterbacks out of the preseason has reached the point where more than one-third of starting quarterbacks did not take a single snap in this year's preseason.
full_text: '' The growing trend of NFL teams keeping their quarterbacks out of the preseason has reached the point where more than one-third of starting quarterbacks did not take a single snap in this year's preseason. The reasons were different for different teams: Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes and Colts quarterback Daniel Jones are recovering from season-ending injuries. Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott and Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson haven't played in the preseason in years, across multiple coaching staffs. Rams coach Sean McVay is perhaps the most cautious coach in the league when it comes to avoiding preseason injuries, so of course reigning MVP quarterback Matthew Stafford didn't play. But the result is the same: If you're tuning into a preseason game, you're increasingly likely to see backup quarterbacks exclusively, and if you see a starter at all, it will typically only be for a series or two. Here's the full list of teams that didn't play their starting quarterbacks at all this preseason, via Mike Reiss of ESPN : Seahawks: Sam Darnold. Patriots: Drake Maye. Cowboys: Dak Prescott. Ravens: Lamar Jackson. Steelers: Aaron Rodgers. Colts: Daniel Jones. Jaguars: Trevor Lawrence. Chiefs: Patrick Mahomes. Eagles: Jalen Hurts. Lions: Jared Goff. Saints: Tyler Shough. Rams: Matthew Stafford.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bears third-round pick Zavion Thomas scores 97-yard touchdown on his first NFL play
summary: Thomas made his preseason debut on Saturday and put on a show.
full_text: ''' Bears rookie wide receiver Zavion Thomas missed the first two preseason games with a knee injury. When he finally got on the field on Saturday, he put on a show. Thomas caught a pass from Tyson Bagent and raced 97 yards to the end zone on his very first NFL play, and finished his first preseason game with five catches for 140 yards, plus a 31-yard punt return and a 22-yard kickoff return. Asked if anyone had a chance of catching him on his long touchdown, the speedy Thomas said he didn't know which Titans player was chasing him, but answered, "Nah, he didn't have a chance." Thomas said that even while he couldn't practice because of his knee, older players were helping him prepare for the moment when he would be on the field, so he expected to play well once he got medical clearance. "It felt amazing. The preparation put into it, it was something that I expected," Thomas said. Thomas didn't put up big numbers during his four years of college football (two at Mississippi State and two at LSU), but he put up an eye-popping number at the Scouting Combine: 4.28 seconds in the 40-yard dash. That got him plenty of attention, and the Bears took a chance on him in the third round. Bagent knows Thomas's speed is a huge asset to the Bears' offense. "Give Zavion a chance and then you're able to see that speed, which is a big reason why he's here," Bagent said. "I think that was Zavion Thomas's first play in the NFL, so greatest start in NFL history."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Dan Campbell not worried about his kicker after Jake Bates misses two extra points
summary: Lions kicker Jake Bates did not finish the preseason strong on Saturday.
full_text: ''' Lions kicker Jake Bates did not finish the preseason strong on Saturday. Lions coach Dan Campbell is not concerned. Bates did not attempt any field goals in the Lions' preseason finale but did attempt three extra points, missing two of them. Bates is the only kicker on the Lions' roster, so he's in no danger of getting cut, and Campbell said the Lions have full confidence in him. "No, I'm not worried about Bates. He just pushed them a little bit. He'll be fine. He'll be fine," Campbell said. Bates also missed a field goal in last week's preseason game, and he wasn't as good in 2025 as he was in 2024, when the Lions signed him out of the United Football League and he became one of the NFL's best kickers. It wouldn't be unreasonable for the Lions to have some concerns at kicker heading into the season, but Campbell insists he doesn't.
author: Michael David Smith

title: UNC G.M. Michael Lombardi's lawyer calls ongoing investigation a "witch hunt"
summary: UNC G.M.
full_text: UNC G.M. Michael Lombardi remains on paid administrative leave while the school investigates him. Recently, his lawyer has complained about the duration of the probe. On Saturday, Tom Mars attacked the investigation in comments to David Ubben of The Athletic . “If UNC had grounds to fire Michael for cause, they wouldn’t need to conduct such a far-ranging, lengthy witch hunt ," Mars told Ubben. "They would have done so by now. I think the motive behind the investigation goes further than a $1.5 million buyout. After all, UNC could fire Michael (or the athletic director or any head coach) for no reason at all just by paying their buyout. In today’s world, $1.5 million is just a drop in the bucket, so there must be other reasons behind this multimillion-dollar investigation.” Previously, Mars provided similar comments to David Hale of ESPN, calling the investigation a " snipe hunt ." Lombardi and Mars are entitled to their opinions on the matter. But if the situation surfaced, as it has been reported, from a complaint made by a former employee to the school, North Carolina has an obligation to conduct a full and thorough investigation. Through it all, Lombardi is still getting paid. Mars almost seems to be daring UNC to fire Lombardi for cause. If that happens, Lombardi's $1.5 million salary will be cut off. While he could have grounds to challenge the decision, he wouldn't be getting paid while the case proceeds. Generally speaking, it's always better to be getting paid than to not be getting paid. If Lombardi and Mars want the investigation to be wrapped up quickly, Lombardi may not like the short-term impact a final decision has on his paycheck.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Saints will keep Spencer Rattler despite trade interest
summary: The Saints waived fourth quarterback Hunter Dekkers on Saturday, leaving Spencer Rattler and Zach Wilson behind Tyler Shough.
full_text: The Saints waived fourth quarterback Hunter Dekkers on Saturday, leaving Spencer Rattler and Zach Wilson behind Tyler Shough. The team received trade interest in Rattler, but plans to keep him, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports. If the Saints do indeed keep three quarterbacks on their roster, the question then becomes who will serve as the backup on game day. Rattler, a fifth-round pick in 2024, competed for the starting job a year ago and ended up starting the first eight games of the season. The Saints went 1-7, and Shough replaced him.\ In two seasons, Rattler has passed for 2,903 yards with 12 touchdowns and 10 interceptions. He was 30-of-44 for 262 yards with an interception in three preseason games. Rattler also ran for 30 yards and a touchdown on seven carries.
author: Charean Williams

title: Kyle Shanahan vaguely suggests George Kittle has "taken a step back"
summary: When 49ers tight end George Kittle recently emerged from the active/physically unable to perform list, many assumed it meant he'd be available to play in the Week 1 game against the Rams in Australia.
full_text: When 49ers tight end George Kittle recently emerged from the active/physically unable to perform list, many assumed it meant he'd be available to play in the Week 1 game against the Rams in Australia. After the recent preseason finale, however, coach Kyle Shanahan made a comment that could be interpreted as meaning Kittle has had a setback in his recovery from a torn Achilles tendon. While discussing whether various injured players will be available for the season-opening game, Shanahan mentioned Kittle's name, adding this: " who’s taken a step back ." It happened quickly. The comment was made almost in passing. There was no further explanation. Did Shanahan mean Kittle has had a setback? Did it mean he has taken a step back toward playing? Whatever Shanahan meant, it will surely be one of the main topics the next time Shanahan meets with reporters.
author: Mike Florio

title: College running back MicahJo Barnett dies after medical emergency on sideline
summary: MicahJo Barnett, a junior running back at William Jewell College in Missouri, died Saturday after experiencing a medical emergency on the sideline during a game, via the Associated Press.
full_text: MicahJo Barnett, a junior running back at William Jewell College in Missouri, died Saturday after experiencing a medical emergency on the sideline during a game, via the Associated Press. The incident happened roughly 20 minutes after kickoff of the game between William Jewel and Fort Lewis College. Barnett had scored a touchdown not long before the incident occurred. "Our thoughts and prayers are with MicahJo's family, our students, the Cardinal Football family, and the rest of our community during this time of loss," the school said in a message on its website. Barnett had scored with 5:15 remaining in the first quarter. The game was stopped with 4:32 left in the quarter. He had carried the ball six times, gaining 30 yards. A vigil for Barnett and his family was scheduled for Saturday night. We extend our condolences to MicahJo Barnett's family, friends, teammates, coaches, and fellow students at William Jewell College.
author: Mike Florio

title: Anthony Richardson the favorite to win backup QB job after preseason finale
summary: Anthony Richardson lost his starting job last year.
full_text: ' Anthony Richardson lost his starting job last year. It appears he has held onto the backup job this year. The Colts have not announced who will enter the season as Daniel Jones' backup, but Richardson outplayed Riley Leonard in the preseason. Richardson completed 7 of 10 passes for 80 yards in the preseason finale against the Lions on Saturday. He finished the preseason 21-of-33 for 249 yards and an interception. "I just wanted to go out there and operate the offense and be confident," Richardson said, via Abby Halpin of the team website. "I was out there with the starters, so I just wanted to go out there and showcase that I could manage the game and be out there and let it rip. I think I did that to a certain extent." Leonard was 3-for-7 for 48 yards and an interception against the Lions, finished the preseason 20-of-42 for 199 yards and two interceptions. The Colts did not throw a touchdown pass in three preseason games. "I just want to do my best and put my best foot forward," Richardson said. "I want everyone to win and everybody to reach their goals, dreams and aspirations that they've wanted since they were a little kid." Richardson, the fourth overall pick in 2023, is entering the final year of his contract.
author: Charean Williams

title: Todd Monken continues wrestling "somewhat" with fates of Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green
summary: The Browns know what they'll be doing as to the top two quarterbacks on the depth chart.
full_text: The Browns know what they'll be doing as to the top two quarterbacks on the depth chart. As to the other two, decision time is coming. Coach Todd Monken acknowledged after Thursday's preseason finale that, as to Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green, " We can’t keep everybody ." Speaking to reporters on Saturday, after some cuts were already made , Monken was asked whether the team is still grappling with the quarterback issue at the bottom of the depth chart. “Somewhat," Monken said. "Like a lot of players, we don’t want to lose any good players that have a future with the Browns, so we’ve still got some discussions to have. But I was very impressed with both Dillon and Taylen. Both did it differently, but Dillon’s at least played. He’s played last year, he’s gotten more reps than Taylen, so he looked like it, and he obviously operated very well. Taylen did the things we thought he would do, which was make some plays with his feet, and there were no issues in terms of the operation." The issue is whether to keep either or neither on the roster, with the outside chance of keeping all four. Both Gabriel and Green would be exposed to waivers if released with the idea of signing them to the practice squad. Gabriel, who had a near-perfect passer rating against the Patriots of 157.9 with three touchdown passes on 15 throws, could be traded. And the most obvious destination would be Atlanta, where former Browns coach Kevin Stefanski has a potential none-of-the-above situation as Week 1 approaches. The Browns still have time to figure it out. But not much. As of this posting, the deadline to get to 53 is less than 28 hours away.
author: Mike Florio

title: The annual frenzy of NFL transactions happens this weekend
summary: Rosters must cut from 90 to 53 by Sunday at 4:00 p.m. ET.
full_text: The Turk will be very busy this weekend. The traditional name for the in-house harbinger of doom, each team's Turk will be telling players on the bubble that the coach wants to see them. "And bring your playbook," he usually adds. It's one of the basic realities of a sport that has 90 players on the roster until the limit plunges, in one fell swoop, to 53. And it will happen through an avalanche of moves that will trim the rosters, build practice squads of up to 16 players, and then spark a flurry of additional cuts and signings at the bottom of the roster. The process is the most basic reminder of the reality that the supply of willing NFL players far outweighs the demand. And that, once the preseason ends, the demand for players to play in the games that don't count instantly evaporates. Players who are released with four or more years of service instantly become free agents. Players who aren't "vested veterans" migrate to the waivers system. Any team can claim a player on waivers, with no limit on the number taken. The players are awarded by priority based on the 2026 draft order, with the Raiders having dibs on all of them. This means that players who make the 53-man roster as of Sunday at 6:00 p.m. ET may not be around for long. For every player claimed on waivers, another player needs to be removed from the roster. The roster cuts at one point were made on the Saturday of Labor Day weekend, only five days before the first game. When the season moved to 17 games, the process was accelerated by a week or so, giving the players who make the team a break before Week 1 preparations begin in earnest. The deadline had been Tuesday. This year, the decision to move the first game to the Wednesday after Labor Day (with two teams heading to Australia for a game the next day) prompted a shift to Sunday. All in all, it's a harsh process. The teams largely have become desensitized to it, because it's a fundamental step in building a team. And the players who don't have starting jobs set in stone understand that there's a risk they'll be leaving their current teams, possibly temporarily. Possibly for good. The practice squad helps to soften the blow. And those 16 spots for 32 teams create up to 512 more jobs. The churning of the roster and the practice squad will continue, throughout the regular season and into the playoffs. The availability of short-term injured reserve will create opportunities. Players who aren't attached to a team will get tryouts. For those who don't make it to a 53-man roster, the dream isn't dead. It's in limbo. And many of them will choose to stay in shape and wait for the phone to ring.
author: Mike Florio

title: Giants cut eight, including WR Isaiah Hodgins
summary: The Giants have begun reducing their roster to 53 players.
full_text: The Giants have begun reducing their roster to 53 players. They announced eight cuts ahead of Sunday's 6 p.m. ET deadline. The Giants will cut CB Ugo Amadi, RB Damon Bankston, TE Josiah Deguara, DL Leki Fotu, WR Isaiah Hodgins, OL Brenden Jaimes, LB Anfernee Orji and WR Kobe Prentice. Hodgins has spent the past 3 1/2 seasons with the Giants, making 66 catches for 708 yards and eight touchdowns. The moves come the day after the Giants wrapped up the preseason with a 23-6 victory over the Jets. The claiming period for players placed on waivers at the roster reduction will expire at 1 p.m. ET on Monday. The Giants are fifth in the claiming order. Teams can then establish a practice squad of 17 players, as long as one player qualifies and is designated as an international player.
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Jets waive DT Mazi Smith
summary: The Jets are releasing defensive tackle Mazi Smith, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
full_text: The Jets are releasing defensive tackle Mazi Smith, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Smith is a former first-round draft pick who was part of the Quinnen Williams deal last season. Harrison Phillips, David Onyemata, T'Vondre Sweat, Jowon Briggs and fourth-round pick Darrell Jackson Jr. were ahead of Smith on the depth chart. The writing was on the wall for Smith in the offseason when the Jets traded for Sweat and signed Onyemata in free agency. The Cowboys selected Smith with the 26th overall pick in the 2023 draft. He spent a little more than two years in Dallas before the Cowboys sent him to New York as part of the blockbuster trade for Williams. Smith appeared in eight games last season, including only three with the Jets. In his career, Smith has 57 tackles, two sacks and six quarterback hits in 42 games.
author: Charean Williams

title: Steelers trade Broderick Jones to Cowboys
summary: After three seasons in Pittsburgh, offensive tackle Broderick Jones will be moving to Dallas.
full_text: After three seasons in Pittsburgh, offensive tackle Broderick Jones will be moving to Dallas. The Steelers have traded Jones to the Cowboys, according to multiple reports. There is no immediate word on the compensation that will go back to Pittsburgh. The Steelers took Jones out of Georgia with the 14th overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft and he has started 38 games through his first three NFL seasons. But last year he suffered a season-ending neck injury in Week 12, and there have been reports out of training camp this year that, even though he's medically cleared, he looks like he has lost strength. Jones is in the fourth and final season of his four-year rookie contract. He is scheduled to make $1.5 million this season, and he'll hit free agency in 2027.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Cardinals trade RB Corey Kiner to Patriots for a 2028 seventh-round pick
summary: The Patriots have added some depth at running back through a trade with the Cardinals.
full_text: The Patriots have added some depth at running back through a trade with the Cardinals. Corey Kiner is being traded from Arizona to New England, with the Patriots sending the Cardinals a 2028 seventh-round pick in the deal, according to Adam Schefter. The Cardinals were planning to waive Kiner, and the Patriots, who are 31st in the waiver order, thought some other team would claim him ahead of them in the waiver order. So the Patriots used a late-round pick a year and a half from now to make sure they could land Kiner. Kiner played four games for the Cardinals as an undrafted rookie last year and looked solid, carrying the ball 12 times for 58 yards, adding two catches for 15 yards, and returning one kickoff for 22 yards. The Cardinals, who added first-round pick Jeremiyah Love and free agent Tyler Allgeier to their running back room this offseason, decided they no longer had a place on their roster for Kiner. Now his place is in New England.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ravens agree to trade OT Diego Pounds to the Chiefs
summary: The Ravens and Chiefs have agreed to a trade ahead of Sunday's deadline for teams to set their initial 53-man rosters.
full_text: The Ravens and Chiefs have agreed to a trade ahead of Sunday's deadline for teams to set their initial 53-man rosters. NFL Media reports that the Ravens will send offensive tackle Diego Pounds to Kansas City. There's no word on compensation coming back to Baltimore. Pounds signed with the Ravens after going undrafted out of Ole Miss this year. He started 24 games at left tackle for the Rebels over the last two seasons and also saw time at the position during three years at North Carolina. The Chiefs list Josh Simmons and Jaylon Moore as the starting tackles on their depth chart with Esa Pole and Kahlil Benson on the second string.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patriots release RB Hassan Haskins
summary: The Patriots traded for running back Corey Kiner on Saturday and they made space for him by parting ways with another back.
full_text: The Patriots traded for running back Corey Kiner on Saturday and they made space for him by parting ways with another back. They announced that they have released Hassan Haskins when they confirmed their trade with Arizona for Kiner. Haskins signed with the Patriots earlier this month and saw action in all three of the team's preseason games. Haskins spent the last two seasons with the Chargers and entered the league as a Titans fourth-round pick in 2022. Kiner joins a running back room that also has TreVeyon Henderson, Rhamondre Stevenson, Lan Larison, JaMycal Hasty, and seventh-round pick Jam Miller in it at the moment.
author: Josh Alper

title: Steelers release LB Jamin Davis
summary: Linebacker Jamin Davis did not make it past final cuts with the Steelers.
full_text: Linebacker Jamin Davis did not make it past final cuts with the Steelers. The NFL's transaction report for Saturday shows that Davis was released. It also includes the 11 cuts that the Steelers announced on Friday as well as word that they have waived wide receiver Levi Wentz. Davis was a Washington first-round pick in 2021 and he has bounced between several teams since being released during the 2024 season. He had three tackles in two games for the Raiders last season. Wentz signed with the Seahawks after going undrafted out of Kansas. He was waived in June and signed with the Steelers a week later.
author: Josh Alper

title: LBs Tomon Fox, Monty Rice among first wave of Rams cuts
summary: A pair of veteran linebackers are among the first players let go by the Rams as they set their initial 53-man roster.
full_text: A pair of veteran linebackers are among the first players let go by the Rams as they set their initial 53-man roster. The NFL's transaction report for Saturday shows that the Rams have released Tomon Fox and Monty Rice. Both players signed with the Rams as free agents this offseason and are now free to sign with other teams. The Rams also waived defensive back Alex Cook, linebacker Devean Deal, wide receiver Tru Edwards, defensive back Steven Gilmore, defensive back Al'zillion Hamilton, offensive tackle Bryce Henderson, linebacker Nikhai Hill-Green, defensive back Alex Johnson, tight end Rohan Jones, defensive back Nate Valcarcel, tight end Dan Villari, and defensive tackle Payton Zdroik. Quarterback Matthew Caldwell was placed on injured reserve to round out the moves. With 16 players off the active roster and punter Jack Bouwmeester on the roster with an exemption as an international player, the Rams have 22 moves left to hit the 53-player limit.
author: Josh Alper

title: Falcons waive seven players, release three others
summary: The Falcons have started making moves ahead of Sunday's deadline to cut their roster to 53 players.
full_text: ' The Falcons have started making moves ahead of Sunday's deadline to cut their roster to 53 players. The NFL's daily transaction report for Saturday shows that they parted ways with 10 players. They also placed defensive back Darren Hall on injured reserve. Defensive lineman Eric Johnson, linebacker Channing Tindall, and offensive lineman Brandon Walton were all released and will not be subject to waiver claims from the rest of the teams in the league. Wide receiver Keelan Marion, tight end Josh Simon, offensive lineman Jaeden Roberts, offensive lineman Andrew Stueber, defensive lineman Devonnsha Maxwell, linebacker Daveren Rayner, and defensive back Keidron Smith are going to be on the waiver wire.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: 49ers cut Adrian Martinez as Kurtis Rourke wins No. 3 QB job
summary: The 49ers didn't see much of Curtis Rourke in the preseason as he missed the final two games with fractured ribs.
full_text: '' The 49ers didn't see much of Curtis Rourke in the preseason as he missed the final two games with fractured ribs. They saw enough of him, though, to keep him as their third quarterback. The 49ers are releasing Adrian Martinez, Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports, which leaves Rourke behind Brock Purdy and Mac Jones. Rourke started the team's first preseason game and went 12-of-14 for 101 yards while rushing for 14 yards on three carries. He broke three ribs during the game, forcing his exit and sending him to the hospital. He is expected to return to practice this week. Martinez appeared in all three preseason games, completing 36-of-68 passes for 346 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, while rushing eight times for 35 yards and one score.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bills will replace grass field at new stadium before home opener
summary: Large divots were a problem during the preseason.
full_text: When the Bills played their first preseason game at their new stadium two weeks ago, a "massive clump" of sod went flying, "roots, dirt, and all." One unnamed player even said, " The field is ass right now ." So, basically, the grass is ass — and the Bills are getting out something more than a lawnmower. Lance Lysowski of the Buffalo News reports that the entire surface will be replaced before the Week 2 Thursday night home opener against the Lions. It will be the first of three straight home games for the Bills. The Bills aren't conceding that the current field, which passed pregame inspection for Thursday night's preseason finale against the Steelers, is enough of a problem to require replacement. "You can be happy with the performance and playability and still make the change," Bills chief operating officer Pete Guelli told Lysowski. "As an organization, we’re committed to having the absolute best possible playing surface for the players. If it’s even slightly better, we’re going to make the change and err on the side of performance." The issue was divots. The goal will be to reduce their frequency and size. "It’s not a cure-all," Bills senior director of grounds Aaron Ramella told Lysowski. "We’re still going to have divots. It’s a living grass field. We’ll be better than where we’re at now. There will be a random push or random divot. That’s football. We’re not playing on a rug anymore." That's the best news. But one of the realities (and expenses) of a grass field is that it takes effort (and money) to make it high-quality. Although an overwhelming majority of players prefer grass to artificial turf, most would prefer a fake field to shoddy sod.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dolphins trade QB Quinn Ewers to Jaguars
summary: Quinn Ewers is on the move.
full_text: '' Quinn Ewers is on the move. According to a report from NFL Network, the Dolphins are trading Ewers to the Jaguars. The two teams will swap Day 3 draft picks in 2028 to complete the deal, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports. Ewers, 23, was a seventh-round pick in last year’s draft. He started three games for Miami late last season, with the club going 1-2 in those contests. He completed 66.3 percent of his passes for 662 yards with three touchdowns and three interceptions in his four appearances. The Dolphins have Cam Miller and Mark Gronowski remaining on their roster at quarterback behind starter Malik Willis. The Jaguars had Nick Mullens, Carter Bradley, and rookie Joey Aguilar on their roster behind starter Trevor Lawrence.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Packers waive DB Travion Fluellen to make room for Jonnu Smith
summary: Free agent tight end Jonnu Smith agreed to a one-year deal with the Packers earlier this week.
full_text: Free agent tight end Jonnu Smith agreed to a one-year deal with the Packers earlier this week. Smith signed his deal on Saturday, and the Packers needed to make room. In a corresponding move, the Packers waived defensive back Travion Fluellen, the team announced. Fluellen signed with the Packers on Aug. 11. Fluellen played collegiately at Houston Baptist for one season before transferring to Middle Tennessee State. In three seasons at Middle Tennessee State, he played 36 games and recorded 197 tackles, 7.5 tackles for loss, one sack, five interceptions and 16 pass breakups. As a senior in 2023, he ended the season ranked third on the team with 64 tackles, including 2.5 stops for loss, a team-high three interceptions and three pass breakups. Fluellen went undrafted in 2024, signing with the Saints as a college free agent. Fluellen spent the final five weeks of the 2024 season on the Saints' practice squad, but he did not appear in a game. The Saints signed him to a futures contract after the season. New Orleans waived him in June 2025, and he was not signed elsewhere last year.

title: Colts' Keenan Allen arrested Sunday morning in Indianapolis on DWI charges
summary: The six-time Pro Bowler was signed to a one-year deal less than two weeks ago to bolster a revamped wide receiver room alongside Alec Pierce and Josh Downs
full_text:
Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen was arrested Sunday morning in Indianapolis on drunken driving charges. He was picked up around 1 a.m. ET and later was saddled with driving while intoxicated (DWI) and DWI endangering a person charges, according to online jail records.
Allen, 34, was signed less than two weeks prior. The Colts concluded the preseason Saturday evening at home against the Lions . Allen caught one pass for 24 yards in the game.
Entering his 14th NFL season, the former California Golden Bear is a 6-time Pro Bowl selection with 1,055 career receptions, 12,051 career receiving yards and 70 career receiving touchdowns; just 949 yards shy of the 13,000 yards club, which has just 23 members all-time.
The former third-round pick has played 12 seasons for the Chargers and spent a gap year in between with Chicago in 2024. Last season, he caught 81 passes for 777 yards and 4 touchdowns in his return to Los Angeles.
It has been a busy offseason for the Colts at the receiver position. They rewarded Alec Pierce with a contract extension and then traded franchise stalwart Michael Pittman Jr. to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Pierce was activated from the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list and returned to practice earlier this week. Faced with entering the regular season without a proven commodity opposite Josh Downs and Pierce, the Colts moved to sign the veteran to a one-year deal.
Indianapolis opens the regular season Sunday, Sep. 13 at home against the Ravens .
author: Josh Edwards

title: 2026 NFL preseason Week 3 rookie QB grades: Ravens undrafted signal caller shines
summary: Rams first-round pick Ty Simpson and Ravens undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano earned the highest marks
full_text:
The NFL has put a bow on the 2026 preseason, and this year's rookie class of signal-callers has put the finishing touches on their first summer in the league. Now, the guillotine that is cut-down day looms.
While the status of players like Fernando Mendoza and Ty Simpson is rock solid, a large contingent of these young quarterbacks hopes to make their current team's 53-man roster or turn what they put on tape into a shot with another team (whether it be the active roster or practice squad) once the dust settles. And this weekend was the final opportunity for that group of players to make their mark.
How'd they do? Let's collect up all 17 rookie quarterbacks that suited up over the final week of the preseason and hand out our grades.
Draft status : 5th round, No. 178 overall (North Dakota State)
Payton saw the field on the final offensive possession of the night for Philadelphia in its preseason defeat by Cincinnati. The Payton-led offense went three-and-out and went backward by three yards. He missed both of his pass attempts and took a sack that lost three yards.
Draft status : 7th round, No. 249 overall (LSU)
Nussmeier got the nod in Kansas City's preseason finale against Seattle and played the entire game. He completed 22 of 34 passes for 198 yards, no touchdowns and an interception. The turnover on his second drive of the game proved costly as the Seahawks turned it into a field goal in a game that proved to be a 9-9 tie. Nussmeier settled down, however, and led scoring drives (all field goals) on his next two possessions. He hopes to make it onto the final 53-man roster and deepen a quarterback room that's headlined by Patrick Mahomes and top backup Justin Fields .
Draft status : Undrafted (Kansas)
It was a lackluster showing for the Kansas product as he got the start in Tampa Bay's preseason finale against Jacksonville. He completed 8-of-15 for 57 yards and was sacked three times, while adding nine yards on the ground on four carries. Daniels played into the third quarter, and the Bucs punted on six of his seven drives. The lone possession where they didn't boot the ball back to the opposition: Daniels fumbled, and the Jaguars recovered.
Draft status : Undrafted (Tennessee)
Aguilar took over in the fourth quarter of Jacksonville's exhibition with Tampa Bay, but didn't make many waves over his three drives. Over that stretch, the Jaguars punted once and turned the ball over on downs twice, for zero points. Aguilar completed 7-of-9 for 57 yards. He also fumbled but recovered the loose ball.
Draft status : 4th round, No. 110 overall (Clemson)
Cade Klubnik got the start for the Jets in their preseason finale against the Giants and was on hand for an opening drive touchdown. However, Klubnik was largely a passenger on the possession. After an interception gave the Jets the ball at the Giants' 36-yard line, running back Chip Trayanum did most of the heavy lifting, as he ran the ball nine times over the 10-play drive. The lone touch Klubnik had on the drive was nearly disastrous as he fumbled the ball, but was able to recover. For the day, he completed 6-of-13 for 59 yards and an interception. That pick came on the opening drive of the second quarter, where he couldn't layer the football over a Giants defender and instead threw it directly into his arms. The fourth-rounder flashed some promise this summer, but his final showing was spotty to say the least.
Draft status : Undrafted (Minnesota State-Moorhead)
Strand was the third quarterback up for Atlanta as they faced the Dolphins , with Tua Tagovailoa and Cooper Rush getting the nod before him. After taking over in the third quarter, Strand played the entire second half, but wasn't able to do similar damage to what he did against Indianapolis the week prior. He completed 6-of-7 for 44 yards, but that lone miss was an interception. He tossed the pick on a third-and-8 play from his own 17-yard line, which resulted in a field goal for Miami on the ensuing possession. The three possessions before the interception all resulted in a punt, and his final drive of the night ended with a kneel-down. Stand endeared himself this summer, but it's unclear if that'll result in the Falcons carrying four quarterbacks on the 53-man roster. Most likely, Atlanta will try to sneak him onto its practice squad unless more significant moves occur at the QB position that free up a spot.
Draft status : Undrafted (Iowa)
Gronowski took over in the second and finished his day with 97 yards through the air on 4-of-8 passing. He was sacked three times while adding 28 yards rushing on four attempts. Out of the gate, he orchestrated a scoring drive to begin the second half, traveling 66 yards over 11 plays before settling for a field goal. The most damming part of Gronowski's day, however, came on the following possession. The Dolphins pushed the ball down to Atlanta's 6-yard line, but Gronowski fumbled the snap on second-and-goal, and the Falcons recovered.
Draft status : 7th round, No. 223 overall (Rutgers)
Kaliakmanis' day was turnt sideways from the jump. He got the start in Washington's preseason finale against the Ravens , but found himself in a two-touchdown hole before really even getting his feet wet. That was thanks to running back Kaytron Allen fumbling on the first possession and giving the ball back to Baltimore after they had already scored on their first drive. The Kaliakmanis-led offense then punted on four of his next six possessions of the first half, with the other two consisting of a missed field goal attempt and a lone rush to simply run out the clock to head to the halftime locker room. Kaliakmanis completed 7-of-13 for 45 yards.
Draft status : Undrafted (UConn)
Fagnano didn't start in the preseason finale, but saw action early as he was in on Baltimore's second possession of the day following a fumble by the Commanders offense. The UConn product took advantage of the short field, leading a 30-yard touchdown drive that ended with him sneaking in for the goal-line score. Fagnano played into the third quarter and put Baltimore in scoring position on six of his seven drives. The Ravens scored three touchdowns with Fagnano in the driver's seat, but Tyler Loop missed two field goal attempts while he was under center. He finished his day 19-of-27 passing for 162 yards and two total touchdowns (one passing and one rushing).
Draft status : 1st round, No. 13 overall (Alabama)
Every Rams fan hopes this will be the last they see of Simpson in 2026, but the first-rounder did leave them with hope for the future beyond Matthew Stafford . Simpson impressed in a win over the Chargers in the preseason finale, completing 18-of-23 for 119 yards and a touchdown. He also rushed for 10 yards on three attempts. Maybe the highlight of Simpson's preseason came on a third-and-3 pass against the Chargers, where he rolled out to his left and delivered a strike to Brennan Presley for an 11-yard touchdown early in the second quarter. Selecting Simpson was polarizing in the moment, but it's hard not to think Les Snead made a wise, forward-thinking decision after seeing him this summer.
Draft status : 1st round, No. 1 overall (Indiana)
Mendoza will begin his rookie season as the backup to Kirk Cousins , and it comes after a preseason in which he showed there's still room for him to develop before rising to the top of the depth chart. In the preseason finale against San Francisco, Mendoza completed 7-of-14 for 57 yards and an interception. The pick came on Mendoza's first possession of the night after Cousins led scoring drives on his first two drives before heading to the bench. Similar to his pick-six against Houston, Mendoza's interception came on a play-action play where he was under center. The ball was too high for his intended target, was tipped, and hauled in by the Niners. Given that Mendoza had little experience working under center in college, it's not surprising to see those growing pains.

title: Dolphins trade QB Quinn Ewers to Jaguars: Miami, Jacksonville earn middling grades
summary: Miami is sending Ewers to Jacksonville for a Day 3 selection in the 2028 NFL Draft
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins cut bait with their longtime starter, Tua Tagovailoa , at the start of the offseason. Now, the franchise is moving on from another notable quarterback in Quinn Ewers . The franchise agreed to a trade to send the 2025 seventh-rounder out of Texas to the Jacksonville Jaguars , according to ESPN . In exchange, the Dolphins will reportedly receive a 2028 sxith-round pick.
After a standout collegiate career at Texas, where he earned second-team All-SEC honors in 2024, Ewers entered the 2025 NFL Draft but didn't have much fanfare. He was taken late on Day 3 to serve as a developmental piece on Miami's QB depth chart behind Tagovailoa, the then-starter.
Ewers saw action as a rookie, starting three games for the Dolphins late last season (Week 16 through Week 18). Over that stretch, he went 1-2 as Miami's starter while completing 50 of his 75 pass attempts (66.7%) for 569 yards, three passing touchdowns, and three interceptions. Ewers also rushed for 19 yards in that time.
Over the preseason, Ewers saw minimal work due to a groin injury. When he was on the field, he completed just one of his eight pass attempts for 27 yards and an interception.
This offseason saw wholesale changes in Miami, as the club hired a new general manager, Jon-Eric Sullivan, and head coach, Jeff Hafley. That new regime put any of the old guard, including Ewers, on thin ice entering the summer, especially after moving on from Tagovailoa and implementing veteran Malik Willis , whom they signed in free agency, as the starter.
Behind Willis, the Dolphins have Cam Miller and undrafted rookie Mark Gronowski on the quarterback depth chart.
Meanwhile, Ewers now arrives to a Jaguars team that has an established starter in Trevor Lawrence , who is coming off arguably the best season of his career under coach Liam Coen. The 23-year-old will now jockey with Nick Mullens, Carter Bradley and Joey Aguilar for positioning in the QB pecking order.
At the end of the day, Ewers was not in the Dolphins' long-term plans. This was an entirely new regime compared to the one that drafted him in 2025, and if the Malik Willis experiment fails, they pivot to a quarterback in the first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. While acquiring a Day 3 pick in the 2028 NFL Draft doesn't exactly move the needle, it's the type of move that Jon-Eric Sullivan should make. They give themselves increased draft capital down the road for a player they probably would've cut otherwise.
The Jaguars come out "on top" of this draft simply because Ewers is the only known commodity in the trade. At the moment, it's unclear what that 2028 sixth-rounder will ultimately become, so we'll give Jacksonville the slight edge in this trade. At one point in his collegiate career, Ewers was considered a highly touted prospect. Given that he was eventually a seventh-round pick, things have certainly gone sideways in that regard, and he hasn't done much to endear himself at the NFL level either. Still, being immersed in Coen's offense and working behind Lawrence could do Ewers a world of good and maybe eventually make him a serviceable backup.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Steelers trade Broderick Jones to Cowboys: Pick compensation, trade grades
summary: Pittsburgh is moving on from Jones after declining his fifth-year option and selecting Max Ihenachor in the first round
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are strengthening their offensive line by adding a former first-round pick to the mix before they begin the 2026 regular season. The club has struck a deal with the Pittsburgh Steelers for offensive tackle Broderick Jones , according to ESPN . In exchange, the Cowboys are reportedly sending third- and sixth-round picks in 2027 to the Steelers, while Pittsburgh is also attaching a 2027 fourth-rounder alongside Jones to facilitate the deal.
Jones entered the league as the 14th overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft after helping Georgia to two national championships. He appeared in 17 games as a rookie (11 starts) before taking on a full-time role during his sophomore season. Jones started all 11 of his games played in 2025 before being placed on injured reserve in late November due to a neck injury he suffered in Week 12 in a game against the Chicago Bears .
Before going down, Jones surrendered six sacks and 23 pressures in 2025, according to TruMedia. This came after a 2024 season in which he was responsible for 11 sacks in 17 games.
The writing was on the wall for Pittsburgh to cut bait with Jones in some capacity. Back in April, the team declined his fifth-year option, which means he is set to be an unrestricted free agent following the 2026 season. The Steelers also selected tackle Max Iheanachor with the 21st overall pick at the 2026 NFL Draft, who will likely now take over for Jones at right tackle opposite 2024 first-round left tackle Troy Fautanu .
As for Dallas, they acquire a first-round talent that deepens its offensive line, specifically behind right tackle Terence Steele . Over the last two seasons, Steele, who is under contract through 2028, has given up 16 sacks and 88 total pressures.
The Steelers had already moved on from Jones before making this trade, selecting tackles high atop the NFL Draft over the last few years. That includes Iheanachor this spring. Given that they had his replacement in-house and declined his fifth-year option, Jones was earmarked to leave Pittsburgh in one form or another. Under these circumstances, the Steelers come out pretty rosy, acquiring two picks in what is expected to be a loaded 2027 NFL Draft class. Yes, they are giving up a 2027 fourth in the process, but moving from the top of Day 3 to the back half of Day 2 is notable.
This is a pretty even swap for both sides. While Pittsburgh lands solid draft capital for the future, the Cowboys help themselves in the here and now. Jones gives them much-needed depth at offensive tackle, with Jones starting at both left and right tackle over the course of his NFL career. It also provides some insurance/competition for Terence Steeler at right tackle after struggling in recent seasons. Jones has a base salary of just $1.5 million for 2026 before becoming a free agent next offseason, so he's a pretty cheap rental that provides quality depth.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Raiders expected to name Kirk Cousins Week 1 starter over No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza
summary: The Raiders plan to open the season with the 38-year-old Cousins under center while Mendoza begins his NFL career as a backup
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders have identified their Week 1 starter: Kirk Cousins . First-year coach Klint Kubiak is expected to name the veteran as their starting quarterback to begin the 2026 regular season, according to CBS Sports senior reporter Matt Zenitz . In turn, this decision means that Fernando Mendoza , the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , will begin his pro career as Cousins' backup.
Cousins, who signed with the Raiders as an offseason free agent, appeared to have the inside track at the Week 1 job all along. With that in mind, this decision, while noteworthy, was somewhat expected. Throughout the offseason, and even before Mendoza was selected first overall, Kubiak, who is entering his first season as head coach after serving as the Seattle Seahawks' offensive coordinator last season, had noted that his preferred philosophy for developing a young quarterback would be to have him sit behind an established starter.
Despite that belief, it appeared that Kubiak let the process play out, as evidenced by this decision coming at the conclusion of the preseason rather than earlier. Had Mendoza played well enough to truly push for the starting job, it appeared Kubiak had an open mind about amending his initial plans. However, Mendoza, while showing flashes of the brilliance on display during a national championship run at Indiana last season, also showcased some rookie lumps as he transitioned to the NFL game.
Over the preseason, Mendoza completed 25 of his 45 pass attempts (55.6%) for 240 yards, one passing touchdown and two interceptions. Meanwhile, Cousins went 13-of-17 passing this summer for 101 yards and a touchdown.
"I just think he's taking practice to the field," Kubiak said of Cousins following the preseason finale, via the official team website . "Like you said, he's led scoring drives. We would have loved to lead three touchdown scoring drives. So, we're not satisfied with field goals and that's an area that we need to improve at. But I see a guy that's leading the offense."
Cousins, 38, is entering his 15th season in the NFL. He's started 167 regular-season games over that stretch and is 88-77-2. That includes a 5-3 record in his eight starts last season for the Atlanta Falcons .
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: NFL places new Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold on the commissioner's exempt list, per report
summary: Arnold is not permitted to practice or play while on the commissioner's exempt list
full_text:
The NFL placed new Seattle Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold on the commissioner's exempt list, according to ESPN . Arnold's placement on the exempt list comes on the heels of the former first-round cornerback officially signing with the Seahawks. Under the provisions of the commissioner's exempt list, Arnold will be paid, but is not permitted to take part in practice or play in a game for Seattle.
The Seahawks signing Arnold had been in the works for a while, and the corner officially jumping aboard on Saturday was merely a formality. It was also likely that the subsequent placement on the commissioner's exempt list would take effect. This comes after Arnold was released by the Detroit Lions following his arrest on felony charges in connection with a robbery and kidnapping in February.
Arnold, 23, entered the NFL as the No. 24 overall pick of the Lions during the 2024 NFL Draft . The Alabama product has started in 22 of his 24 regular-season games, including seven starts in eight games during the 2025 season, which was cut short due to a shoulder injury. When he was on the field last season, Arnold totaled 31 tackles, eight pass breakups and an interception.
He now joins a Seattle secondary that boasts Devon Witherspoon , whom the Seahawks recently made the highest-paid corner in the NFL with a four-year, $132 million extension.
"It was an opportunity to bring on a player that we felt strongly about during the draft process," Macdonald told reporters earlier this month when asked about the then-looming addition of Arnold. "We also understand that it's a serious situation with a legal matter. There's a process behind it, so we respect that. That's how we'll operate, just letting that process play out and let the league decide if and when his return to play is. We'll understand that that's at play, but there's also an opportunity to bring him and give him an opportunity to earn a position here.
"We feel really strongly about our locker room and our team. We had a great visit with Terrion. Obviously, we knew him going throughout the process. I referenced the folks that have been in his corner throughout the whole process as well, and we respect those people. We're not going to ignore those folks that we really respect and have a strong opinion about it as well. When we put all of those things together, we felt like it was a good opportunity for the team."
While he ultimately signed with the Seattle, Arnold also worked out for the Houston Texans , New Orleans Saints and New York Giants upon his release from Detroit.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: How Jordan Love helped Packers win preseason game over Cardinals without playing
summary: Green Bay ended the game with consecutive drives that ended with touchdowns
full_text:
Jordan Love may have found his next calling when his playing days come to an end. Love served as the Packers ' play caller throughout the second half of Green Bay's 42-38 preseason win over the Cardinals .
After a scoreless third quarter, the Packers scored 17 points in the fourth quarter with Love calling the plays. The Packers ended the game with consecutive drives that ended with touchdowns.
"That was pretty cool," Packers coach Matt Lafleur said afterward. "Just to hear his demeanor on the headset and how calm, cool, and collected he was throughout the entire game, especially in those critical moments. And it's not a surprise to me because that's what we see on the field."
JLove was really driving the bus pic.twitter.com/wNNgC6wNu0
Green Bay's offense looked like a well-oiled machine during the fourth quarter. Over that span, the Packers gained 155 yards and averaged 6.74 yards per play. Love's backup, Kyle McCord , threw two of his four touchdown passes with Love calling the plays that included his game-winning touchdown pass to Kisean Johnson with 1:34 left.
LET'S GO! 📺: Packers TV Network pic.twitter.com/XgjdlZd4Ip
McCord said that Love told him at halftime that he would be calling the shots during the second half.
"I said, 'Have you done that before?' He said, 'Naw. We'll see," McCord said afterward . "He was great. He obviously knows the offense like the back of his hand and called some really good plays, especially there toward the end."
While his debut as an NFL play caller was a success, Love will now resume his duties as Green Bay's franchise quarterback. Now in his seventh season, Love is entering his fourth season as the team's starting quarterback. He enters the 2026 season just 17 touchdown passes away from 100 for his career.
The win gave the Packers a 2-1 record to end the preseason. They open the regular-season opener against the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 13.
Green Bay's next game will mark the start of Love's sixth season in the NFL – and fourth as the Packers' full-time starter.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Infectious energy? More like 'infectious disease' as Cam Skattebo ruffles feathers at Giants practice
summary: Skattebo's play style is not always well-received, especially during training camp
full_text:
Cam Skattebo is about as physical a running back as there is in the NFL . His hard-nosed play style made him a standout performer before his season-ending ankle injury as a rookie. He is also among the more flamboyant ballcarriers in the league. His backflip celebrations sometimes garner as much attention as the plays that warrant them.
All of that is well and good on Sundays when Skattebo is doing it against a different team. But in the context of the New York Giants ' training camp, his brash football personality has tended to rub teammates the wrong way.
Skattebo was reportedly at the center of a fight this week that stemmed from a couple of close calls with vulnerable defensive players. On one rep, when the defense was not allowed to hit, he made a catch and slid close to a couple of defensive backs' legs, according to the New York Daily News . Jevon Holland and Gregory Newsome took exception to the potentially dangerous play, and the situation between Newsome and Skattebo escalated.
Days earlier, Skattebo ran over linebacker Zaire Barnes in a period where, again, defensive players were not permitted to make hits.
At the suggestion that Skattebo is wearing on his defensive teammates' nerves, one of his fellow offensive players pushed back. Offensive lineman Jermaine Eluemunor squashed the idea that Skattebo is the source of any rotten team chemistry.
🧢 Stop trying to create a BS Narrative https://t.co/CkLFunX6jg
At the same time, though, the Giants want Skattebo to keep himself in check. Coach John Harbaugh earlier this offseason asked him to limit his backflips during camp so as to reduce the potential for reinjury. And after his slide at Wednesday's practice, Harbaugh made it clear he wants to set boundaries between the whistles, too.
"Skatt's great," Harbaugh said . "He does bring a lot of energy. But he did get a 15-yard penalty at the end of practice. Did you notice that? That's not infectious. Well, it is infectious, actually. Infectious in a bad way. Like an infectious disease type of thing. You don't want that. You want it to be directed in a positive way."
During his rookie season in 2025, Skattebo's "infectious" personality made him a favorite among teammates and Giants fans. However, that ended when he suffered a gruesome dislocation of his right ankle on Oct. 26, 2025.
Giants fans are aching to see Skattebo headbutt defenders, run right through them and pull off backflips when he crosses the goal line. That is what made him a must-watch ballcarrier in a rookie campaign that featured 617 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns across just eight games. Defenses cannot stand him, which is terrific when he plays against another team and less so when he lines up across from his own teammates for weeks on end. Fortunately for the Giants and their fans, the season is just over two weeks away. They begin the 2026 season on Sunday Night Football on Sept. 13 against the NFC East rival Dallas Cowboys, which means Skattebo will have the opportunity to run over defenders in another uniform instead of his own.
Skattebo is listed atop the depth chart at running back, but Harris has drawn praise since his arrival via free agency.
Harris, who by all accounts has looked good in practice, has the running style that suits the Greg Roman system, and he could cut into Skattebo's carries, especially if he keeps up his practice antics.
"Najee offers something different," Assistant general manager Brandon Brown told reporters on Wednesday. "When you have a back that played at 235 before his injury that doesn't need things blocked up cleanly for him to push the pile, and then he has a familiarity with G-Ro from L.A., those are things that you can't just gloss over. When you have an opportunity to add talent, we're never going to shy away from that."
On the addition of Harris, Brown added: "No one was butthurt." "It was very much adding competition, and that's the thing that's been very cool about the meritocracy. It's not personal. It's just the business of making this team as good as it can be."
The Giants have plenty of competition for carries and touches this season, with four capable running backs (Skattebo, Harris, Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary), and a coach like Harbaugh won't put up with the drama.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Giants-Ravens trade grades: New York aces trade by acquiring promising young defender at minimal cost
summary: C.J. Okoye is reuniting with John Harbaugh in the Big Apple
full_text:
With NFL cutdown day fast approaching, teams continue to make moves to finalize their 53-man rosters. The first notable move on Saturday was the Ravens trading defensive lineman C.J. Okoye to the Giants for a 2028 seventh-round pick, according to ESPN .
Okoye was traded hours after recovering a fumble during Baltimore's preseason win over the Commanders . During his first season in Baltimore, Okoye clearly made a good impression on John Harbaugh, who is embarking on his first season as Giants coach.
A native of Nigeria, the 24-year-old Okoye was part of the NFL's International Pathway Program. He broke into the NFL with the Chargers in 2023, and in his first preseason game , he sacked Rams quarterback Stetson Bennett in what was the first organized game of his professional life. Okoye was awarded the game ball afterward.
C.J. Okoye, nigeriano que até ontem nunca tinha jogado futebol americano, conseguiu um sack em sua primeira partida. Baita história do International Pathway Program da NFL. pic.twitter.com/J9VlEczPkZ
Okoye spent two years on the Chargers' practice squad before signing with Baltimore in 2025. He started the season on the practice squad but was promoted to the active roster in October. Okoye appeared in 13 games and registered 15 tackles and a pass breakup.
Who won the trade? Let's find out.
The Giants get dinged a little bit because they probably could have acquired Okoye off waivers after he was released by the Ravens. That being said, the Giants deserve credit for being proactive in pursuing a player that Harbaugh clearly sees potential in. Instead of risking another team picking Okoye up on the waiver wire, the Giants made sure that Okoye would not hit the open market.
Overall, though, this is a good move by the Giants for several reasons. They acquired a young, promising player at limited cost who gives the Giants valuable depth at an important position. The best-case scenario is Okoye developing into an impact player who can help solidify New York's interior defensive line. If it doesn't work out that way, the Giants didn't spend much in the form of money or draft capital.
The Ravens did their old coach a solid with this trade. Baltimore obviously wasn't planning on Okoye being part of their 53-man roster, and instead of releasing him and getting nothing in return, they chose to get something in return while reuniting him with his former coach. It's a rare trade situation where everyone wins.
Baltimore didn't receive a higher grade because they probably could have gotten a little more for Okoye, given the Giants' clear interest in acquiring him. They also chose to part ways with a promising player, which could hurt them if they suffer injuries on the defensive line this season.

title: Origins of “The Turk”
summary: The Arizona Cardinals, like every other NFL club, have 90 players signed for training camp. On Sunday, August 30, the roster must be pared down to 53 players. That is a lot of guys suddenly unemployed. The day after is when teams begin making claims off the waiver wire for players that have been released […]
full_text: This year, “The Turk” struck RB Trey Benson #33 first (Photo by Jonathan Bachman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals, like every other NFL club, have 90 players signed for training camp. On Sunday, August 30, the roster must be pared down to 53 players. That is a lot of guys suddenly unemployed. The day after is when teams begin making claims off the waiver wire for players that have been released from other teams. RELATED: POSITIONAL PLAYERS THAT NEED TO BE ADDRESSED The person doing the player cuts? That is “The Turk.” In 1946, a new professional football league began, called the “All-America Football Conference” (AAFC). This new NFL-rival league consisted of eight teams, of which four would be situated in NFL cities such as Chicago, Cleveland, New York, and Los Angeles. The AAFC raided NFL rosters and coaching staffs. They signed players who were once on NFL rosters and then entered World War II, but had contract offers waiting for them. This new league signed numerous athletes who had to forgo their sophomore, junior, and senior college seasons, and upon return, found that all of their eligibility had been forfeited. Paul Brown was hired to coach the AAFC Cleveland squad while he was still in the Navy. The Cleveland Rams eventually received approval from the other owners to relocate to Los Angeles, a move that Rams owner Dan Reeves had been lobbying for two years. He finally got his wish when air travel became available, replacing the need for trains to travel to games. Back in those days, pro football teams held their training camps at small college campuses. This provided remoteness for both players and coaches. Athletes could focus solely on the game and studying the playbook without the distraction of having to mow the lawn, or change the oil, or wives or girlfriends or both, the baby waking up at 2:00 a.m., or little Billy having a bad dream. These campuses had a football team, so there was a stadium for practice and other practice fields. Players could sleep in empty dorm rooms, which usually housed two students per room – perfect for a duo of players. Classrooms were ideal for position meeting rooms, and there was a mess hall for meals. The isolation was ideal for focusing on the upcoming season. For the longest time, the NFL, and later the American Football League, would schedule some preseason games in cities that were devoid of NFL teams. This brought the game of pro football to a new set of fans in the hopes that they would grab onto the game and follow a team. At one time, the State of Florida did not have any professional teams in any sport. So, the NFL scheduled exhibition games. Jacksonville had the 62,000-capacity Gator Bowl, while Miami had the 72,000-seat Orange Bowl available. The Tangerine Bowl in Orlando could hold 60,000, while Tampa offered 74,000 seats in Tampa Stadium. All of these cities have since had a professional football team call them home, with three now having NFL franchises. In today’s NFL universe, the league is more focused on bringing its game to international venues and fans. But back in the day, they were more focused on expanding their presence to non-NFL cities and states in the hopes that fans would choose a favorite team and follow their seasons. All across the country, the NFL and AFL had preseason games in Memphis, Tulsa, Norfolk, Sacramento, Jackson, Hartford, Boise, Birmingham, Austin, Shreveport, San Antonio, Portland, Mobile, San Jose, Oklahoma City, and Tucson. Columbus, Ohio, held an annual Browns contest in the preseason for decades. Even cities that now have NFL clubs were visited beforehand, such as New Orleans, Las Vegas, and Nashville, to name a few. As training camps went along their merry way, after certain preseason games, there would be a round of player cuts. Clubs would have 90 players in camp, and then on the Monday after the exhibition game, the franchise would have to pare down to 85 players. After the next preseason game, the roster would then be shortened to 75 players. And finally, after the final exhibition game, the coaching staff would have to get to 53 players. Except for the final cuts, all of the player releases would occur at the training camp college campus. And who would do the cuts? The “Turk.” The Turk was a mystical creature who would prowl NFL training camps. What once was two players soundly asleep in a college dorm room would become one player who would wake up and find an empty bed beside him with maybe a single sock on the floor, a pencil once used to take notes, and a half-eaten apple sitting on the nightstand. No blood, no claw marks, no suitcase, and no roommate would be found. “The Turk” is the term used for the person who would come to get players that are about to be cut. This was always an assistant coach. Cuts were performed when it became dark, after players had retired to their rooms to study, but before the 11:00 p.m. lights out. The scene is usually a closed door with players engulfed in their playbooks, and the brightly lit hallway lurks a shadow that would approach. If the shadow continued, both players were safe. If the shadow stopped, the door would creak and open slowly, and the coach would say, “(Insert player name), coach wants to see you. Bring your playbook.” Then the assistant coach would accompany the player into the head coach’s office, who would then tell the athlete his “release speech” and send the player to the airport, or, back in the day, the train station. When the other surviving team members would wake up and gather for breakfast, they would notice other players who were no longer in the room. “The Turk” had come in the night and snatched them. This was coined in 1949 by Don Paul, a Los Angeles Rams linebacker, who would say, “The Turk always strikes at night.” As was the Rams’ custom and all the other teams’, the cuts were done in the evening on cutdown day. This eliminated the other players from seeing their now-former teammates leave the campus since everyone was in their rooms. The reason Paul used the term “Turk” is that, in the 12th through the 16 th centuries, the Turkish army made most of its raids and attacks after dark. Thus, the term is still used even today. Barry Shuck is a pro football historical writer and a member of the Professional Football Researchers’ Association
