title: Ben Johnson is ‘the most influential person that I’ve been around’
summary: Declan Doyle was the youngest offensive coordinator in the NFL last season under Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson, and the Bears let him make the lateral move to the Baltimore Ravens so he’d get an opportunity to call plays. This year, he’s still the youngest play caller in the NFL (now 30), and he […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - AUGUST 03: Head Coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears, Defensive Coordinator Dennis Allen of the Chicago Bears, and Offensive Coordinator Declan Doyle of the Chicago Bears observe warmups during Bears training camp at Soldier Field in Chicago, IL on Saturday, August 3rd, 2025 (Photo by Ben Hsu/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Declan Doyle was the youngest offensive coordinator in the NFL last season under Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson, and the Bears let him make the lateral move to the Baltimore Ravens so he’d get an opportunity to call plays. This year, he’s still the youngest play caller in the NFL (now 30), and he made an immediate impression on the Ravens. You’ve heard the players rave about Declan Doyle all offseason. Now see why for yourself. Check out Wired right now: https://t.co/FHwqKSF8Hm pic.twitter.com/iaUwOnJERC — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) July 23, 2026 Doyle’s coaching career started at Iowa in 2016, where he was an offensive student assistant until 2018, but in 2019 he was hired by head coach Sean Payton and the New Orleans Saints. When Payton retired following the 2021 season, Doyle stayed in New Orleans one more year, but when Payton unretired to take the Denver Broncos job in 2023, Doyle followed Payton to the Mile High City. This is Doyle’s 11th year coaching football, and he spent just one year in Chicago with Johnson, but it was an impactful time for him. “He is brilliant; he’s detailed. He made me view football in a completely different lens.” Doyle said of Johnson via Ryan Mink, the Editorial Director for the Ravens’ team site. “From the spacing of the field, the spacing of the passing game. He taught me more about football in a year than … he’s arguably the best coach I’ve ever been around. He’s probably the most influential person that I’ve been around. In addition to it, my relationship with him is like he was the older brother I never had. I felt like he was the closest thing to myself that I’ve ever been around in coaching in just how he approaches the game, how he felt about offense, his logic.” Now I gave you Doyle’s coaching history to highlight all his time spent with Payton, the 2006 NFL Coach of the Year, 2009 Super Bowl champion, owner of a 184–108 record (.630), and a likely future Hall of Famer, and yet he has all that praise for Ben Johnson based on their lone year together.

title: Bengals eyeing Steelers’ Kaleb Johnson, per report: Is he a good fit for Cincinnati?
summary: According to Pittsburgh radio personality Andrew Fillipponi, the Cincinnati Bengals are among the teams that could have interest in Steelers running back Kaleb Johnson, who appears to be on the roster bubble in Pittsburgh as the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline approaches. Johnson’s availability would be an interesting development for Cincinnati. The Bengals have spent much […]
full_text: According to Pittsburgh radio personality Andrew Fillipponi, the Cincinnati Bengals are among the teams that could have interest in Steelers running back Kaleb Johnson, who appears to be on the roster bubble in Pittsburgh as the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline approaches. Johnson’s availability would be an interesting development for Cincinnati. The Bengals have spent much of the preseason evaluating their depth behind Chase Brown and Samaje Perine, with players such as Tahj Brooks, Kendall Milton, and others competing for opportunities. Following the Bengals’ preseason finale against the Philadelphia Eagles, Brooks and Milton remain among the players whose roster futures are uncertain. If Pittsburgh ultimately decides to move on from Johnson, Cincinnati could potentially view him as a reclamation project with considerably more upside than his brief NFL résumé would suggest. Rumor: The Bengals are eyeing Steelers RB Kaleb Johnson. If he’s cut. And could possibly try trading for the 3rd round bust RB. Cincinnati has very little depth behind Chase Brown. And really liked Johnson in the 2025 NFL Draft. He went to Cincy for a draft visit. Stay tuned. pic.twitter.com/bJL8QqBNQS — Andrew Fillipponi (@ThePoniExpress) August 29, 2026 Johnson was a highly productive college running back Johnson is only entering his second NFL season, but his college résumé was impressive enough to make him a third-round selection. The Steelers selected Johnson No. 83 overall in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Iowa, making him the 17th player selected in that year’s draft class at the running back position. His final season with the Hawkeyes was particularly impressive. In 2024, Johnson rushed 240 times for 1,537 yards and 21 touchdowns, averaging an impressive 6.4 yards per carry. He also caught 22 passes for 188 yards and two touchdowns. Over three seasons at Iowa, Johnson accumulated: 508 rushing attempts 2,779 rushing yards 30 rushing touchdowns 29 receptions 240 receiving yards 2 receiving touchdowns His 2,779 rushing yards rank sixth in Iowa history, and he became just the fifth player in program history to record two 200-plus-yard rushing performances. That production was a major reason Pittsburgh invested a third-round pick in him. His NFL career, however, hasn’t gone according to plan. Johnson hasn’t been able to establish himself in Pittsburgh Johnson appeared in just 10 games as a rookie, carrying the ball 28 times for only 69 yards, an average of 2.5 yards per carry. He did not score a touchdown and caught just one pass for nine yards. He did contribute as a kickoff returner, bringing back eight kicks for 190 yards, a 23.8-yard average. One of Johnson’s more notable performances came against Cincinnati last season. He carried five times for 15 yards during Pittsburgh’s 34-12 victory over the Bengals in Week 11. But that wasn’t enough to establish him as a regular part of Pittsburgh’s offense. And his situation hasn’t improved dramatically during the 2026 preseason. Johnson has rushed 12 times for 42 yards through Pittsburgh’s first two preseason games, while adding two receptions for 15 yards. He did have a somewhat encouraging performance against the Jets, carrying 10 times for 39 yards and catching both of his targets for 15 yards. But Johnson has remained behind Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle in Pittsburgh’s running-back hierarchy, and his roster status remains uncertain. That has led to increasing speculation that Pittsburgh could either trade him or ultimately release him. Why would the Bengals be interested? The obvious question is: Why would Cincinnati want another running back? The answer is that the Bengals’ depth behind Brown and Perine isn’t exactly settled. Brown is clearly positioned as Cincinnati’s primary back after establishing himself as a major part of the offense, while Perine provides veteran experience and pass-protection ability. After those two, however, the Bengals have questions. Brooks hasn’t consistently separated himself from the competition. Milton has flashed but hasn’t generated overwhelming production. Cincinnati also has other young backs competing for opportunities, with Jamal Haynes and Kentrel Bullock having solid outings in the preseason finale versus the Eagles. That’s where Johnson becomes intriguing. At his best, Johnson was a physical, productive runner who excelled in Iowa’s zone-running scheme. His 1,537-yard junior season demonstrated that he has the ability to carry a significant workload. And he’s still only 23 years old. A change of scenery could potentially give him an opportunity to restart his development. The Bengals wouldn’t necessarily need to give up much If Pittsburgh decides that Johnson isn’t going to make the roster, the question becomes whether Cincinnati would rather claim him off waivers or attempt to acquire him via trade. A trade would obviously require some compensation, and there’s little reason for Cincinnati to surrender significant draft capital for a player who could potentially become available after roster cuts. The Steelers are reportedly exploring trade possibilities for Johnson, with recent speculation suggesting that a late-round pick swap could be enough to facilitate a deal. One recent Steelers Depot proposa l had Pittsburgh sending Johnson and a seventh-round pick to Dallas in exchange for a sixth-rounder. That illustrates the type of market Johnson could be in. The Bengals probably wouldn’t want to pay much for a player who could potentially be available on waivers. But if Cincinnati’s personnel department believes Johnson still possesses the talent that made him a third-round pick, a late-round flier could make sense. There is some irony to the potential fit There’s also an interesting bit of history here. Johnson’s best NFL game as a rookie against the Bengals was modest by any measure — five carries for 15 yards — but Cincinnati’s defense got a firsthand look at him last season. More importantly, Johnson grew up in Cincinnati and attended Hamilton High School before starring at Iowa. And, as Fillipponi noted, the former Hawkeyes back had a pre-draft visit with the Bengals. So a move to the Bengals would represent a return home for the former Hamilton standout. That’s not a reason for Cincinnati to acquire him, of course, but it certainly makes the possibility more interesting from a local perspective. Should the Bengals actually pursue him? There’s a reasonable argument for both sides. On one hand, Johnson’s NFL production to date has been disappointing. He averaged only 2.5 yards per carry as a rookie, hasn’t established himself as a reliable receiving option, and hasn’t consistently separated himself from Pittsburgh’s other running backs. On the other hand, he’s a former third-round pick with an elite college résumé who is only 23 years old. That’s exactly the type of player a team might be willing to take a relatively inexpensive chance on—especially with the track record of the Bengals liking these types of backgrounds for cheap additions. And Cincinnati has already demonstrated this offseason that it is willing to add talent to positions where competition is fierce. The Bengals don’t necessarily need Kaleb Johnson. But if Pittsburgh decides to move on from him, Cincinnati should at least be doing its homework. The Bengals’ preseason made one thing abundantly clear: depth matters. And if Johnson is released, Cincinnati could have an opportunity to add a talented young running back who simply hasn’t found the right situation yet. For now, though, this remains a report of potential interest rather than any indication that a trade is imminent. The next 48 hours should tell us whether the former Iowa star is headed back to Cincinnati — or looking for his third NFL opportunity elsewhere.

It seems safe to say that this defense won’t get embarrassed the way previous ones did in the last couple of years.

title: 3 draft-eligible prospects to watch this weekend as college football begins
summary: Week 0 of the college football season begins this Saturday. While there aren’t any marquee matchups this week, 14th-ranked USC will be in action against San Jose State. There will also be a handful of other prospects to pay attention to spread throughout the seven other games of the weekend. Arguably the best game could […]
full_text: Jul 24, 2025; Las Vegas, NV, USA; USC offensive lineman Elijah Paige speaks to the media during the Big Ten NCAA college football media days at Mandalay Bay Resort. Mandatory Credit: Lucas Peltier-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Week 0 of the college football season begins this Saturday. While there aren’t any marquee matchups this week, 14th-ranked USC will be in action against San Jose State. There will also be a handful of other prospects to pay attention to spread throughout the seven other games of the weekend. Arguably the best game could be NC State versus Virginia. Virginia played in the ACC title game, and NC State returns a dynamic quarterback in CJ Bailey. Let’s take a look at a few draft-eligible prospects worth watching this weekend. Elijah Paige The Bengals have questions about the swing tackle position heading into the 2026 season. There are really even some questions about the starting left tackle spot going forward as Orlando Brown Jr. will be turning 31 years old after this season. Elijah Paige is a left tackle prospect for the USC Trojans. The 6’7” 315 pound prospect finished the 2025 season with an 84.0 pass blocking grade. He plays with a wide base, is quick out of his stance off of the snap, and allowed just six total pressures through the seven games he played last season. Lower body injuries plagued him throughout the season though, ultimately shutting him down early. He will need to improve as a run blocker, grading out with a 60.2 last year. He also lunged quite often which led to him missing his intended target when getting out in space as a run blocker. There are traits worth monitoring here, and he is just now entering his redshirt junior season. Elijah Paige (#72) USC ✅ Size at 6’7” and 325 pounds ✅ Recovery athleticism ✅ Quickness off the snap ✅ Allowed just 6 pressures and 0 sacks in 7 games played during 2025 ✅ 84.0 pass blocking grade in 2025 pic.twitter.com/AsOqRE6nbf — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) May 31, 2026 Xavier Chaplin Sticking with offensive tackle prospects, Chaplin fits the mold of the size Cincinnati typically covets in an offensive tackle prospect. A transfer from Auburn, Chaplin will be playing for Florida State in 2026. He was recently listed at 6’6” and 346 pounds. He is a massive player at tackle who moves fairly well for a player with that size. While the size, athleticism, and finishing mentality are all positives, his footwork has been a mess. Hopefully he will be able to clean that up, along with playing with better pad level consistency in 2026. He will also need to clean up the penalties, recording 12 of them during the 2025 season. As of now, this could be a day-three type of prospect that the Bengals could target as a future swing tackle. Chaplin and his Florida State teammates will kick off the season against New Mexico State on Saturday night. Boley is a 6’5”, 329-pound left tackle for Virginia. He is an experienced player, entering the season having already played over 2,300 total snaps. Boley is an athletic offensive tackle, having been clocked at 19 miles per hour on the GPS data tracking system. He comes from NFL bloodlines, with his father Michael playing nine seasons in the NFL at linebacker. I thought Boley struggled at times handling power into his chest, and he had difficulty connecting with his target out in space. This is an experienced day three prospect, and there is a world where the Bengals could double dip at the offensive tackle position during the 2027 NFL Draft. title: Browns fans weigh in on Todd Monken’s decision to start Deshaun Watson over Shedeur Sanders
summary: Cleveland Browns head coach made the unpopular decision this week to name Deshaun Watson as the team’s starting quarterback in Week 1 over Shedeur Sanders. We’ve heard a variety of things, including that since the team starts off with two road games, this gives the team to chance to see if Watson will deliver in […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - APRIL 21: Head coach Todd Monken and Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns watch a drill during a voluntary veteran minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on April 21, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Cleveland Browns head coach made the unpopular decision this week to name Deshaun Watson as the team’s starting quarterback in Week 1 over Shedeur Sanders . We’ve heard a variety of things, including that since the team starts off with two road games, this gives the team to chance to see if Watson will deliver in those games prior to deciding what to do in front of the home crowd in Week 3. For this week’s Reacts poll, if I was to ask fans what they thought of Watson starting, I think it would have been 90% or higher toward the negative. Therefore, I tried to put a spin on things by framing your mindset towards head coach Todd Monken instead. The question asked, “Does Monken naming Watson the starter impact your view of the head coach?” 65% of fans still voted that it was a dumb decision by Monken (even though the language in the graphic to the left was edited to be nicer). The remaining 35% of fans said that they respect Monken’s decision (for now). It was a hot-button topic that lots of Browns fans weighed in on, if you go back and read the comments . Among the responses, one fan said: I cannot answer the survey because I don’t believe it was his decision. Spidey thinks Monken made the right call: From all indications, the players have Watson’s back. Heck, how many were here when the trade was made?!? They don’t carry any of the grudges the fans have And they don’t care about the 2027 QB or tanking. Therefore, put yourself in their shoes. You’ve seen both of them perform in training camp and preseason games. There’s not much difference in the results (TDs and INTs) and it certainly appears that Watson has better command in the huddle and LOS. If I’m a player and Monken made the decision based on the media and fans booing, I’d think less of the coach. Heck, I remember thinking less of my coaches in high school if I saw them hanging out with players’ parents or other fans with an interest in seeing one player over another. Monken has Watson on the team. The players have Watson as teammate. Those are the top two factors for Monken. And woe to the leader of men who bends to the whims of the outside world. Half Baked Again said: I have always wondered why we think the Ravens OC was a great hire. I mean that team lived by their defense and Lamar’s legs. They never had a working offense without Lamar. This decision tells me that the Browns are clearly tanking and I do not think Monkin will be here next year (he was set up to fail). Also, none of the QBs will be here next year. title: Cleveland Browns 53-man roster cuts tracker
summary: The Cleveland Browns have until Sunday at 6:00 PM ET to make roster cuts and announce their initial 53-man roster. Some of those cuts or rumors about roster moves might leak early, though. The Browns may also announce them in waves — for example, some cuts may be announced Friday, some on Saturday, etc. All […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns have until Sunday at 6:00 PM ET to make roster cuts and announce their initial 53-man roster. Some of those cuts or rumors about roster moves might leak early, though. The Browns may also announce them in waves — for example, some cuts may be announced Friday, some on Saturday, etc. All players who are released with less than four years of service must go through waivers and are eligible to be claimed by any other team until 1:00 PM ET on Monday . After that, any unclaimed player can be signed and teams will begin to fill out their 16-man practice squads. Veterans with more than four years of service can sign immediately after being released. You can also use the comments section to discuss cuts around the NFL that may be of interest to Cleveland. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 225/1 odds to win the Super Bowl, heading into final roster cuts. Browns Roster Cuts Live Blog Sunday (August 30, 2026) 9:51 AM: Hmmm… 9:42 AM: It is cutdown day, and the Browns still have 20 moves to make. Typically, you start seeing things leak one-by-one with a few players who either made or didn’t make the 53-man roster, but the vibe of this year’s cutdowns seems a bit…different. Maybe we’ll just see another press release that names the remaining moves. Saturday (August 29, 2026) 11:45 AM: No more moves till Sunday, according to Tony Grossi: Browns not expected to announce any cuts today. One more practice & then cut to 53 on Sunday. — Tony Grossi (@TonyGrossi) August 29, 2026 11:10 AM: Welp, media sessions before practice have started and no more cuts. At one point, the team planned to practice tomorrow as well, which could explain the delay in more moves. Injuries today could be interesting to evaluate along with roster decisions tonight, tomorrow. 7:30 AM : Reminder that the Browns are scheduled to practice today, with players speaking to the media at 11 AM, with Todd Monken following at 11:50 before the 12:15 practice. It would be somewhat strange, unless there was some secret plan with a player or two , for more than 53 players to be practicing today. Then again, Monken can do what he wants until the players are cut. Would also be risking injuries for players who are going to get cut and could sign elsewhere. Just seems unlikely, so stayed tuned here to the tracker all morning! Friday (August 28, 2026) 3:36 PM: By my count, the Browns are now down to 73 players, meaning they have 20 moves remaining to get down to 53 players by Sunday at 6:00 pm ET. I’m not sure if there will be any more moves today, but my current guess is that the remaining moves will be announced tomorrow. What you might start hearing, before that official news release, are players’ agents leaking that “so-and-so has been informed that they have made the 53-man roster,” or some sources indicating that a particular player has been notified that they’ll be cut. Going back to the first batch of cuts below, none of them are a surprise. Avery was a guy on my 53-man roster, but he was meant to be a temporary placeholder due to injury concerns; I did not expect him to be a long-term player on the roster. 3:25 PM: We have our first batch of Browns cuts: 16 moves in total (4 contracts terminated, 12 players waived). The terminated players are TE Jack Stoll (from IR), OT Tyre Phillips , CB Tre Avery , and CB Tyler Hall . The players waived are WR Ben Patterson , TE Jermaine Terry II , TE Drew Biber , OT Jeremiah Byers , OT Izavion Miller , DT Coziah Izzard , DT Patrick Jenkins , DE Jamil Muhammad , CB Jeremiah McClendon , CB Nate Evans , S Christopher Edmonds , and P Nik Constantinou . 1:24 PM: Not a reportable rumor as I don’t have a second source, but enough to at least share here as a keep-your-eyes-out kinda thing. I’ve heard that the Falcons and Chargers at least discussed a Tua trade, which could open up a spot for Dillon Gabriel in Atlanta (just as everyone joked/expected when Kevin Stefanski was hired there). – Jared 10:15 AM: Regarding the timing of the Browns’ roster cuts, Jared Mueller made a good point on one of our site’s internal communications. Head coach Todd Monken is scheduled to talk to the media at 11:00 AM ET on Saturday, with practice to follow at 12:15 PM on Saturday. It seems highly likely that the Browns will have their 53-man roster decided by then. I’ve never heard of a case where the team keeps players around for one more practice in between making their final roster cuts. 10:02 AM: Good morning, everyone! I posted my 53-man roster projection this morning. There were plenty of tough decisions at quarterback, wide receiver, tight end, and cornerback. With these potential roster cuts, news could literally hit any time between now and Sunday evening. Typically, Andrew Berry does not wait through the deadline to make cuts. We’ll keep you posted on any Browns-related news that comes in, as well as other cuts around the league. One thing to keep in mind is that the final preseason games in general takes place today, as only a few games took place Thursday evening. In general, you likely won’t see league-wide news about roster cuts until Saturday. 12:00 AM: The Browns just finished their third and final preseason game, beating the New England Patriots by a score of 37-13 . We already heard about one big roster cut on Thursday morning, as reports indicated that Cleveland was waiving WR Cedric Tillman . Tillman was going to be a cut on my 53-man roster projection anyway, due to the way things have unfolded in camp this year and the impressive nature of rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston . title: Browns: Is this rookie playing himself into a starter’s role?
summary: Cleveland Browns general manager Andrew Berry entered the 2026 offseason facing an odd situation. The offensive line, long one of the team’s strengths, was aging, injured, and highly paid, leaving Berry to decide whether to stick with the status quo for another year or attempt to rebuild the entire starting unit in a single offseason.  […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 11: Austin Barber #58 of the Cleveland Browns walks off the field after the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 11, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Cleveland Browns general manager Andrew Berry entered the 2026 offseason facing an odd situation. The offensive line, long one of the team’s strengths, was aging, injured, and highly paid, leaving Berry to decide whether to stick with the status quo for another year or attempt to rebuild the entire starting unit in a single offseason. Berry chose the latter, which saw guard Joel Bitonio retire, center Ethan Pocic sign with the Baltimore Ravens in free agency, guard Wyatt Teller sign with the Houston Texans in free agency, and tackle Jack Conklin still looking for a team as a free agent. The other remaining starter, Dawand Jones, is still on the team but expected to serve a backup role this season as the coveted swing tackle. In their place are left tackle Spencer Fano, the team’s first-round choice in the 2026 NFL Draft; left guard Zion Johnson and center Elgton Jenkins, signed as free agents; right guard Teven Jenkins, who the Browns chose to re-sign; and right tackle Tytus Howard, who the Browns acquired in a trade. Berry did not stop there, however, as he also selected tackle Austin Barber and center Parker Brailsford in the 2026 draft. Watch Austin Barber at right guard. He washes the shade, or one-technique, down to his left, then releases into the screen and gets physical with the defensive back. The #Browns rookie can play multiple positions and brings a nasty, mean demeanor to the offensive line. pic.twitter.com/2l7KSZoW1R — Lance Reisland (Coach Riz) (@LanceReisland) August 29, 2026 Brailsford has been slowed during training camp and the preseason due to a hand injury, but Barber has been catching everyone’s attention – most notably head coach Todd Monken – and could be in line to claim a starting spot at right guard. Monken was asked about the rookie on Saturday and was very complimentary ( quote via a team-provided transcript ): “What a great job he’s done playing, starting at tackle, then going to guard. I think he’s only going to continue to get better, so I’ve been very pleased with him. He takes coaching. There was a screen that we ran during the game that, the week before, when it got caught, he was a little bit casual down the field on, not accelerating his feet, and you saw it in the game the other night. He accelerated and ran through the defender to get out of the way of the defender and did a great job. He certainly takes coaching from the meeting room, from his past experiences to the field.” The fact that Monken mentioned twice that Barber “takes coaching” is something that should not be overlooked, as that appears to be a key trait that the head coach looks for as he builds the first roster of his NFL head coaching career. And could Barber actually find himself in the huddle when the offense takes the field for the first time in Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars? Monken did not rule it out : “I love our depth there. Again, I think Teven has the advantage, obviously, as the veteran player, but we still have this week, we still have today and a few practices to really finalize. I’d give Teven the lean, but I don’t think it’s done yet.” Berry admitted during the broadcast of one of the preseason games that rebuilding the entire offensive line is not an ideal situation to be in, but the early signs are positive so far about the work he did in not only landing five new starters, but building some solid depth along the line. And if Barber continues to ascend and land in the starting lineup, that offseason work will only look that much better.

The Cleveland Browns head into their initial 53-man roster decisions not knowing how many quarterbacks they will keep after starter Deshaun Watson . At this point, it feels as likely that all three of Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel , and Taylen Green are on that roster as not. Few believe the Browns long-term answer is currently on the roster. The Minnesota Vikings had hoped they had solved their quarterback need when they drafted JJ McCarthy with the 10th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. The team was so confident that they let QB Sam Darnold leave in free agency to hand the keys over to McCarthy. So far, that has gone so poorly that the Vikings signed Kyler Murray and gave him the starting job early and camp, and now reports are that McCarthy may not even make the initial 53-man roster in Minnesota : O’Connell gave him the day off Wednesday so that he could rest up enough to start Friday’s final preseason matchup with the Broncos. That report from The Athletic fits what we heard from Vikings fans over at The Daily Norseman, who were talking about a McCarthy-for-Sanders trade earlier this week: McCarthy played 10 games last season, after missing his entire rookie year due to a knee injury. With the former Michigan Wolverine as a starter, Minnesota was 6-4, but McCarthy only completed 58% of his passes for 1,632 yards with 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. More than one in the Vikings media believes that McCarthy will not have a chance to add to those numbers: Tomorrow likely ends JJ McCarthy’s time in Minnesota. Worse than getting nothing from the 2023 1.10, the team doubled down on him when they chose to let Sam Darnold walk. title: Browns can’t lose sight of the true goal at the quarterback position
summary: NFL teams, and by extension their fans, certainly love the concept of a developmental quarterback. It is a phenomenon seen across the league every season. A quarterback gets selected in the fifth, sixth, or seventh round of the draft, or perhaps is even an undrafted free agent, but has just enough athletic ability that everyone […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 10: Deshaun Watson #4, Shedeur Sanders #2, Dillon Gabriel #6 and Taylen Green #15 of the Cleveland Browns run a drill during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 10, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images NFL teams, and by extension their fans, certainly love the concept of a developmental quarterback. It is a phenomenon seen across the league every season. A quarterback gets selected in the fifth, sixth, or seventh round of the draft, or perhaps is even an undrafted free agent, but has just enough athletic ability that everyone starts talking themselves into the possibility of what might be. If everything goes absolutely perfectly, so the thinking goes, then perhaps the player can be a viable insurance policy in case the starter is injured or comes due for a big-money contract. Or, perhaps even better, the developmental quarterback can be traded to a desperate team and bring back far more value than they cost. It is a pleasant fiction, no doubt, but more often than not runs into reality. Because for every Tom Brady (a sixth-round draft choice) or Brock Purdy (Mr. Irrelevant), you have a host of players like Athan Kaliakmanis, Quinn Ewers, Chad Kelly, or Ben DiNucci. And as everyone in Cleveland was reminded last season, once the games start for real, practice time is too limited and too valuable to give snaps to anyone other than that week’s starting quarterback. So any “development” that is going to take place in a given year is essentially done by the time the team finishes the preseason schedule. Which brings us to the Cleveland Browns and the current state of their quarterback room. Rookie, Taylen Green, showing off his speed 🏃 NEvsCLE on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Vf6XHfIMw6 — NFL (@NFL) August 28, 2026 Rookie Taylen Green is the quintessential developmental quarterback. Selected in the sixth round of this year’s NFL Draft, Green is clearly the best athlete among the quarterbacks and has the size at 6-foot-6 and 230 pounds to hold up to being hit by NFL players. But his game is still raw, even after making 53 starts in college, and he needs a lot of work to be considered a viable backup, let alone a starter. Nothing wrong with that, of course, only in the case of the Browns, fully 75 percent of their quarterback room are developmental quarterbacks. That may come as a shock to some, but it is true. Dillon Gabriel put up numbers in the first half 😮‍💨 – 12/15 – 186 pass yards – 3 TDs NEvsCLE on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/EO6pUKzGyV — NFL (@NFL) August 28, 2026 Despite his famous last name and legion of online fans, there is not another team that would start Shedeur Sanders at quarterback. Despite a full offseason program, OTAs, minicamps, and training camp, he has still not mastered the basics of being an NFL quarterback. Things like calling the play, being loud enough for the linemen to hear him, or getting rid of the ball. Dillon Gabriel is in the same boat, but for different reasons. He is considered too short at 5-foot-11 to be a starting quarterback, and he can’t make up for that because his lack of arm strength comes out when he tries to throw a deep pass. He can process the operational side of the position just fine, but his physical limitations mean he is destined to be a backup quarterback for the majority of his career. Now that is not to say that either quarterback has not improved over their rookie seasons. That would be unfair to claim. But it comes with the caveat that they had nowhere to go but up after rookie seasons that saw Gabriel at No. 57 in EPA/Play and Sanders at No. 60 . Their Total EPA was even worse, with Gabriel (-53.85) checking in at No. 78 and Sanders (-73.37) at No. 81, ahead of just Brady Cook, Geno Smith, and fellow rookie Cam Ward. Shedeur Sanders enters the game and completes his first pass 🎯 CLEvsCHI on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/uRgDiH2kaL — NFL (@NFL) August 15, 2026 Having one developmental quarterback on the roster? That’s fine. Having three of your four quarterbacks fall into the developmental category – especially when the starter is Deshaun Watson? That’s a problem. As Browns fans, we’ve been beaten down by bad quarterback play so much over the years that many have forgotten what the actual goal is from the position. It’s not to simply be better, or more popular, than the guy sitting next to you in a meeting room. The goal is to actually be good at the game. Good enough to consistently take your team to the playoffs and have a realistic chance at winning a Super Bowl. If you can’t do that as a quarterback, then literally nothing else matters. And the reality is that the Browns don’t currently have a quarterback on the roster capable of meeting that benchmark. It is going to be another long season for the Browns, but that doesn’t mean it can’t be enjoyable. And it certainly does not have to be filled with arguing over a quarterback room that will undergo a major renovation once the season is finished. So sit back, watch the young guys on offense, take a look at what the defense is doing under a new defensive coordinator, and enjoy the weekly tilts as much as possible. And above all, pray that the decision makers in Berea never forget the most important aspect of what they need from the quarterback position.

title: The surprising Cowboys player who leads in total preseason snaps
summary: You’ve read the title of this post, so you’re fairly sure the Cowboys’ leader in preseason snaps is a down-roster player you probably haven’t heard much of. But do you think you can at least figure out which position that player is playing? Perhaps it’s a down-roster defensive back with tons of special teams snaps? […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Sam Howell #16 of the Dallas Cowboys celebrates after scoring a two point conversion during the fourth quarter of the 2026 NFL preseason game against the New Orleans Saints at AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images You’ve read the title of this post, so you’re fairly sure the Cowboys’ leader in preseason snaps is a down-roster player you probably haven’t heard much of. But do you think you can at least figure out which position that player is playing? Perhaps it’s a down-roster defensive back with tons of special teams snaps? Perhaps an edge rusher forced to play extra snaps because the Cowboys limited plays for their top guys? Maybe one of the offensive linemen? Or is it a wide receiver doubling as a special teams regular? It’s not a quarterback (even though Joe Milton ranks eighth overall in total regular snaps with 106), it’s not a running back, and it’s certainly not the fullback. The player leading the Cowboys in preseason snaps is OT Drew Shelton, with 174 snaps over three games (160 on offense, 14 on special teams). This comes as a bit of a surprise as the Cowboys have struggled at both backup tackle spots this offseason, but it looks like they were determined to maximize the fourth-round pick’s snaps and maybe accelerate his development in the process. Officially listed as the backup right tackle, Shelton started at right tackle in the preseason opener and then started at left tackle the next two games. The rookie struggled initially (PFF grade in Games 1 and 2: 48.5, 28.9) before posting his best grade of the preseason against the Saints with 67.1. Still, the Cowboys made a move to bring in Broderick Jones at the position in a trade with the Steelers. Also, a look at who showed out in the finale and who hurt their chances. In injury news, the Cowboys lose a third-year veteran who was looking to make the team. Then, would the Cowboys put one of […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Broderick Jones #77 of the Pittsburgh Steelers in action during the game against the Green Bay Packers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys concluded their preseason, and feeling unsettled about their team, added some offensive tackle help. Also, a look at who showed out in the finale and who hurt their chances. In injury news, the Cowboys lose a third-year veteran who was looking to make the team. Then, would the Cowboys put one of the summer standouts on waivers? Sources: Cowboys acquire OT Jones in exchange for two draft picks – Brooke Pryor, ESPN Looking for offensive line help, the Cowboys made a trade for a former first-round pick. The Steelers are sending Jones and a fourth-round pick to the Cowboys in exchange for a future third- and sixth-round pick, sources told ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. Jones, whom the Steelers selected after trading up for the No. 14 pick, was the team’s starting left tackle in 2025 until he sustained a season-ending neck injury in Week 11 against the Chicago Bears . After a lengthy recovery from the resulting spinal fusion surgery, Jones was cleared to resume football activities at the start of training camp, but he struggled to return to form. Grading the trade: Steelers just ripped off the Dallas Cowboys when you see what they received in return for Broderick Jones – Rob Gregson, A to Z Sports Did the Cowboys get fleeced? Not everyone is happy with the cost of doing business. For all the criticism Omar Khan has received for the Broderick Jones selection, the Steelers general manager just pulled off something remarkable. To take a tackle who was unplayable because of his medicals and everything Pittsburgh saw in the preseason, and flip that player into a third- and sixth-round pick while only giving up Jones and a fourth, that is tremendous value. I’m still having trouble wrapping my brain around it. We had to check two to three times from multiple outlets to make sure it was true that the Steelers are receiving a third-round pick in exchange for Jones. Not only a third, but a sixth as well. 2 Winners, 2 Losers from Cowboys final dress rehearsal vs Saints – Angel Torres, Cowboys Wire Two players came through with big games when they needed it most. However, others fell shorts and it could be the end of the line for them with the team. Cornerback Caelen Carson opened the preseason against Seattle with two opening-drive penalties that eventually ended with the Seahawks ‘ only touchdown of the night. Carson once again committed a costly penalty against New Orleans that resulted in another score =. Dallas entered the contest with 17 total penalties called on them and were flagged six additional times for infractions against the Saints. Of the 23 total penalties in the preseason, Carson alone has accounted for four, or 17.3% of the total penalties accepted. Marist Liufau to have surgery on fractured forearm; will miss ‘some weeks’ – Tommy Yarish, dallascowboys.com The converted linebacker got some unfortunate injury news and he’s going to be out for significant time. Cowboys outside linebacker Marist Liufau is expected to miss “some weeks” with a fractured forearm and will have surgery as early as Monday, according to Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer. Liufau suffered the injury in Friday’s preseason game against the Saints late in the first quarter while making a tackle. “What a great competitor. He’ll be back.” Schottenheimer said of Liufau. Cowboys’ Jordan Hudson just earned himself a lot of money (back in college) – Levi Dombro, The Landry Hat From NFL gridiron to BMOC? Jordan Hudson likely goes back to school with extra change in his pocket. Don’t ask me to explain the rules; it’s a bunch of complex legalese and people suing each other so that some big college programs can have a better shot at competing in a wild west landscape that seemingly has no actual rules, even though they somehow seem to be taking advantage of them. Hudson’s big outing against the Saints, combined with reports surfacing on Thursday that he was granted eligibility to return to the collegiate ranks and enter the transfer portal, means that the young player could get a major NIL bag from a college looking to kick its morals aside and win some games. Dallas Cowboys Can’t Afford To Let Camden Brown Get Sniped By NFL Rivals – Randy Gurzi, Sports Illustrated The Cowboys would be wise not to get cute and keep Camden Brown on the roster. If they place him on waivers, he could go bye bye. Despite his knack for big plays, Brown finds himself deep on the Dallas depth chart. The Cowboys have two of the best wideouts in the game in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. They’re joined by Ryan Flournoy, who had a breakout season in 2025. There’s also KaVontae Turpin who is their WR4 and primary kick returner.

title: What the Cowboys’ new offensive tackle brings to the team
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have addressed their tackle depth by trading for a former first-round pick of the Pittsburgh Steelers, Broderick Jones. In exchange for Jones and a Steelers 2027 fourth-round pick , the Cowboys sent the Steelers a 2027 third- and sixth-round pick. Many expected the team to look outside for help at tackle, but […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 27: Broderick Jones #77 of the Pittsburgh Steelers stands on the field between plays during the fourth quarter of a preseason game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have addressed their tackle depth by trading for a former first-round pick of the Pittsburgh Steelers, Broderick Jones. In exchange for Jones and a Steelers 2027 fourth-round pick , the Cowboys sent the Steelers a 2027 third- and sixth-round pick. Many expected the team to look outside for help at tackle, but this move is a little surprising. What did the Cowboys get from this deal? We’ll take a look at his journey so far and discuss how he fits with his new team. Jones was the fourth offensive lineman selected in the 2023 draft because of his great athleticism. He showed impressive speed for a guy his size. He possessed agility and power from heavy hands and a strong grip. He didn’t allow a single sack in 2022, and he helped the Georgia Bulldogs win back-to-back National Championships. The sky was the limit for this athletically gifted lineman. Unfortunately, his NFL adventure has not been so pleasant. The Steelers moved him to right tackle midway through his rookie season, where he did okay in run support, but struggled mightily in pass protection. It was a mixed bag, but there was definitely something to work with. Things went south during his second year. Right tackle wasn’t his thing. He wasn’t technically sound, and speed rushers abused him regularly. He gave up 11 sacks and frequently committed penalties. Last season, he moved back to his more natural position at left tackle, hoping to unleash his strengths, but things didn’t improve. He continued to struggle with pass protection, and his season was cut short after 11 games when he suffered a neck injury and underwent spinal fusion surgery. The Steelers declined to pick up his fifth-year option, meaning he has one year left on his rookie deal. He entered camp fighting for the swing tackle spot in Pittsburgh, but his performance has once again been underwhelming, leading to this trade. Here is what the tape has shown us thus far. He doesn’t secure blocks well. Defenders get into his chest and carom off him with ease. Despite his length, he doesn’t use his hands very well and can be tossed aside. He plays stiff, failing to bend his knees and gain leverage. He can be a lazy blocker. He’ll strike, but he doesn’t always land, and he’s quick to give up on the play after he thinks the job is done. He also wears his emotion on his sleeve, showing his frustration too often. There are some good things. He is a former first-rounder after all. Before the snap, he’s always looking around. He has a plan. He pops out of his stance quickly and has good length. He can move from one defender to the next seamlessly. His agility is still alive. He needs to learn how to put his strengths together, and so far, he’s just too scattered. The Cowboys need depth at tackle and are hoping a change of scenery can spark a turnaround for this young lineman. Jones possesses the tools to match Klayton Adams’ multiple, gap-heavy run schemes. He has the athleticism to kick out or pull across the line of scrimmage, allowing him to be an aggressive hunter in the second level. While he hasn’t shown it at the pro level, Jones has the strength to latch on and torque to displace defenders. He also has that mean temperament that fits well with the Cowboys’ aggressive nature. That’s one more angry blocker in the trenches for this group. But unless he can harness that anger into productive reps, that won’t mean a whole lot. This is an interesting move for the Cowboys. One might have thought they’d go after something a little more reliable instead of an unfinished project with high upside. It’s also a bit pricey considering the draft cost, but if they can somehow crack the code and unleash his raw talent, he’ll become another screaming deal courtesy of the Steelers.

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 15
summary: It is Day 15 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: DALLAS, TX - CIRCA 1970's: Running back Calvin Hill #35 of the Dallas Cowboys carries the ball against the San Francisco 49ers during a circa 1970's NFL game at Texas Stadium in Dallas, Texas. Hill played for the Cowboys from 1969-75. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Day 15 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. We’ve got a fun one here for Day 15 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit the victory that finally carried the Cowboys into the Super Bowl. After years of postseason disappointment, Dallas relied on Duane Thomas, two decisive interceptions and another dominant defensive performance to defeat San Francisco in the NFC Championship Game. Sunday, January 3, 1971 Kezar Stadium, San Francisco, California Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 17, San Francisco 49ers 10 The Cowboys’ path had not been straightforward. Dallas stood at 5-4 before winning its final five regular-season games to claim the newly formed NFC East with a 10-4 record. A grinding 5-0 playoff win over Detroit then sent Tom Landry’s team west to face the 49ers at Kezar Stadium. San Francisco presented a serious challenge. Quarterback John Brodie had been named NFL MVP, while former Cowboys defensive coordinator Dick Nolan was now leading the 49ers against his old mentor. San Francisco had also eliminated the 12-win Minnesota Vikings on the road to reach the conference championship. The 49ers opened the scoring through Bruce Gossett’s 16-yard field goal. Dallas struggled to throw against San Francisco’s defense, but Mike Clark answered with a 21-yard kick during the second quarter. Neither offense reached the end zone before halftime, leaving the game tied at 3-3. Everything changed during the third quarter. After Brodie was sacked on first down, Lee Roy Jordan stepped in front of his next pass and intercepted it at the San Francisco 13-yard line. Thomas scored on the following play, breaking through several defenders for a 13-yard touchdown that moved Dallas ahead 10-3. Brodie tried to answer by attacking downfield, but Mel Renfro intercepted an underthrown pass intended for Gene Washington. The Cowboys converted their second takeaway into another touchdown when Craig Morton found Walt Garrison from five yards out, extending the lead to 17-3. San Francisco responded before the end of the quarter. Brodie connected with Dick Witcher for a 26-yard touchdown, cutting the deficit to seven points and ending Dallas’ long streak without allowing a touchdown. The 49ers still had an entire quarter to complete the comeback, but the Cowboys’ defense refused to break. San Francisco’s best fourth-quarter opportunities went unfinished. Gossett’s long field-goal attempt fell short with approximately eight minutes remaining. Later, the 49ers faced fourth-and-seven with just over two minutes left, but Brodie’s pass to Ken Willard could not be secured in traffic. Dallas took possession and closed out their first conference championship in franchise history. This game belongs on the countdown because it removed the barrier that had followed Dallas throughout the late 1960s. The Cowboys had lost NFL Championship Games to Green Bay in 1966 and 1967, then suffered further playoff disappointment in the following two seasons. Winning at Kezar finally placed Landry’s franchise on football’s biggest stage. #Cowboys vs #49ers 1970 NFC Championship Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 17, San Francisco 49ers 10 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/Cwhmk3XQhJ — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 29, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Thomas rushed for 143 yards, more than twice San Francisco’s entire team total of 61 rushing yards. title: Final 53-man roster predictions for the Cowboys
summary: We are approaching final roster cuts of the 2026 season when the Dallas Cowboys will have to make their decisions about who to roll with to start the new year. There’s usually some roster gymnastics included as teams make last-second deals and grab guys from other teams, but who do you expect to see on […]
full_text: We are approaching final roster cuts of the 2026 season when the Dallas Cowboys will have to make their decisions about who to roll with to start the new year. There’s usually some roster gymnastics included as teams make last-second deals and grab guys from other teams, but who do you expect to see on the list? Here is a final 53-man roster predictions for the Cowboys. Quarterback Dak Prescott, Joe Milton III, and Sam Howell What’s changed: After the final preseason game showed some flashback flaws for Milton and reminded us that Howell is still pretty decent, the team could choose to go long at the game’s most important position. Running Back Javonte Williams, Malik Davis, Jaydon Blue, and Hunter Luepke What’s changed: Not playing Davis or Blue in the preseason finale cements their spot on the roster, while Phil Mafah or Israel Abanikanda have done nothing to sway opinions. Tight End Jake Ferguson, Brevyn Spann-Ford, and Luke Schoonmaker What’s changed: Nothing. This one has been set for a while as the only thing up for consideration was if undrafted free agent Michael Trigg would earn a spot, which he hasn’t. Wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Ryan Flournoy, KaVontae Turpin, and Jonathan Mingo What’s changed: Nothing. The roster battle between Mingo and UDFA Camden Brown still goes to the veteran. The rookie has had a great camp and deserves to make it, but the team also has other young choices like draft pick Anthony Smith and fellow UDFA Jordan Hudson who will clear waivers if Brown doesn’t. Offensive line Tyler Guyton, Tyler Smith, Cooper Beebe, Tyler Booker, Terence Steele, T.J. Bass, Nick Leverett, Nate Thomas, and Drew Shelton What’s changed: This group still has the most questions. Trevor Keegan still has his shot in the dark, but Leverett has been the more impressive interior guy in preseason action. Much to the chagrin of the fanbase, Shelton sticks around as a development project. He played considerably better in the finale. Nate Thomas is an enigma and could be a surprise cut if the team opts to look outside for a veteran tackle . Second-year tackle-turned-guard gets a roster spot; however, he could start the season on injured reserve after dealing with a knee issue. Outside Linebacker Rashan Gary, Donovan Ezeiruaku, Von Miller, Malachi Lawrence, and Sam Williams What’s changed: The team has really pushed hard to see what Sam Williams and Marist Liufau could do in the new system, but the results haven’t been good. Liufau broke his wrist in Friday night’s game, so he’ll start the year on injured reserve if they keep him. Williams played deep into the game. He might be left off if the coaches go with James Houston, and don’t write off the guy everyone loves to write off, Tyrus Wheat. He continues to do a little bit of everything and is just one of those guys coaches love to have on their team. Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, Otito Ogbannia, LT Overton, and Jay Toia What’s changed: No changes, but the dependent factor here is the health of veteran free agent Jonathan Bullard. If his groin/abdomen is good to go, he makes the team. If he starts on injured reserve, second-year nose tackle Toia slides into his spot. Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, Dee Winters, Jaishawn Barham, and Shemar James What’s changed: Nothing. The first three are rock solid, with the speed of second-year draft pick James rounding out the last spot. Justin Barron or Curtis Robinson have an outside chance for one of those final spots, but it seems very reasonable that they’ll clear waivers and return on the practice squad. Cornerback DaRon Bland, Cobie Durant, Shavon Revel Jr., Caelen Carson, Devin Moore, and Derion Kendrick What’s changed: No adjustments from last time. The first three are chalk, the last three are a little cringe. Carson may have his problems, but he can be pesky as depth corners go. Moore is a development project taken in the fourth round, so it’s assumed he’ll be given a chance. Kendrick remains the off-script selection as he continues to do well in preseason action. Word on the street is that an outside free agent will take one of these spots, with Adoree Jackson’s name floated around a lot, so prepare for that. Safety Caleb Downs, Malik Hooker, Jalen Thompson, P.J. Locke, and Markquese Bell What’s changed: Nothing. The team loves all these guys. Julius Wood is a pet cat of many who has played well and rung bells, but the coaches appear to have rung their own Bell when it comes to the safety pecking order. Special teams Brandon Aubrey, Bryan Anger, and Trent Sieg What’s changed: Absolutely nothing, and we’re perfectly happy about that. Here is the final 53 with injury designations projected. Note: only 52 spots are filled, as one is being left for an outside player, whether it’s a free agent or a claim from another team.

title: 4 biggest questions facing the coaching staff after preseason finale
summary: Although it would have been nice for the Dallas Cowboys to end their preseason on a high note, the 27-24 loss to the New Orleans Saints still provided useful insights into who is secure on the roster, and who let opportunities slip away. With the preseason complete, Dallas can shift fully toward the season opener […]
full_text: Although it would have been nice for the Dallas Cowboys to end their preseason on a high note, the 27-24 loss to the New Orleans Saints still provided useful insights into who is secure on the roster, and who let opportunities slip away. With the preseason complete, Dallas can shift fully toward the season opener against the New York Giants. Before the cutdown to 53, here are the hardest decisions the coaches and personnel department face. 1. Keeping three quarterbacks? After a fierce competition for the backup job, Dallas faces a tough call between Joe Milton and Sam Howell. Milton was terrific in the first two games but took a step back against the Saints (8-of-15 for 92 yards). Howell seized the opportunity with a strong second-half showing (12-of-18 for 155 yards and two touchdowns). He displayed resilience and calm under pressure, including a tough two-point conversion run that tied the game. That doesn’t erase Milton’s strong summer and the improvements he has shown. Do the Cowboys choose one over the other, or try to keep both? Howell may offer the higher floor, while Milton has the higher ceiling. In a scenario where Dak Prescott misses extended time, whom would you rather have? With an expected improvement on defense, does one style complement the unit better than the other? If roster space allows, Dallas should try to keep both. 2. Dropping Izzy and/or Mafah? Who stays and who goes between Phil Mafah and Israel Abanikanda? Or are they both gone? The Cowboys surprised some observers by sitting Jaydon Blue and Malik Davis against the Saints, giving the primary work to Abanikanda and Mafah. That decision raises the question of whether either will make the 53-man roster. Mafah was the more productive runner, while Abanikanda had a costly fumble. Blue’s and Davis’ inactivity strongly suggests both have made the team. Counting fullback Hunter Luepke, that would mean Dallas is already carrying four players in the backfield. The sense is that if the team waives both, it feels comfortable reclaiming at least one via waivers. This may not be the hardest call, but one that will have to be made. 3. Exposing Camden Brown to waivers? Are the Cowboys brave enough to put Camden Brown on waivers in hopes of sneaking him onto the practice squad? Brown has made one play after another this summer. His strong practices translated to the games: six receptions for 166 yards (27.7 average) and two touchdowns. He shows exceptional ability to locate the ball to make difficult catches, and he shows consistency as he delivered another highlight-reel high-point grab versus the Saints. The top four receivers—CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Ryan Flournoy, and KaVontae Turpin—are locked in. Dallas must also decide on Jonathan Mingo (who didn’t dress), Anthony Smith, and Marquez Valdes-Scantling. Mingo’s absence suggests that final receiver battle is between keeping Brown or not keeping a sixth WR. Dallas would be crazy to cut Brown, but stranger things have happened. 4. Do they need to sign a veteran tackle? Drew Shelton saw extended playing time throughout the preseason. While he had positive moments, he still needs more development before he’s ready as the primary swing tackle. Nate Thomas has also been inconsistent. That leaves the question of whether the team can afford to stand pat or whether it should add a veteran. Among currently available options are Joseph Noteboom (who has Dallas-area ties) and Cam Robinson (who brings extensive starting experience). Once cuts take place league-wide, Dallas will have additional choices and can make a more informed decision on whether to get outside help or stick with the current group. What’s your top roster question the team needs to answer?

title: How the final preseason game changed the Cowboys backup QB plan
summary: There are high expectations for this year’s Dallas Cowboys. Improvements on defense combined with what looks like another potent offensive group set the table for a fun season. However, all that fun can end quickly if Dak Prescott goes down. We’ve seen it happen multiple times in recent years, and it doesn’t feel good. While […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Sam Howell #16 of the Dallas Cowboys throws during the third quarter of the 2026 NFL preseason game against the New Orleans Saints at AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images There are high expectations for this year’s Dallas Cowboys. Improvements on defense combined with what looks like another potent offensive group set the table for a fun season. However, all that fun can end quickly if Dak Prescott goes down. We’ve seen it happen multiple times in recent years, and it doesn’t feel good. While a long-term absence for Prescott is a recipe for a losing season, the team can still absorb a short-term injury stint if they have a viable backup on the roster. We’ve seen them do exactly that when Cooper Rush went 4-1 over a five-game stretch in 2022. A quality backup is important, especially with how much firepower they have on offense. They don’t want all that goodness to go to waste. Enter Joe Milton III and Sam Howell, who have been battling it out for the team’s primary backup quarterback job. And it’s been quite the battle. They’ve gone back and forth, one-upping each other throughout the preseason. Howell started the first preseason game, but Milton jumped him after a strong performance and earned the start in the second game. He kept the momentum going with an even better performance last week, but on Friday night, he had some moments where he was off, opening the door for Howell. Sure enough, Howell responded with his best preseason performance. Suddenly, the backup QB battle got a whole lot more interesting. Milton’s development has been encouraging. This is his third year, and his growth has pleased the coaching staff and fans alike. Last week against the Cardinals, his comfort level showed. He processed things quickly, his footwork was sharp, and he delivered beautifully thrown balls to his receivers. It was fantastic. At certain moments against the Saints, he reverted to the previous version of Milton. He was skittish, his throws were off-balance, and he delivered those patented overthrown passes that we saw far too often last season. This small sample doesn’t undo what he’s accomplished this year, but it creates enough doubt to make one wonder if they should have a contingency to their contingency. Howell’s solid play highlights this dilemma even more. When they have a third quarterback who shows he can command the offense and make good decisions, it’s hard to toss that aside. Would they dare risk exposing him to the waiver wire so a more QB-needy team could steal him? On Friday night, Howell looked like a good backup quarterback. He stayed calm in the pocket, but evaded pressure when things collapsed around him. He made quick, well-placed throws to his receivers. And when he had a chance to make a big play, he did, erasing a 15-point deficit when it otherwise looked as if the offense wasn’t going to find the end zone in this game. This third preseason game has thrown a wrench into the backup quarterback situation, assuming the team hasn’t already made their mind up. Maybe keeping three quarterbacks has always been their plan. It’s tough to say. What’s even tougher is making this decision if they are still undecided. The Cowboys have several roster battles in flux where they can use any extra spot available. Milton pulling away with the backup job made things simpler, but now it might be smarter to hedge their bet and keep both. The most important factor is ensuring they have a quality backup, which it seems like they do. And that’s Milton. If they want extra security, they can choose to hang on to Howell as well. Injuries can change the landscape quickly, and holding on to good players in the most important position in football is never a bad idea. That means the Cowboys could enter the 2026 season carrying three quarterbacks, so prepare your final roster predictions accordingly.

summary: Voting before the final preseason game, Broncos Country was already high on Sam Ehlinger as Denver’s backup QB. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Voting before the final preseason game, Broncos Country was already high on Sam Ehlinger as Denver’s backup QB. But had the poll benn taken after the win over the Vikings — in which Ehlinger threw three touchdowns in spite of an early interception — it’s possible the presumed No. 3 quarterback would have had even more votes for pushing him up the depth chart to No.2. No matter which game and who the opponent is, three TDs is impressive. Head coach Sean Payton was particularly impressed with the second touchdown, which officially went down as a 14-yard touchdown pass to player-of-the-night Cody Schrader. But in reality the play was more like a 30-yard pass after scrambling outside and finding a wide open Schrader. “Well, there’s more to it than that,” Payton said of his chest-bump celly on the sidelines with No. 4. Payton explained that not only was he happy for the touchdown, he was relieved that Ehlinger didn’t run into him while scrambling toward the sidelines. “After he threw it, he was falling backwards and I kind of was in the white … two more feet and my concern was all of a sudden the ball hit my chest and I’m the reason he doesn’t throw it. I was excited for him. It was a really good [throw].” CODY MFN SCHRADER TOUCHDOWN pic.twitter.com/GoL2zNOfD9 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 29, 2026 Asked about whether the Broncos would keep three QBs, Sean Payton merely offered, “we’ll see.” Ehlinger knows the drill. That’s the life of a backup quarterback. But he made his case, and now he waits. “When it comes down to roster decisions and things of that nature, it’s completely out of my control, and so I don’t derive my confidence from the result of what happens with numbers,” he said. “I have great confidence in this organization, and the relationships that we have and the way that they’ve handled things up until this point. So I’m in a really good spot.” If Ehlinger doesn’t stay in Denver, he said he’d look forward to whatever opportunity there is. At this moment, however, he has his mind on something more than making the roster. “Well my wife’s due date is on Tuesday. title: Sean Payton challenged Broncos roster hopefuls to “make us spin the chair”
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! For players on the roster bubble, the last preseason game is their last audition. Even if it’s not enough to stick with the Denver Broncos, it’s an opportunity to show other teams they deserve a shot. After the 34-6 drubbing of the Minnesota Vikings, there are current Broncos who made their […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 28: Head Coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos walks on the sidelines during the second quarter against the Minnesota Vikings in a preseason game at Empower Field at Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! For players on the roster bubble, the last preseason game is their last audition. Even if it’s not enough to stick with the Denver Broncos, it’s an opportunity to show other teams they deserve a shot. After the 34-6 drubbing of the Minnesota Vikings, there are current Broncos who made their case for a roster spot. Namely, Sam Ehlinger, Justin Joly, and Cody Schrader. For others, the NFL dream may come to an end. Now it’s in the hands of Denver head coach Sean Payton and general manager George Paton. Payton had an interesting analogy for the guys on the bubble after the win against the Vikings: “Look at the beginning of the night, just talking to these guys before the game. Historically speaking, it used to be four preseason games; obviously, it’s three now, but this game has had its moments. I’m talking about the last preseason game where Raheem Mostert goes for 140, (Victor) Cruz has three touchdowns, or there’s just so many times that all of a sudden somebody made a team. “So we talk about that all the time, there are a number of guys that it’s not as important for, but there are a number that it’s the most important thing, period. I don’t watch a lot of TV, but my wife likes watching (The) Voice, where the singers sing. So today it was like, ‘Hey, make us spin the chair.’ Make us spin it.” Payton and Paton want this to be difficult. The better the depth, the better the Broncos will be. And for a team coming off a 14-3 season and hosting the AFC Championship Game, that pretty much brings everyone back, only making their roster decisions even tougher. “I look back to my first year here, and we were looking to claim,” Payton said to the media after the win against Minnesota. “We’ll find spots, and that was like that in New Orleans early on, and as you build something that gets a little bit more polished, players are … Gradually, the quality of your team, it becomes a harder roster to make. So those teams out there that have new coaches that are rebuilding, they’ll be more active, and those are the teams sometimes that can end up with one of your players.” The better the depth, the more likely it is that Payton knows he’ll lose quality players. The other factor in this, as Payton frequently says, is the release of players from other rosters. That’s the other factor in all of this. “We’re rooting for every one of them,” Payton said. “Remember it’s the right 53 and getting the proper evaluation. I will spend more time concerned with who’s making it as opposed to the ones that maybe possibly aren’t, and I just finished saying this in the locker room. Oftentimes, in those tough meetings, the next two days, within a month, within two months, all of a sudden, a player will be back in your building, that happens. “So nothing’s changed relative to this time of the season. The big change obviously is what we went from four to three preseason games. The roster has to be down by four o’clock Sunday. And then Monday, practice squads will be formed. So our practice Monday gets pushed back a little later because of that.” To carry over Payton’s analogy to The Voice, we’ll find out who forced Payton and Paton to turn their chair. Broncos links
