title: The Day After the Day After: Houston Texans lose 16-13 at Carolina Panthers to end their preseason
summary: Preseason games are done, but the work is only beginning. Finally, the preseason is over. The last few games will wrap up this weekend and then teams immediately roll into trimming the rosters. The only people who will be stressing as much as those players on the roster bubbles will be the front offices. Not […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - AUGUST 28: Carolina Panthers quarterback Kyle Trask (14)runs with the ball during a preseason NFL football game between the Houston Texans and the Carolina Panthers on August 28, 2026, at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C.(Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Preseason games are done, but the work is only beginning . Finally, the preseason is over. The last few games will wrap up this weekend and then teams immediately roll into trimming the rosters. The only people who will be stressing as much as those players on the roster bubbles will be the front offices. Not only do they have to finalize any cuts, but they will be scouring all means of communication (wires, social media, phones, etc) to find those critical depth pieces to fill out the final roster (53 on the active roster (up to 48 suited players + 5 inactive for the actual game) and up to 17 practice squad players) before the start of the regular season. For the Texans, while they’ve made some moves due to injury (more later), they will frantically build roster depth. Given the emphasis on special teams and trying to solidify depth, especially along the lines, these moves could have some actual game impact. Where the value is: The preseason game counts for far less now than in the past. Those looking for clues about the potential fortunes of a franchise should look at the joint practices. The reports coming out of the Carolina/Houston sessions showcased a dominant Houston defense, to a degree that Carolina coach Dave Canales lost track of basic counting . It also noted that the offense, with Stroud, Collins, and Montgomery, could move at-will against a competent Carolina defense. Reports from other joint practices seemed to validate the optimistic reports about Houston’s offense. Granted, Houston’s preseason slate didn’t include the top tier contenders, but the Panthers were a playoff team last season and Las Vegas improved from whatever last year was. Overall, while there is not much to say about the games themselves, the practices auger well. The Injury Demons have a new Houston home: For any fans of the Houston Astros between 2023-2025, you might have wondered if someone unleashed an ancient curse that sprang forth demons that would ravage the team with injuries. The butchers’ bill for the Astros was quite painful and extensive. In 2026, the injury demons seem to have left them alone. They just moved to a different part of the city. While there have been no shortage of dings, scraps and bruises as Texans’ players get into game shape, there has been a rash of rather substantial injuries. You had the first preseason game when QB3 Graham Martz suffered a season-ending ACL tear in game action. The following week of practice saw Houston lose a significant offensive weapon, as WR Jayden Higgins tore his ACL. Then Dylan Horton was lost due to a torn Achilles. Just this past week, major free agent pick-up OT Braden Smith left practice in a cart due to a foot injury. Joining him for medical examination would be backup DL Ali Gaye, who was brought in to cover for Horton. Throw less severe, but no less disruptive injuries to Jaylen Noel (hamstring) and Wade Woodaz (thumb), and the Texans are dealing with some roster attrition. This has already forced emergencies moves by the front office. The loss of Higgins and Noel, along with the slow reintegration of Tank Dell, drove Houston to sign two veteran WRs in Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones, along with trading for Kayshon Boutte from New England, at the cost of Jaylen Reed and a 2028 7 th round pick. While Smith won’t miss as much time as his last season with the Colts, he will not return to the line for a few weeks. Higgins was supposed to provide Stroud another receiving weapon. Horton and Gaye were not projected starters, but both figured to see time as part of the DL rotation. We are not talking cursed-by-an-electric-substation 49ers-level of injury, but this is not great. It is early and players like Smith, Noel and Woodaz should be back, but for a team with Super Bowl aspirations, this not how you want to break camp. Time Helps: Brett Rypien may not make the final roster. Given that Houston only had four total QBs in camp and Mertz is out for the season, the team will at least want another arm with some experience with the squad. While not making people think of his uncle Mark during his 1991 MVP season, Rypien did play better in this game (13 of 23, 101 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT). The failures of the final drive rest more with a porous Oline vs. Rypien himself. Having more reps with the squad helped him vs. the limited hours he had last week. While no one is under any illusions that playing Rypien will be a great thing for Houston, having him as an emergency QB on the roster wouldn’t be the worst thing in the world. FUN WITH NUMBERS: 2003: The last time the Texans had a winless preseason. Preseason records, pride among certain types of workers. However, it is worth noting that this 0-3 preseason is only the 2nd time in the Texans’ 25 years of existence that the squad did not log a preseason win. You have to go all the way back to 2003, when the then-second year squad went 0-4. That team would finish 5-11. Even in the worst of the worst-case scenarios, Houston should expect to finish with more wins than that, and definitely more wins than this preseason. 10: Total second half points scored in Houston’s preseason games . When Fairbairn hit a 47-yard field goal with 1:11 left in the 3rd quarter, it marked the first second-half score for Houston this entire preseason. The Rypien 6-yard TD pass to Zay Jones marked the first second-half TD for the squad this preseason. Yes, most of the players at this point in the contest are likely off to other jobs after this weekend, but for those players that Houston might look to for depth, it isn’t the biggest endorsement for their being meaningful contributors to the roster. GAME BALLS: While there were some stand-out players, like DE Sebastian Harsh (3 total tackles (2 solo), 1 sack/1TFL) and George Odum (11 tackles (7 solo), 1 PD, 1 INT), in light of the pending roster cuts, we will be extra generous with game balls and hand those out to those players who come Sunday night will no longer be on the Texans roster, and for up to 25% of those cuts, likely the last time they put on the NFL jersey of their dreams. SHOULD BE FORCED TO LISTENING TO PANTHER’S GM DAN MORGAN DRONE ABOUT HIS ROSTER MOVES ON REPEAT WHILE WORKING ON MAKING DAVID TEPPER LOOK LIKE A NICE GUY Panthers’ GM Dan Morgan : Maybe he is shaping up to be a good GM, but don’t let that man ever talk in an extended interview, or if you do, issue a warning about not operating heavy machinery if forced to listen. Houston’s Play in Inclement Weather: Being a warm weather team that plays primarily in a domed stadium, Houston is going to have some disadvantages when it comes to playing in weather. That bore out in a rainy game. Yes, both teams had issues with ball security, but it was especially apparent that Houston had issues with dealing with the weather (4 turnovers and multiple other fumbles). Given that brutal weather like cold can impact key Houston players, whatever the team can do to account for that is a must.

title: Colts backup QB battle heads to split decision after preseason finale
summary: The Indianapolis Colts closed the preseason with a 25-16 loss to the Detroit Lions inside Lucas Oil Stadium, giving both quarterbacks vying for the backup job one final quarter to showcase why they deserve to suit up with the horseshoe on their helmet each Sunday.  Detroit certainly didn’t make things easier and controlled the preseason […]
full_text: Indianapolis Colts quarterbacks Riley Leonard #15 and Anthony Richardson #5 throw passes to receivers during training camp practice at Droplight Grand Park Sports Campus in Westfield, Ind. —July 26, 2025. | Thomas Butler-Guerrero The Indianapolis Colts closed the preseason with a 25-16 loss to the Detroit Lions inside Lucas Oil Stadium, giving both quarterbacks vying for the backup job one final quarter to showcase why they deserve to suit up with the horseshoe on their helmet each Sunday. Detroit certainly didn’t make things easier and controlled the preseason finale with 356 total yards, running 75 offensive plays while converting 13-of-19 third downs. Indianapolis was limited to just 48 plays in comparison and finished just 1-for-10 on third down. Despite the Colts’ defense giving their offense three short fields, Indy could only score 16 points on nine true drives. Anthony Richardson Sr. and Riley Leonard made for a whimsical debate over the course of training camp through the preseason. Richardson, the fourth overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, got the start with the first-team offensive line in a unit that also featured receiver Keenan Allen making his Colts debut. On the Colts’ second offensive play, Richardson dropped back and found Allen on a deep crosser for 24 yards to march right into Lions territory. Yes, you read that correctly. It was Allen who caught the first pass of the game, which would actually be the Colts’ second-longest play from scrimmage. welcome to indy Keenan Allen. 🤝 #DETvsIND on CBS4 pic.twitter.com/RDUDvrnVSj — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) August 29, 2026 The Colts’ first two drives stalled just outside of the red zone as Blake Grupe made both of his field goals from 46-yards and 36-yards out. Spencer Shrader later drilled a 60-yarder as both kickers had one last audition in Indy. The starting defensive unit needed just three plays to terminate the Lions opening drive, which set the tone as the Colts forced four turnovers and seized possession inside enemy territory three times. Standout cornerback Sauce Gardner picked off Lions QB Luke Altmyer, who was trying to fit his second throw into a tight window while on the run. Across 17 snaps, Richardson completed 7-of-10 passes for 80 yards and took one sack on his final snap. The offense generated 100 total yards during his three drives. In three preseason games, Richardson finished 21-for-33 with 249 passing yards and one interception. The dual-threat runner also added 68 rushing yards on 10 carries and one rushing touchdown with one fumble. Then it was Leonard’s turn. After the Lions executed a 16-play drive that took over eight minutes off the game clock, Leonard had seven minutes to prove why he should earn the backup QB job. He took the opposite approach of a soft landing as he tucked it himself, lowered his shoulder and absorbed a massive hit from Lions linebacker and former Colt Joe Bachie. It looked bleak as the backups were seemingly stalled near midfield, but facing fourth-and-6, Leonard stepped up in the pocket to deliver a strong throw while taking a hit, and completed a 25-yard pass on a corner to receiver Anthony Gould. The 5-foot-8 slot receiver led the Colts with a team-high four catches for 51 receiving yards, including the longest play of the day. Two plays later, second-year running back DJ Giddens showed patience in the backfield before plunging six yards into the end zone to level the score at 13-13. For both Leonard and Giddens, it was exactly the kind of drive both players needed to potentially stamp their name on the 53-man roster. Then came the other side of the evaluation after rookie Caden Curry recovered a fumble on the ensuing kickoff. Despite excellent field position, nothing developed. Leonard’s first pass fell short after pressure disrupted the pass protection and altered the throw. After he short-armed a bubble route that fell incomplete on the next play, the Lions blitz caused a whiff from Giddens in pass protection, and Leonard’s throw floated into the diving hands of cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. The sixth-round QB was limited to just 12 snaps, but probably wishes that he could erase the last four. In three preseason games, Leonard finished 20-of-42 for 199 passing yards with two interceptions and two fumbles. Richardson caught a rhythm with the second unit that was simply absent when Leonard was the signal caller. Both quarterbacks dealt with their share of errors, whether it was Richardson securing the snaps or Leonard throwing the ball past the line of scrimmage. It is fair to say that Leonard was more consistent during training camp, but if the preseason matters at all, then Richardson clearly outperformed Leonard to earn the backup job. It seems like each time one of the Colts’ rookie edge rushers makes a play, the other seems to make a play of his own. Whether it be in practice or the preseason games, both Caden Curry and George Gumbs Jr. have shown flashes of their ability to wreak havoc in the backfield or create momentum-shifting plays. Curry, a sixth-round draft pick and Greenwood, Ind. native, recovered a fumble on a kickoff late in the first half. Just two plays into the second half, Gumbs stripped the ball out of the hands of Altmyer, then recovered the fumble to give the Colts reserves excellent field position. Gumbs got it! #DETvsIND on CBS4 pic.twitter.com/KfKKJZtosZ — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) August 29, 2026 There are just 24 hours until all 32 NFL franchises must decrease their rosters from 90 players to a final 53-man roster, by Sunday at 6 p.m. The Colts can allow a third emergency QB to suit up without having to use an active roster spot, but the decision will ultimately decide who the organization intends to continue developing heading into the 2026 season.
author: Thomas Butler-Guerrero

title: Colts fall to Lions, 25-16, in preseason finale, but backups show a bit more fight
summary: The Indianapolis Colts are winless in this years’ preseason, finishing 0-2-1, as they fell 25-16 at home to the Detroit Lions. Of course, more important than the actual win in preseason, is how the Colts depth performed well after a disappointing showing last weekend hosting the Atlanta Falcons. Here are some takeaways from this year’s […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - AUGUST 29: DJ Giddens #21 of the Indianapolis Colts runs for a touchdown against the Detroit Lions during the preseason game at Lucas Oil Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts are winless in this years’ preseason, finishing 0-2-1, as they fell 25-16 at home to the Detroit Lions. Of course, more important than the actual win in preseason, is how the Colts depth performed well after a disappointing showing last weekend hosting the Atlanta Falcons. Here are some takeaways from this year’s preseason finale: OFFENSE: Quarterback: The primary backup quarterback job behind starter Daniel Jones appears to be Anthony Richardson Sr.’s (barring a trade), as he completed 7 of 10 passes for 80 total passing yards. Richardson hit the layups, had a few good throws , while missing a few others. However, he was in the driver’s seat entering the day and did nothing to hurt his stock in this one. Meanwhile, presumed 3rd-string quarterback Riley Leonard was rockier, completing 3 of 7 throws for 48 total passing yards and an interception. Colts third-string Easton Stick got his first preseason run, closing this one out in further mop-up duty. He completed 8 of 15 total passes for 78 total passing yards, and unfortunately for him, should be an easy cut, but could be a practice squad signing as the Colts look to keep a 4th-string depth quarterback. Running Back: Rookie running back Seth McGowan ran with the first-team offense, and once again, had a handful of nice carries , rushing for 20 total rushing yards on 4 carries. He appears to have overtaken DJ Giddens, who’s been limited with a hamstring injury, for the RB2 job behind star workhorse Jonathan Taylor. While Giddens rushed for a 6-yard touchdown late in the second quarter , he also once again showed his continued struggles in pass protection, completely whiffing on a block —which directly led to Leonard’s interception denoted above. Giddens has probably shown enough talent as a rusher to stick as the Colts’ RB3 for now though, but will need to improve as a pass blocker to see the football field more. Wide Receiver: Veteran Keenan Allen had his first reception as a Colt, which was a 24-yard reception from Richardson Sr. early in this one. Rookie 7th round pick Deion Burks continued to play well in preseason , and the Colts appear to have a tough decision in their wide receiver room lower on the depth chart. Among those competing, Coleman Owen, who adds special teams return ability, had a 12-yard reception before being forced to leave to the Colts blue medical tent after sustaining a big hit. The group of Alec Pierce, Josh Downs, Keenan Allen, Ashton Dulin, and maybe Laquon Treadwell appear to be all locks, but beyond them, is anybody’s guess. Nick Westbrook-Ikhine may be redundant with Allen’s signing, while Burks offers more long-term upside as a wide receiver, but doesn’t offer the same special teams value and versatility as either Anthony Gould or Coleman Owen, which could be the bottom line difference. Offensive Line: The backup Dalton Tucker transition to center was an interesting experiment, but has run its course, as Indianapolis has to find a 2nd-string center consistently capable of snapping a ball to the quarterback in shotgun, which once again was an issue for the former with several errant shotgun snaps —which has been a re-occurring theme throughout training camp and preseason. DEFENSE : Edge: Rookie George Gumbs Jr. once again flashed as a rotational edge , while 2nd-string edge Jaylahn Tuimoloau continues to be ‘just a guy’ out there at edge, but made his biggest impact on special teams . Fellow rookie Caden Curry had a nice pass pressure , and like Tuimoloatu, also made his mark on special teams in this one with a fumble recovery on a kick return (*which kudos to Bryce Boettcher on the punchout). To me, Curry is the ideal lower on the depth chart backup edge, with his energy, hustle, and special teams versatility, and it would be very surprising to me if he doesn’t stick on the Colts final 53-man roster. Linebacker: Rookie linebacker CJ Allen, who’s currently listed as the first-team starter on defense alongside fellow linebacker, veteran Akeem Davis-Gaither, was very underwhelming in this one. He struggled to get off blocks and was nonexistent in the run defense game. It may be a fair question of whether the Colts will continue to go with Allen as the starter, who still has some work to do. Speaking of Boettcher, he finished with 6 tackles. Cornerback: The Colts cornerback depth is suspect outside their ‘Big 3’ of Sauce Gardner, Charvarius Ward, and Justin Walley. Ron Carter Jr. was the latest Colts backup cornerback to get picked on in preseason. Cam Taylor-Britt probably sticks, who had a nice run stop , but it wouldn’t be surprising if the Colts are very active at this position on the waiver wire, and completely revamp their backup cornerbacks 5-6. Safety: 2nd-year safety Hunter Wohler got a lot of run in this one , but should be a lock to make the final 53-man roster. He’s a good versatile backup football player, who can help the squad in a number of ways on both defense and special teams. Rookie AJ Haulcy should be the starting safety, but Wohler will contribute out there. SPECIAL TEAMS: Kicker: It appears as though Spencer Shrader has won this competition outright through his preseason play, as he knocked down a 60-yard field goal, while fellow contender Blake Grupe doinked in a 46-yard field goal and also converted a 36-yard field goal attempt. The scripts have been flipped in training camp and preseason, as Shrader, who largely struggled in camp, has really come on with the preseason lights on for the Colts.
author: Luke Schultheis

title: What to Watch For: Colts host Lions for Preseason Finale
summary: The Indianapolis Colts (0-1-1)(-2.5) host the Detroit Lions (1-1)(+2.5) for the two teams’ preseason finale, which will kickoff shortly at 1 PM EST in the friendly confines of Lucas Oil Stadium. For those attending and otherwise viewing for potential shadows on the field, the roof will be closed today. Colts fans can watch the game […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - AUGUST 22: Anthony Richardson Sr. #5 of the Indianapolis Colts warms up prior to a preseason game against the Atlanta Falcons at Lucas Oil Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Chris Carter/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts (0-1-1)(-2.5) host the Detroit Lions (1-1)(+2.5) for the two teams’ preseason finale, which will kickoff shortly at 1 PM EST in the friendly confines of Lucas Oil Stadium. For those attending and otherwise viewing for potential shadows on the field, the roof will be closed today . Colts fans can watch the game on CBs4 (with Greg Rakestraw handling the play-by-play and retired longtime NFL coach Rick Venturi as the analyst) and NFL Network (Jason Benetti on play-by-play and T.J. Lang as the analyst respectively). For those looking to tune in, you can listen in on 93.5 & 107.5 The Fan or 97.1 Hank FM. Regarding the Colts, the plan is to play their starters for this final dress rehearsal ahead of the regular season for around two series—although offensively for Indianapolis, neither starting quarterback Daniel Jones nor running back Jonathan Taylor will be suiting up in this one, and rightfully so. Steichen also indicated earlier this week that a pair of grizzled veterans, wide receiver Keenan Allen and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner will both play at least a few plays in the upcoming preseason finale. Backup quarterback Anthony Richardson will draw the start again for Indianapolis, having started in the preseason opener. Richardson will take the first quarter, with fellow backup Riley Leonard coming in relief earlier this go around during the second quarter. As it stands, Richardson appears to be in the driver’s seat for the primary backup quarterback job behind Jones, but a poor performance this afternoon (or even a trade) could elevate Leonard a rung in the pecking order again. Like the Colts, the Lions are expected to play their starters sparingly, which means Indianapolis should see a lot of quarterbacks Josh Dobbs and Luke Altmyer, who are battling for the primary backup job behind Jared Goff. For the Colts, these are the competitions I’ll be watching for: Backup Quarterback : The QB2 job behind Jones appears to be Richardson’s to lose right now, but as mentioned, a lackluster showing in this one, coupled with Leonard playing well in relief of him, could potentially make this an open-ended question again. Placekickers : Blake Grupe has been rock solid throughout training camp compared to Spencer Shrader, who largely struggled, but it’s been Grupe who’s had the uncharacteristic misses through two preseason games, while the latter has really shined—including at least a few converted kicks from long distance. It would seem to me that it would matter more who performs when the game lights and pressure come on, and granted, it’s only preseason, but it’s closer to a simulated game than training camp. Backup Running Back : DJ Giddens has been limited during training camp with a lingering hamstring injury, but is still limited as the primary backup to Taylor. Meanwhile, rookie Seth McGowan has stood out throughout training camp and preseason, and with Taylor not playing in this one, who will make the stronger RB2 case behind him? Rookie linebacker CJ Allen : Despite being limited with his own injuries, Allen is still listed as the first-team defense starter on the last preseason depth chart alongside veteran Akeem Davis-Gaither. Linebacker Jaylon Carlies has surprisingly played well this training camp and preseason, so if Allen struggles, maybe this could be another positional question for the Colts going forward. Fellow rookie Bryce Boettcher is currently listed with the 3rd-team, but he’s played really well when called upon with his instincts and quickness, and I’d be surprised if he doesn’t ascend the depth chart eventually through the regular season. Rotational Edge : Former 2025 2nd round pick Jaylahn Tuimoloau has yet to flash throughout training camp and preseason, and while he’s been going up against the superior backup 2 offensive linemen, both rookies George Gumbs Jr. and Caden Curry have stood out more in preseason than he has to-date—albeit against inferior o-line competition (which is something to consider). Eventually Tuimoloau needs to show out, or he may get passed up in the Colts defensive edge rotation, sooner rather than later.
author: Luke Schultheis

title: Preseason Week 3 Colts vs. Lions Game Thread
summary: The Indianapolis Colts are at home to take on the Detroit Lions in week 3 of the 2026 preseason, kickoff is at 1:00 p.m. EST. In the last preseason contest of 2026 there is a lot to look forward to. Shane Steichen announced earlier in the week that the starters will play the first 8-10 plays. So […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 13: Bryce Boettcher #50 of the Indianapolis Colts lines up during an NFL preseason football game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts are at home to take on the Detroit Lions in week 3 of the 2026 preseason, kickoff is at 1:00 p.m. EST. In the last preseason contest of 2026 there is a lot to look forward to. Shane Steichen announced earlier in the week that the starters will play the first 8-10 plays. So we’ll get to see the likes of Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner, Grover Stewart and the rest of the fellas get out there and play ball, at least for a little bit. Next, there are always the rookies. CJ Allen was fine against the Atlanta Falcons a week ago. Everyone, myself included, was hoping for multiple splash plays from the rookie linebacker but we didn’t get them. And that’s okay. It means absolutely nothing. If it’s week 10 of the regular season and we’ve yet to see a positive highlight reel worthy play, well, then it’s time to worry. As of now, Allen is likely still trying to get up to speed with the defense after missing time with injury. I’m willing to be patient with the second rounder, but I’m still hoping to see something exciting today. AJ Halucy didn’t suit up in week 2 but I currently have him penciled in as the Colts starting safety opposite Cam Bynum. With that said, Halucy once again won’t suit up this week. This is a disappointment but in the grand scheme of things, not playing in a meaningless preseason game, it’s a big deal at all. In week one Caden Curry was all over the field against the Patriots. Last week he was more subdued, as were the rest of his Indy teammates. Today, Curry should get ample opportunity to show that week one wasn’t a fluke and that the Greenwood native belongs on the roster. Bryce Boettcher’s week one preseason performance was an interception or forced fumble away from being legendary. That said, he was one of few Colts players that flashed in week two as well. When Indy drafted Boettcher, I’ll admit, I wasn’t completely sold. I was excited to see what he could do in coverage but I wasn’t that hopeful for his abilities in the ground game. And so far, I’ve been wrong. Through two preseason games Boettcher has looked like a missile flying at opposing running backs and as long as he doesn’t hurt himself in the process, I’m all for it. With the regular season fast upon us, I do expect to see Boettcher make a fair number of mistakes as rookies who play as fast as he does, tend to do. But as long as he’s making those mistakes at full speed, I’ll be happy. Another surprise so far has been George Gumbs Jr.. Showing far more as a pass rusher than anyone could have expected him to this early in his carrier. Curry is getting the hype as a guy with more production and local appeal, but don’t sleep on Gumbs. Like Curry, he’s shown far more than you expect from a guy with his draft pedigree. The offensive line got more help in this draft via Jalen Farmer. Farmer has shown flashes thus far of being a very good all around guard with the potential to be an absolute road grader on the right side. I was hoping to get another look at the massive man from UK, but news has broken that Farmer will sit this one out. If the preseason is any indication, Seth McGowan, is a good running back. He’ll probably never develop into a guy that touches the ball 15-20 times a game for you with any consistency over a long period of time. But McGowan has shown everything you hope for from a RB2. Which is good because after RB2 the Colts depth chart starts to look a little bleak. Fellow seventh rounder Deion Burks is in a battle for a roster spot. He has shown some good things so far but he will need to show more on special teams in order to find his way on to the roster. I like Burks a lot as a player and usually when I like a guy this much during camp and preseason, I am disappointed come roster cutdown day. Hopefully Burks bucks that trend, time will tell. The QB2 battle appears to be over. Riley Leonard played the entire first half against the Falcons and I think we can all agree, we’ve seen enough of that. Every interview I see with the guy, I like Leonard a lot. Seems like a good kid and I appreciate his athleticism with the ball in his hands when he has an opportunity to pull the ball down and run. But he had a golden opportunity to play well and really push Anthony Richardson for the QB2 role a week ago and he failed to do so. Richardson on the other hand continued to play well. It wasn’t as good as his week one performance but the (somehow, still) young QB made as many plays as can be expected when your opponents fourth and fifth string players appear to be that much better than your own. The Colts entire roster seemed to be vastly outmatched a week ago (zero concerns here, it’s the preseason folks) and Richardson did all he could to keep the ship sailing straight. On one play he managed to break a sack, avoid a tackler and push two defenders forward to pick up a first down. It’s not going to make any highlight reels but it was the kind of play that (if consistently made) will keep your team afloat if the starter has to miss time. Today we’ll also get our first look at Keenen Allen in a Colts uniform. So that’s fun. Josh Downs, Tyler Warren, Mooney Ward and Alec Pierce are among those that will not play today. We are two weeks away from regular season football and today many young men will likely play their last snap of competitive football. So I’ll try to enjoy the last three quarters of today’s game for what it will be: a beautiful mess. Prediction: Lions: 23 Colts: 23 As always, go Colts. RELATED What To Watch For with Luke Schultheis This is your preseason week three open thread so hang out here, chat, celebrate, commiserate, and argue in the comments! Go wild (within reason)! Go Colts!
author: Chris Shepherd

title: One of the Colts’ hottest battles has nothing to do with the quarterbacks
summary: Spencer Shrader was becoming a bit of a hero for the Indianapolis Colts. It didn’t take long either. After a penalty gave the Colts new life against the Broncos, Shrader kicked the game winner as time expired. That moved the Colts to an unexpected 2-0 and let the good times roll. Those good times came […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - AUGUST 22: Spencer Shrader #3 of the Indianapolis Colts kicks a field goal during a preseason game against the Atlanta Falcons at Lucas Oil Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Chris Carter/Getty Images) | Getty Images Spencer Shrader was becoming a bit of a hero for the Indianapolis Colts. It didn’t take long either. After a penalty gave the Colts new life against the Broncos, Shrader kicked the game winner as time expired. That moved the Colts to an unexpected 2-0 and let the good times roll. Those good times came to a screeching halt, however, when a Las Vegas Raider ran into his knee and knocked him out for the rest of the year. Unfortunately, that’s how sports goes, and it has led to one of the more intriguing battles in camp. Michael Badgley was actually the second choice for the Colts, but his inability to hit extra points nearly cost the Colts wins and ultimately his job. Eyes turned to Blake Grupe. He didn’t disappoint. He was so good that he was actually perfect: 10-10 on field goals and nailing all 11 extra points. He even set the franchise record for longest made field goal. Grupe has carried that success into the offseason and appears to have the edge. So, how is there a battle? The Colts have a kicker, in-house, that was perfect last year and has been solid in camp. Practice is great, but when it comes to game-day kicks, Shrader has shone. His biggest knock was leg strength. That kick against Denver, yeah, it had to be re-kicked because his first attempt fell short. In two preseason games, though, Shrader has hit from 53 and 61 yards out, going a perfect 4-4. Meanwhile, Grupe has been the opposite of perfect, missing from beyond 60 and botching a 36-yarder. That can’t happen. Sports is all about doors. Doors shut. Doors open. When Spencer Shrader went down Week 5, it created an opportunity for Blake Grupe to eventually take over. Now that Grupe has struggled in game action, that same door Shrader opened is now allowing him back in. Grupe still appears to have the edge, but this is definitely a battle to watch as the preseason continues.
author: Jon Spradley

title: Breaking Down The Jaguars Trade for Dolphins QB Quinn Ewers
summary: With the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline approaching on Sunday at 6 pm, the Jacksonville Jaguars have made a move to add depth at quarterback. On Saturday afternoon, the team announced a trade for Miami Dolphins backup signal-caller Quinn Ewers, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo. Compensation The cost for the acquisition with […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - AUGUST 14: Quinn Ewers #14 of the Miami Dolphins looks to pass as Tyler Owens #18 of the Washington Commanders applies pressure during the first half of a preseason game at Northwest Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline approaching on Sunday at 6 pm, the Jacksonville Jaguars have made a move to add depth at quarterback. On Saturday afternoon, the team announced a trade for Miami Dolphins backup signal-caller Quinn Ewers, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo . Compensation The cost for the acquisition with the Dolphins will be a 2028 sixth-round draft pick, per the team. They add a low-risk backup option who showed enough in three late-season starts to earn real consideration, for the cost of a 2028 sixth-round pick that will barely register on the draft capital ledger. We have acquired QB Quinn Ewers from the Miami Dolphins in exchange for a sixth-round selection in the 2028 NFL Draft, pending a physical.⁰⁰ @Shift4 | #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/z58qeitP2D — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) August 29, 2026 Most importantly, avoiding giving away draft capital in the highly valued 2027 draft was a win for Jaguars general manager James Gladstone, in my book. The move comes at a natural crossroads for both franchises. Miami, now building around Malik Willis following what was described as the most expensive cut in NFL history in releasing Tua Tagovailoa, had their backup quarterback situation complicated by Ewers’ rough preseason showing and the groin injury that followed. For Jacksonville, the addition raises immediate questions about Nick Mullens’ standing in the quarterback room heading into the season. Who Is Quinn Ewers? Ewers, 23, arrived in the NFL as one of the most polarizing draft stories in recent memory. The 6-foot-2, 209-pound quarterback spent one season at Ohio State before transferring to Texas, where he became the face of a program resurgence that produced three seasons, a 33-10 record, two consecutive trips to the College Football Playoff national semifinals, 9,128 passing yards, and 68 touchdowns, per the Houston Chronicle. He earned second-team All-Big 12 honors in 2023 and second-team All-SEC recognition in 2024, per Pro Football Reference. Despite that resume, Ewers was not selected until the seventh round of the 2025 NFL Draft, the 231st overall pick, and final quarterback taken in the draft. He currently has three years remaining on his four-year rookie contract (worth $4.33 million). The draft slide was widely attributed to questions about his arm strength, footwork consistency, and pocket movement against elite competition late in his college career. 2025 Rookie Season Ewers made the Dolphins’ initial 53-man roster as a rookie, serving behind Tua Tagovailoa and Zach Wilson. He appeared in four games and made three starts, finishing the season with the following line: Completions/Attempts: 55-of-83 Completion Percentage: 66.3% Passing Yards: 622 Touchdowns: 3 Interceptions: 3 Passer Rating: 85.5 His three starts came at the end of the 2025 regular season filling in for Tagovailoa, and handled those opportunities well, showing the decision-making and downfield accuracy that had made him such a highly regarded prospect coming out of Texas. He ended 2025 going 1-2 as a starter, highlighted by a 20-17 victory over Tampa Bay where he went 14 of 22 for 172 yards, with two touchdowns and zero turnovers. A Difficult 2026 Ewers entered the 2026 offseason with every reason for optimism. He performed well during OTAs and minicamp, drawing positive reviews from the Miami coaching staff and building on the foundation of his late-season 2025 starts. With Miami bringing in Malik Willis to lead the offense the prevailing thought was that Ewers could compete for the backup role or potentially be a dark horse candidate in the race for the starting role. The preseason, however, did not go as planned . In his Week 1 appearance against the Washington Commanders, Ewers completed just one of eight pass attempts for 27 yards, and threw an interception. Quan Martin gets the interception from Quinn Ewers. pic.twitter.com/P5IU9d5vGP — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) August 14, 2026 That performance prompted multiple Dolphins analysts to publicly note that a cut was a real possibility. The groin injury that followed effectively sealed his fate in Miami. With Ewers sidelined and unable to appear in the team’s second preseason game, Malik Willis moved decisively into the starting role, and Cam Miller stepped in to handle the third preseason game responsibilities with Willis resting. By the time roster cutdowns arrived, Ewers had become expendable in a Miami quarterback room that no longer needed him. Argument For Upside The argument exists that Ewers has more promise in a new offense than seen from Mullens, Carter Bradley, and Joey Aguilar, however. Despite his 2026 offseason inconsistency, context often matters. Playing behind a bad backup Dolphins offensive line, with an extremely shallow receiving room, for a staff who didn’t draft you is generally not a recipe for quarterback success. There’s a possible upside play in effect with Ewers, where Jacksonville could, theoretically, tap into some previously untapped potential, with a better supporting cast and system. The combination of Josh Cameron, CJ Williams, Nate Boerkircher, and Tanner Koziol, with Liam Coen is arguably a better group of pass catchers than the core of depth pass catchers working in Miami. With new Dolphins new general manager, Jon-Eric Sullivan, head coach, Jeff Hafley, and offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik all hired in 2026, the argument that this offense being a scenario of right quarterback, wrong scheme also could exist. Jacksonville’s bet on traits makes some sense there, for such a low cost for a former second team All SEC quarterback. What This Means for the Jaguars The most immediate question the trade raises is what it signals for Nick Mullens. Jacksonville’s veteran backup had a reasonably strong preseason, most notably in the team’s Week 2 preseason outing against the Carolina Panthers, where he opened the game completing six of his first seven attempts for 65 yards at a 9.3 yards-per-reception clip. He then wrapped up week three going five of seven for 62 yards. However, Mullen’s practice performances were less consistent than the game day box scores indicate, with multiple days of the second team offense struggling to move the ball, which somewhat muddles the evaluation. Whether Mullens retains the No. 2 spot, slides to No. 3 behind Ewers, or finds himself a surprise casualty of the trade is a question the Jaguars will answer when they finalize their 53-man roster over the next day. What is clear is that Jacksonville now has a 23-year-old developmental quarterback with legitimate upside, and multiple years to grow into the system. What’s Next? The Jaguars will have two weeks to begin the acclimation period for Ewers, giving them plenty of time to work on the new quarterback, and get him up to speed before the season begins. The NFL’s 53-man roster cutdown deadline is Sunday and the Jaguars open the 2026 regular season at home against the Cleveland Browns on September 13th.
author: Travis Holmes

title: Jacksonville Jaguars Winners And Losers From Preseason Week 3: Jags Close Strong Behind Rookie Depth
summary: Now that’s how you play three phases of preseason football. The Jacksonville Jaguars took down the visiting Tamp Bay Buccaneers, 19-0, Friday behind three phases of solid play. The Jags got some representative offense, a special teams touchdown and 61-yard field goal as well as a turnover on defense. It was a complete departure from […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 28: Michael Wortham #0 of the Jacksonville Jaguars returns a punt for a touchdown as Cam'ron Silmon-Craig #42 blocks against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during a preseason game at EverBank Field on August 28, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Now that’s how you play three phases of preseason football. The Jacksonville Jaguars took down the visiting Tamp Bay Buccaneers, 19-0, Friday behind three phases of solid play . The Jags got some representative offense, a special teams touchdown and 61-yard field goal as well as a turnover on defense. It was a complete departure from the mess that was the Carolina game. Are the Jaguars now primed to win the Super Bowl because Wesley Williams and Michael Wortham played well? Who’s to say, but at the very least that was a solid way to send this team into the 53-man roster phase ahead of the Week 1 tilt against the Cleveland Browns. WINNERS Defensive Ends Have a freaking day Bryan Thomas Jr. and Wesley Williams. Friday night was a feast for two rookie defensive ends in Thomas Jr. (not the wide receiver!) and Williams. The former had 2.5 sacks and two tackles for loss while Williams had two tackles and a fumble recovery. Thomas Jr. BRYAN Thomas Jr. 🍸 #TBvsJAX on FOX30 https://t.co/lv4FJk7wo1 pic.twitter.com/9znNgxJ1UO — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) August 29, 2026 It was probably always going to be the case that Williams, a fourth round pick out of Duke, was going to make the roster. Not so much for Thomas Jr., but he made a tremendous effort in his final dress rehearsal as to why he should make the 53-man team. While the Jags may have issues on the backup offensive line front, Tampa Bay certainly does as well and the Jags feasted in the backfield to the tune of five total sacks. A special shoutout also goes to second-year Auburn man Jalen McLeod who somewhat quietly led the team with seven tackles and one tackle for loss. All three of these guys put great tape out there in the final preseason game and by all counts should continue to rock a Jags jersey. Jalen McLeod TFL in coverage #noticing — John Shipley (@_John_Shipley) August 28, 2026 Michael Wortham Speaking of having a day, Wortham really decided he wanted to make the roster too. The rookie out of Montana went out and collected 170 total all-purpose yards including a 63-yard punt return touchdown. He finished tied for first on the team in receiving with three catches for 47 yards. An emerging question mark from preseason was who could possibly be the Jags number two return man behind Parker Washington? Well, Wortham made an incredibly strong case for it being him moving forward and I don’t think any Jags fan would complain after seeing that dude cross the length of the field and turn on the afterburners. It’s CJ Williams’ or Josh Cameron’s backup WR spot to lose, but hey good for Wortham for making people in the front office at leas think about it. Credit where it’s due, the special teams unit blocked the hell out of that punt return and had multiple bodies up to see Wortham to the end zone. That’s what you like to see from the backups. Blessed I can’t thank god enough🖤 https://t.co/gES7h9YvIn — ⚡️Michael wortham🏅💎 (@Moneymike61) August 29, 2026 Hunter Long Someone maybe not on the roster bubble but could always use a good showing was Hunter Long. And prior to injury, he looked like a man among boys out there. Long tied Wortham in yardage with two catches for 47 yards, taking the first offensive possession for the Jags for 34 yards. Long was rumbling and stumbling when he had the ball in his hands, putting up a good showing for why he should be kept around. After drafting two tight ends in April, Long might be on the outside looking in by default, but he made his case. At the very least, he seems like for the practice squad and for a call-up if a guy goes down. We know he can play and will play hard as hell. He certainly cannot hurt this team by keeping him in Duval. Carter Bradley Closing Strong For all the shit Bradley has gotten, and much of it deserved, hats off to the dude for closing the preseason in the best way possible. Most of Friday night saw Bradley getting killed by his offensive front, mouthing to himself that he wasn’t getting helped and footballs bouncing helplessly out of the reach of receivers who need the catches to make a living. That was until the third quarter. Bradley and the gang mounted a 14 play (!!) 74-yard touchdown drive that saw Bradley float a pass to DeeJay Dallas for six. For good measure, Bradley ran hard for a two-point conversion that had to just feel euphoric for the dude after all he had been through the past two games and change. This won’t change his fate in the NFL, but the rookie closed strong. He even played hurt as evidenced by his hand being wrapped up on the sideline after his scoring drive. I have given Bradley plenty of grief, but I have to give him his flowers for grinding that score out. Coach calls the @Jaguars TD 🙌 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YcSDgTx4sq — NFL (@NFL) August 29, 2026 Special Teams Cam Little and Logan Cooke are good. Thank you for your attention to this matter. Cam Little making a 61-yard FG look easy 😮‍💨 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/EzUJqzox6r — NFL (@NFL) August 29, 2026 LOSERS Backup Offensive Line Hey so this might be an issue, yeah? I’m not so certain much of anyone flashed as great backup offensive line options through the length of the preseason outside of rookie Emmanuel Pregnon. The team is getting Cole Van Lanen back which is cause for celebration, but questions still linger about Chuma Edoga and his status which could cause him to miss the roster altogether. This isn’t an inspired group and the backups didn’t impress against Tampa Bay, helping give way to four sacks and a moribund 2.8 yards per rush. Backup Quarterback Nick Mullens, you’re the backup quarterback. Congrats. Buy the Rivalry Jersey now. Trevor Lawrence needs to stay healthy and this is all for naught, but if there is another nitpick area of concern for the Jags you can make the case that it’s the QB2 position. It likely (hopefully) doesn’t matter in the long run but Mullens didn’t exactly flash on TV. His camp reports were fine so hopefully if he’s ever needed facing live game action, he turns to that version of himself. This franchise goes by the way of Lawrence anyway so if Mullens, or really anybody else, is in it’s probably over regardless.

title: Three Reasons the Jaguars Beat the Buccaneers
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars closed out the preseason with a 19-0 shutout of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Friday night, and while preseason results need to be treated with the appropriate amount of caution, this was more than simply a scoreline. With neither team using its starters, the game was effectively a final audition for players […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 28: Michael Wortham #0 of the Jacksonville Jaguars returns a punt for a touchdown during their preseason matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at EverBank Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars closed out the preseason with a 19-0 shutout of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Friday night, and while preseason results need to be treated with the appropriate amount of caution, this was more than simply a scoreline. With neither team using its starters, the game was effectively a final audition for players fighting for roster spots, and Jacksonville’s depth came out on top in emphatic fashion. Here are three reasons the Jaguars dominated the Buccaneers at EverBank Stadium. Defense: Bryan Thomas Jr. led a relentless pass rush Thomas Jr. BRYAN Thomas Jr. 🍸 #TBvsJAX on FOX30 https://t.co/lv4FJk7wo1 pic.twitter.com/9znNgxJ1UO — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) August 29, 2026 The Jaguars’ defense set the tone from the opening snap, and undrafted rookie Bryan Thomas Jr. was at the heart of it. Thomas finished with 2.5 sacks, four quarterback hits and four tackles, repeatedly finding his way into the Tampa Bay backfield as the Buccaneers struggled to protect their quarterbacks. Jacksonville finished with five sacks overall and held Tampa Bay to just 87 total yards, six first downs and a miserable 2-for-12 on third down. Thomas’ performance was particularly significant because of what was at stake. An undrafted rookie does not get many better opportunities to force his way onto an NFL roster than the final preseason game, and Thomas took his chance. He showed the explosive pass-rushing ability that had made him intriguing during camp, but also held up against the run and consistently created problems for Tampa Bay’s quarterbacks. Liam Coen certainly noticed. The Jaguars head coach said Thomas has a “gift of rushing the passer” that cannot be ignored, adding that the rookie’s play was making the roster decision increasingly difficult. With Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker ahead of him, Jacksonville does not need Thomas to carry its pass rush immediately. But Friday night provided a pretty compelling argument that the Jaguars have another young edge rusher worth keeping around. Offense: Jacksonville’s reserves did enough to control the game Carter Bradley throws it to Hunter Long for six! Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/lBgMXfB3Fe — NFL (@NFL) August 15, 2026 The Jaguars’ offense was hardly flawless. They failed to convert a third down in the first half and had some frustrating stretches, while Carter Bradley missed a couple of opportunities on deep passes. But compared with Tampa Bay, Jacksonville’s quarterbacks were considerably more effective, and the offense consistently did enough to keep the pressure on the Buccaneers. Nick Mullens got the game started with an efficient 5-of-7 passing performance for 62 yards in the first quarter, including a 34-yard completion to tight end Hunter Long and a key fourth-down conversion. Bradley then took over and finished 8-of-15 for 77 yards and a touchdown, adding a rushing two-point conversion as Jacksonville gradually pulled away. The Jaguars finished with 249 total yards and held the ball for almost 35 minutes, compared with just 87 yards and 25:05 of possession for Tampa Bay. That disparity is perhaps the most important takeaway from a preseason game like this. Neither team was relying on its starters, so the question was less about which roster has the better top end and more about which team had the better players further down the depth chart. Jacksonville’s reserves moved the ball, protected it and sustained drives. Tampa Bay’s offense repeatedly went three-and-out and struggled to generate anything resembling momentum. Special Teams: Michael Wortham provided the knockout blow Michael Wortham takes this 63-yard punt return TO THE HOUSE 🏠 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wkUjxEOIcp — NFL (@NFL) August 29, 2026 If Thomas was the defensive star, Michael Wortham was the player who made sure everybody remembered his name. The rookie wide receiver had already shown flashes on offense, catching three passes for 47 yards, but his biggest contribution came on special teams. Wortham returned five punts for 123 yards, an outstanding 24.6-yard average, and his 63-yard touchdown return late in the fourth quarter turned Jacksonville’s comfortable 11-0 lead into a 19-0 rout. It was exactly the kind of performance a player on the roster bubble needs. Wortham showed he can contribute as a receiver, then demonstrated the explosiveness and open-field ability that could give him another route onto the roster. Coen had already seen enough during the preseason to believe there was something worth developing, and Friday night made the decision considerably harder. More importantly, Wortham’s touchdown was representative of the entire game. Jacksonville’s young players kept making plays. Tampa Bay’s young players kept struggling to respond. By the time Wortham sprinted 63 yards down the sideline, the Jaguars had turned what could have been a scrappy preseason contest into a convincing statement from the bottom half of their roster. For Jacksonville, that is probably the most encouraging part of the night. The starters did not need to rescue them. The players fighting for their NFL futures did the job themselves.

title: Chiefs final cutdown tracker: Reports and rumors ahead of Sunday’s deadline
summary: By 5:00 p.m. (Arrowhead Time) on Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs must reduce their 90-man active roster by 38 players in order to get it down to the in-season limit of 53 players. The team will eventually release a complete list of all of its moves — but until then, news about some of them […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 25: Wesley Bissainthe #59 participates during Kansas City Chiefs Training Camp at Missouri Western State University on July 25, 2026 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images By 5:00 p.m. (Arrowhead Time) on Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs must reduce their 90-man active roster by 38 players in order to get it down to the in-season limit of 53 players. T he team will eventually release a complete list of all of its moves — but until then, news about some of them will trickle out. Here, we’ll track all the roster moves Kansas City is reported to have made. With each new report, we’re also updating our Chiefs roster page , so you can easily see how many players are left in each position group. We’re awaiting the 53-man roster that will attempt to bring the Chiefs back to the postseason. Currently, Kansas City has (-176) odds to make the playoffs, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Reported Chiefs roster moves Saturday, August 29 Cornerback Zelmar Vedder was waived, according to Houston reporter Aaron Wilson . The Chiefs struck a deal with the Baltimore Ravens to acquire rookie left tackle Diego Pounds . Linebacker Wesley Bissainthe was waived, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter . How roster changes are made When players with fewer than four accrued seasons are cut, they have been waived . (Players acquire an accrued season when they are on a team’s active roster, its Reserve/Injured list, or its Reserve/PUP list for at least six games in a given season). When players with at least four accrued seasons are cut, they have been released . They immediately become free agents. Waived players may be claimed by another team, which then assumes the balance of their contract. The team that had the most recent draft’s first pick has precedence over waiver claims from all other teams. The team with the most recent draft’s 32nd pick has precedence over waiver claims from no other teams — and so on. If a waived player isn’t claimed by noon on Monday, they become free agents. Players can also be waived with an injury designation — commonly referred to as waived/injured . If these players go unclaimed, they automatically revert to the team’s Reserve/Injured list. This has already happened with prior cuts of tackle Matt Waletzko and wide receiver Jeff Caldwell. That is one of three Reserve lists that do not count against the 53-man limit. The other two are the Reserve/PUP (physically-unable-to-perform) and Reserve/NFI (non-football-injury) lists. Players on the latter two lists at the final cutdown must miss at least four regular-season games before being activated to the roster, which occurs when they pass a physical. Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott — who missed all of training camp recovering from a torn ACL from 2025 — is the only player eligible for the Reserve/PUP list. The salaries for players on a team’s Reserve/PUP and Reserve/Injured lists count against the salary cap. Outside of first- and second-round picks, most players without veteran status can see their base salary cut in half while on reserve lists at the discretion of the team. Salaries for players on Reserve/NFI are not paid (unless a contract provision specifies otherwise). Players placed on Reserve/Injured in the offseason (up through the final cutdown day) must miss the whole season. If a player is placed on Reserve/Injured after the final cutdown day, they may be designated for return after they have missed at least four games. But on final cutdown day, a team may declare up to two players being placed on its Reserve/Injured list as being eligible to be treated as if they are placed on Reserve/Injured after the final cutdown. Teams may make only eight designations for return during a given season — a limit that is extended to 10 if the team appears in the postseason. If a team labels a player as eligible for return at the final cutdown, it counts against this limit — even if the player is never actually designated for return. Players designated for return from Reserve/Injured are eligible to practice with the team for up to 21 days. At any time during that period, they may be activated to the roster. If they are not, they must remain on the Reserve list for the remainder of the season. Finally… players may be removed from the roster by being traded to another team. Just like with a waiver claim, the player’s new team assumes their existing contract, which counts against their cap. But any money that has already been paid to the traded (or waived) player (such as signing and workout bonuses) must be carried against the original team’s cap. Roster change s ummary Current roster size: 89 (not including one exempt player) Released: None Waived: LB Wesley Bissainthe, CB Zelmar Vedder Waived/injured: None Traded: None Free agents signed: None Acquired through trade: OT Diego Pounds Placed on Reserve/Injured: None Placed on Reserve/NFI: None

title: Chiefs are reportedly trading for a left tackle from the Ravens
summary: As the Kansas City Chiefs work through cutting down the offseason roster to 53 players by Sunday’s deadline, general manager Brett Veach is active on the trade market. Earlier this week, he made a deal for an offensive lineman from the New York Giants. On Saturday evening, he reportedly made another deal. According to Mike […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - AUGUST 15: Diego Pounds #61 of the Baltimore Ravens prepares to block during an NFL preseason football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at M&T Bank Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images As the Kansas City Chiefs work through cutting down the offseason roster to 53 players by Sunday’s deadline, general manager Brett Veach is active on the trade market. Earlier this week, he made a deal for an offensive lineman from the New York Giants . On Saturday evening, he reportedly made another deal. Adding Pounds: The #Ravens are trading OT Diego Pounds to the #Chiefs , sources tell me and @MikeGarafolo . The undrafted free agent from Ole Miss lands in KC. pic.twitter.com/jlIxXx6K8U — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) August 29, 2026 According to Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport of NFL Network , the Chiefs struck a trade with the Baltimore Ravens to acquire rookie offensive tackle Diego Pounds. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the trade compensation “is contingent on the picks that Kansas City has available at the end of the season; it could result in either a Day 3 2027 pick or a Day 3 2028 pick.” Pounds was an undrafted free agent from Ole Miss who signed with Baltimore following the 2026 NFL Draft. At the NFL Scouting Combine in March, Pounds measured 6 feet 6 inches tall and 325 pounds. His arm length measured 33 3/4 inches, and his hands measured 9 3/4 inches. Over four seasons in college, finishing with two years at Ole Miss after starting at North Carolina, Pounds was nearly exclusively a left tackle. Pounds played just one snap at left guard compared to 2,561 snaps at left tackle in college. This preseason, Pounds has lined up 58 times at left tackle for the Ravens. Over 26 pass-blocking snaps, Pounds has allowed no pressure over three preseason games, according to Pro Football Focus. Pounds’ experience at left tackle begs the question: what does this mean for starting left tackle Josh Simmons (Back)? Per Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated , there is some concern about Simmons’ availability , but the trade for Pounds is not directly related to the starter’s health. The Ravens are trading OT Diego Pounds to the Chiefs for a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick (could end up being a seventh, KC doesn't have one right now). KC's been looking to improve its OL depth. This, to be clear, isn't about Josh Simmons, though there is concern there.… — Albert Breer (@AlbertBreer) August 29, 2026 Two situations regarding Simmons will be important to monitor. The first will be on Sunday, when the Chiefs must trim the roster to 53 players. On cutdown day, the Chiefs can designate up to two players to be placed on the Reserve/Injured list and eligible to return during the season. Any designations made Sunday will count toward the eight allowable players to return from the list during the season. Starting Monday, any player placed on the reserve list can be designated to return at any point after Week 4 of the regular season. Assuming Simmons makes it through early next week on the active roster, the Chiefs will issue their first injury report for Week 1’s “Monday Night Football” matchup against the Denver Broncos on Thursday, September 10.

title: 5 things we learned from the Chiefs’ final preseason game of the season
summary: Last week I wrote that the Kansas City Chiefs almost won the franchise’s first preseason game since 2023. Well, this week, the team still didn’t win this one, but the losing streak is over! Friday night’s game was the “rookie quarterback Garrett Nussmeier” show. And aside from one very bad interception, I thought he managed […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Defensive end R. Mason Thomas #51 of the Kansas City Chiefs rushes to the quarterback in the second quarter during an NFL preseason game against the Los Angeles Rams at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week I wrote that the Kansas City Chiefs almost won the franchise’s first preseason game since 2023. Well, this week, the team still didn’t win this one, but the losing streak is over! Friday night’s game was the “rookie quarterback Garrett Nussmeier” show. And aside from one very bad interception, I thought he managed the game well and put the Chiefs in a position to compete for the win. The big story of the night was the Chiefs’ first-team defense, which looked like it was in midseason form. With cuts down to the 53-man roster around the corner, there were numerous guys who played well enough to at least make general manager Brett Veach’s job difficult this Sunday. Here are five things we learned from the Chiefs’ 9-9 tie against the Seattle Seahawks . 1. Mansoor Delane is the real deal, Holyfield There is a reason that his name isn’t Boysoor Delane — it’s MANsoor, because that’s what he looks like on the football field. So far this preseason, what we’ve seen out of Delane is a guy who can tackle and cover like L’Jarius Sneed, but is also a blue-chip athlete. good player this Mansoor Delane pic.twitter.com/FsQ1XjhxcJ — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) August 29, 2026 It’s hard to find cornerbacks who like to tackle, or are as good at it as Delane is. But more importantly, it’s the way he sees the game. He can read and react to what receivers and running backs are doing, and get downfield in a flash. Kansas City has a long history of fielding some of the best defensive backs in the league, and when it’s all said and done, I think Delane has the potential to be up there with the best of them. 2. R Mason Thomas looks special No, that wasn’t the reincarnation of Derrick Thomas that you were watching on the field in this game. It’s been a long time since the Chiefs have had a pass rusher who looks this explosive on the edge. I’ll admit I wasn’t a fan of the pick back in April, but I’m quickly becoming a believer. You may want to argue that Thomas isn’t going against starters in these games, and to that I say, a guy with a get-off like this is going to be a problem, no matter who he is going against. R MASON THOMAS FROM THE OUTSIDE 💪 pic.twitter.com/IequkX9Zvo — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) August 29, 2026 This sort of speed translates into the regular season. 3. Marcus Harris played his way onto this team If you didn’t know who Marcus Harris was before this game, you do now. The 6-foot-3, 295-pound defensive tackle was originally a seventh-round pick for the Houston Texans back in 2024. The 25-year-old lineman started his college career playing for the Kansas Jayhawks in 2019 and 2020, before transferring to Auburn, where he would stay until he entered the draft. In his final year at Auburn, Harris registered seven sacks, but it was his run defense that stuck out in this game. He has a low center of gravity, which allows him to get under blocks and disrupt the backfield. 4. This defense has a chance to be special Beyond the impressive play by Delane and Thomas, the Chiefs defense played well overall, especially in the first quarter when the first team was out on the field. Guys in the secondary were flying around the field, and the pass rush looked explosive. There is going to be a moment similar to the closing moments of Week 5 last season against the Jacksonville Jaguars , where the Chiefs are trying to make a goal-line stand to win the game. Except, this time around, I think Kansas City has the bodies on defense to make a stand. When you combine the players they have on this side of the ball with the brilliant mind of defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo, you have all the ingredients to ruin someone’s day on defense. 5. We learned that there are still things we don’t know Will offensive tackle Josh Simmons miss significant time with his back injury? Is quarterback Patrick Mahomes really 100% good to go to play in this game? How will the Chiefs split the workload in the backfield? Will it be a 70/30 split with Kenneth Walker III taking the bulk of the carries? What effect will offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy have on the play calling? Will the Chiefs be better than last season? I think it is, but this is all speculation until they go out and actually do it in the regular season.

title: Chiefs News: Brett Veach prepared to add and subtract from roster this weekend
summary: The latest The Kansas City Chiefs finished the 2026 preseason with a 0-2-1 record after a 9-9 tie with the Seattle Seahawks on Friday night. Now general manager Brett Veach and the Chiefs’ front office will be trimming down the 91-man offseason roster to 53 players by Sunday’s deadline. Brett Veach on how Chiefs prepare […]
full_text: Kansas City Chiefs general manager Brett Veach observes players while standing alongside head coach Andy Reid during training camp at Missouri Western State University on Monday, July 28, 2025, in St. Joseph, Missouri. (Emily Curiel/The Kansas City Star/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) The latest The Kansas City Chiefs finished the 2026 preseason with a 0-2-1 record after a 9-9 tie with the Seattle Seahawks on Friday night. Now general manager Brett Veach and the Chiefs’ front office will be trimming down the 91-man offseason roster to 53 players by Sunday’s deadline. Brett Veach on how Chiefs prepare for roster additions & subtractions on cutdown day | The Kansas City Star “Every year, these last few weeks are always tough,” Veach said. “You have a lot of guys that have done a lot of great things for us over the years, and a lot of great competitions in the position groups. And as I mentioned, now it’s just a matter of kind of stacking our board like we do during the draft process, and targeting positions and needs, and creating dialog with other teams, and just trying to get our roster better. “And I think we have a lot of talent on both sides, but we’re certainly not a finished product. And again, there’s certainly areas that you know we can improve, and we’ll continue to do that throughout the season.” 5 takeaways from Kansas City Chiefs’ preseason finale vs. Seahawks | KSHB 41 4. No longer running on empty Kenneth Walker III didn’t play — and has barely played in the preseason — but the Chiefs’ run game continued to impress. Emari Demercado, who had nine carries for 37 yards, Emmett Johnson, who had seven carries for 39 yards, and Brashard Smith, who finished with 16 carries for 72 yards, totaled 32 carries for 148 yards and collectively added four receptions for 25 more yards. When the Chiefs’ offense was at its best during Eric Bieniemy’s first tenure as coordinator, the playcalling had balance, and the run game had an edge. Chiefs 53-man roster projection: Who earned a spot in preseason finale? | The Athletic Receivers (6) In: Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, Tyquan Thornton, Jalen Royals, Cyrus Allen, Andrew Armstrong Missed the cut: Nikko Remigio, Jimmy Holiday, Jason Brownlee, Xavier Loyd, Omari Evans, Jacob De Jesus, Jeff Weimer Remigio remains a high-floor, low-ceiling option at returner, and it seems likely he’d get back to the practice squad. We say the Chiefs go that route here while believing Smith and Allen can handle punt returns for the short term, with the option to elevate Remigio later if things don’t go well. In this scenario, Armstrong claims one of the last roster spots as a taller red zone weapon while flashing as an excellent run blocker. Armstrong led the Chiefs with five catches for 54 yards in Friday’s game. Chiefs 53-man roster projection 3.0: One final crack at the team’s initial roster | The Kansas City Star Tight end (3): Travis Kelce, Noah Gray, Jared Wiley Entering Year 14 in 2026, Travis Kelce still looks like he will be a critical part of the Chiefs’ offense. The only question in this room is whether the Chiefs keep four tight ends — and if they carry only three, who will be the third? Kansas City is high on Jake Briningstool, but given the extra quarterback and retaining Armstrong, it’s difficult to commit to him being on the initial roster. Briningstool is likely to pass through waivers, and if he does, he’s as good a bet as any cut to land back with the Chiefs’ practice squad. Four Takeaways From the Chiefs’ 9-9 Tie With the Seahawks | Sports Illustrated Potentially concerning observations about the cornerback room Early on tonight, it was veteran L’Jarius Sneed who opened his preseason slate as the Chiefs’ designated nickel man. He’s a player defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo is quite fond of, so it shouldn’t be a surprise that he may be in the mix for the first-string gig. With that said, the perceived fall of offseason signing Kader Kohou is alarming. Kohou had a quiet training camp and missed time this preseason due to injury. He played moderately late into the Seahawks game alongside several players who could be cut in the next 48 hours. It’s conceivable that Spagnuolo and Co. merely wanted to get the former Miami Dolphin some additional reps, although the context is something to note. Could part of the unofficial depth chart turn out to be true? Around the NFL Ravens’ Loop misses two FGs, booed amid job security questions | ESPN Loop is looking to come back from last season’s nightmare finale, when his 44-yard, last-second miss ended Baltimore’s season eight months ago. After missing wide left on tries from 51 and 58 yards Friday, Loop finished the preseason 5-of-8 (62.5%). It appeared that Ravens coach Jesse Minter, who had expressed confidence in Loop all offseason, struck a different tone after the game. Two-back system for Raiders? Klint Kubiak ‘really excited’ about Ashton Jeanty, Mike Washington Jr. | NFL.com Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak was asked Friday if he planned to utilize Jeanty and Washington similarly to how he used Kenneth Walker III and Zach Charbonnet last year in Seattle. “I think that they’re both going to prepare to play a lot of football,” Kubiak said. “As these games unfold, you react to the game. I think we’ve got two guys that we’re really excited about. We’ve got some younger guys that we’re really excited about, too. … They’ve just got to make the most of every rep that they get. The annual frenzy of NFL transactions happens this weekend | Pro Football Talk The deadline had been Tuesday. This year, the decision to move the first game to the Wednesday after Labor Day (with two teams heading to Australia for a game the next day) prompted a shift to Sunday. All in all, it’s a harsh process. The teams largely have become desensitized to it, because it’s a fundamental step in building a team. And the players who don’t have starting jobs set in stone understand that there’s a risk they’ll be leaving their current teams, possibly temporarily. Possibly for good. The practice squad helps to soften the blow. And those 16 spots for 32 teams create up to 512 more jobs. title: Should Rams trade Stetson Bennett for J.J. McCarthy?
summary: As speculation mounts that the Minnesota Vikings are prepared to part with recent first-round pick J.J. McCarthy, the Los Angeles Rams could swoop in with an interesting trade idea for both sides. Would Stetson Bennett make more sense as the Vikings’ QB3 than McCarthy and would McCarthy make more sense as the Rams’ QB2 than […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - AUGUST 22: Minnesota Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy (9) passes during the NFL preseason game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Minnesota Vikings on August 22nd, 2026, at U.S. Bank in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images As speculation mounts that the Minnesota Vikings are prepared to part with recent first-round pick J.J. McCarthy, the Los Angeles Rams could swoop in with an interesting trade idea for both sides. Would Stetson Bennett make more sense as the Vikings’ QB3 than McCarthy and would McCarthy make more sense as the Rams’ QB2 than Bennett? A change of scenery could benefit both quarterbacks, as well as Sean McVay and his former offensive coordinator Kevin O’Connell in Minnesota. Trading J.J. McCarthy can't be ruled out, but from everything I know, the situation isn't urgent, dire or toxic enough for the Vikings to just give him away. We shall see how the next few days play out. https://t.co/WMYgHvsRWA — Kevin Seifert (@SeifertESPN) August 28, 2026 Although it is far from official, people who cover the Vikings are starting to suspect that the Vikings could trade McCarthy, while others believe the team will flat out release him if the team is unable to find a trade partner. By all accounts, former Rams backup Carson Wentz will be backing up Kyler Murray when Minnesota opens the season in Week 1. McCarthy, the 10th overall pick in 2024 out of Michigan, missed his entire rookie season with injury. When he returned in 2025, he started 10 games, and though he flashed some talent, finished with 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. The team had more success when Wentz was under center, and then the Vikings went out and signed Murray in the offseason. As far as Stetson Bennett, despite some media hype that he was “great” in the second preseason game, the truth is probably close to him being underwhelming . At least as far as being the backup to Matthew Stafford in 2026. While Ty Simpson is far from ready to be a starter, he gives L.A. a closer model of Stafford and what type of offense McVay can run around the quarterback position than Bennett ever could. While McCarthy would also be a scary option as a backup due to his poor play in the NFL so far, he would be a better one than Bennett, a quarterback who is almost 29 and has never played in the NFL. Bennett could be Minnesota’s QB3, if they’re looking for an upgrade over Max Brosmer, while McCarthy could be a go-between on the Rams as L.A. continues to develop Simpson way behind the scenes. Would either side go for it? It definitely benefits the Rams more than it does the Vikings, and Minnesota has a new GM as of this past summer, someone who didn’t draft McCarthy and is probably ready to move on. So if the Vikings are considering cutting McCarthy anyway, and the Rams are considering the same for Bennett, a straight player-for-player swap could help both teams move on with dignity.
