title: Why the Rams’ preseason was ‘historically’ great
summary: The Angeles Rams had a great preseason, going 3-0 with zero turnovers and no sacks taken, and they passed each eye test you can think of. How will Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford top this in the regular season? Can the Rams go 17-0 with arguably the most stacked roster they’ve had in decades? If […]
full_text: The Angeles Rams had a great preseason, going 3-0 with zero turnovers and no sacks taken, and they passed each eye test you can think of. How will Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford top this in the regular season? Can the Rams go 17-0 with arguably the most stacked roster they’ve had in decades? If the Rams come out flat, people will talk. This team is expected to be special, not decent, not good, not very good; special. This team is built from top to bottom (they appear to have depth), and they should be able to build off of their strong preseason. That is the expectation. The Rams had a good preseason. Hurray! Now, it’s time to gear up. Will the Rams have a good regular season? You don’t trade for Myles Garrett and expect not to. Rams played a historically clean preseason with no turnovers or sacks (ramswire) “ In their three wins over the Chiefs, Saints and Chargers, the Rams didn’t commit a single turnover, nor did they allow a single sack. According to the NFL’s GSIS Statistics, no other team this preseason can say the same thing. They’re the only team in the league that didn’t allow a sack, and they’re one of four teams without a turnover; the other three all have one game left.“ Former NFL HC, Ex-Executive React as Ty Simpson Helps Rams Make History (heavy.com) “Ty Simpson put on another strong performance in the Los Angeles Rams’ preseason finale against the Los Angeles Chargers, helping cap off what was a historic exhibition slate for the franchise. “TY SIMPSON!” Super Bowl champion former head coach Jon Gruden posted on X on August 27, sharing a clip from the Rams of the rookie’s touchdown pass to Brennan Presley.“ Kelly Stafford Sends Strong Message After ‘Surprising’ Rams Trade (yahoo.sports) “The Los Angeles Rams like the roster balance reacquiring Tutu Atwell in a trade with the Miami Dolphins gives them, and it is going over with the family of star quarterback and reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, as his wife, Kelly Stafford, let on. “Ahhhh!!! My girls are gonna be so excited [smiling face holding back tears and hands raised emojis],” Kelly Stafford captioned a post on her Instagram story on August 27. She included the words over a graphic announcing Atwell’s return to the Rams.“ Sean McVay sheds light on Rams’ trade for Tutu Atwell (ramswire) “Additionally, Atwell won’t bump any wide receivers that were previously going to make the team off the roster. That’s an indication the Rams could keep as many as seven wideouts. “No. It had nothing to do with that,” McVay said. It was exclusively a guy that we’re familiar with that you could really get at what we felt like was good for us and good for Jarquez. He’ll do a good job for the Dolphins. It’s never easy when you have a guys that are such great people. But we’re familiar with Tutu. He adds depth, gives us an opportunity to be able to have that speed element and he can do some different things. It had nothing to do with anything other than adding depth to the receiver room.” Stetson Bennett trade hypothesis is gaining traction, and the Rams might be listening (ramblinfan) “Entering his fourth season in Horns, Bennett is either worthy of the backup role or he isn’t. And the fact that he hasn’t yet been named QB2 is telling . The former Georgia quarterback is playing in the last season of his rookie contract. There is no more wiggle room. What if Los Angeles sat Bennett for a different reason altogether? Teams often sit players who are the topic of trade talks. Sitting players limits the injury risk that could derail negotiations.“ Rams Preseason Hero Facing ‘Concerning’ Update Following Tutu Atwell Trade (sports.yahoo) “CJ Daniels isn’t guaranteed a spot on the active roster ahead of the Sept. 10 showdown against the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia. Even though Daniels has impressed fans in the NFL Preseason. DaSilva even shared the “concerning” part involving the past Miami Hurricanes star. “There was a lot of excitement about Daniels entering training camp and the preseason, and while he didn’t do anything wrong this summer, the Rams’ depth at wide receiver is great – especially with Atwell back. Plus, it’s a little bit concerning that he played so deep into the final preseason game,” DaSilva wrote on Friday.“ Sean McVay confirms what fans knew all along about Rams’ quarterback room (ramblinfan) “We’ve got three quarterbacks on our roster,” McVay said after Thursday’s preseason win over the Chargers. “Obviously, we’ve got the reigning MVP of the league. And then we got two guys that we feel really good about. And if you say, ‘Hey, what does that really mean?’ That’s what it means. We feel really good about those two guys. I’m not pigeon-holeing myself into any sort of decision other than I feel really good about Stetson Bennett. I feel really good about Ty Simpson.” The wheels were set in motion at the moment the Rams drafted Simpson. When Jimmy Garoppolo did not re-sign in free agency, the depth chart was already forming: Stafford as the starter, Bennett as the backup, and Simpson as an emergency reserve.“ 5 potential surprise cuts by Rams: 2 rookie draft picks in danger? (ramswire) “Around this time each year, teams make surprising decisions during final roster cuts . Players whose roster spots seemed safe get cut and sent to waivers, shocking the fanbase. The Los Angeles Rams aren’t immune to making unexpected decisions, with the release of John Franklin-Myers in 2019 immediately coming to mind. The Rams’ roster is mostly set in the eyes of Sean McVay and Les Snead, but fans may have different expectations for who Los Angeles will keep. These five players have a good chance to make the team, but they could wind up being surprise cuts by the Rams.“ Can Rams defense end LA’s shockingly long shutout drought? (sports.yahoo) “During the Sean McVay era, it’s been the offense carrying the Los Angeles Rams for the most part. Only once since 2017 have the Rams finished a season better than 10th in points allowed. That was in 2020, when the Rams ranked first in points and yards allowed on defense – a dominant defense wasted by an underwhelming offense. They’ve had star players come and go but it’s hard to say the Rams have had a better collective defense than the one they’ve assembled in 2026. With Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie, Jaylen Watson, Kobie Turner, Byron Young and others, the Rams have the potential to be the NFL’s No. 1 defense.“ ESPN model projects Myles Garrett to barely crack top 5 in sacks for 2026 (ramswire) “ESPN’s model set his projected mean sack total at 10.1, which is fifth among all players. Aidan Hutchinson (12.5), Micah Parsons (11.1), Will Anderson Jr. (10.5) and Nik Bonitto (10.3) all finished higher than Garrett. This is Walder’s explanation for Garrett’s low projection. Yes, I’m as surprised as you are that Garrett is not No. 1 on this list. Even though I know how the model works, I still thought the NFL-record 23 sacks from last season would be enough to put him over the top. Not quite, it turns out! There are three primary factors working against Garrett: 1. He is 30 years old 2. The Rams blitzed only 19% of the time last season, the second-lowest rate in the NFL 3. Los Angeles faces a quarterback slate that takes sacks less frequently than average” Comment of the Day: “I would have liked to see Simpson air a few out. One thing for sure, the guy has poise. If he was rattled at times he didn’t show it. Coaches can’t teach speed and the same goes for courage under fire. You have it, or you don’t. I read a great quote regarding heroism. I’ll change it to “leadership”. When a (leader) is scared, he’s the only one that knows it.“ -oldfartramfan Feedpost of the Day:

title: Rams running back Dean Connors is a gamer: Upon Further Review
summary: Dean Connors has given the Los Angeles Rams all they can handle when it comes to filling out their running backs room on NFL roster cutdown day this weekend. He’s not going to be RB1 or RB2 on this team with Kyren Williams and Blake Corum firmly entrenched in those spots, but his preseason performances […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Dean Connors #33 of the Los Angeles Rams carries the ball during the first half in a preseason game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dean Connors has given the Los Angeles Rams all they can handle when it comes to filling out their running backs room on NFL roster cutdown day this weekend. He’s not going to be RB1 or RB2 on this team with Kyren Williams and Blake Corum firmly entrenched in those spots, but his preseason performances have certainly been an encouraging sign of what he could offer this team should he make the final 53-man roster. Will he? There’s no doubt it will be a tough ask for the undrafted rookie out of Houston. But in the following few clips, you can see why so many fans are clamoring for No. 33 to get a shot with the club this year. Connors led the Rams in rushing in their preseason finale against the Los Angeles Chargers , posting 69 yards on 18 carries in a 20-18 win. He’s a stocky back, standing 5-foot-11 and 205 pounds, but he runs with an impressive smoothness. In the following clip, watch how fluidly he breaks to the outside for a first-down gain. The Rams aren’t hiding the run here. Twin tight ends to the left of the formation (from the quarterback’s viewpoint) with C.J. Daniels motioning to an in-line insert as well. The play flows to the right, opening up a cutback lane left with space. One of those tight ends washes out the defensive end and Connors swiftly cuts and bounces to the outside without slowing his momentum. Then, he has the speed to beat a cornerback to the boundary and nets a 12-yard gain. A quick-twitch cut and a second gear to create an explosive. That sounds like a set of traits Sean McVay would love to get in the mix, given how aggressively the Rams seek out explosive plays. Vision and patience are something else about Connors that stands out. It can’t be emphasized enough how helpful it is to have an offensive line that is just wrecking shop in front of a ball carrier. The Chargers are getting blown off the ball here. But even with a line like that, there are countless examples of NFL running backs, both guys on the fringes and ones who make final rosters, who don’t have the patience to wait for the best possible running lane. Connors is willing to wait, though, and responds quickly once that hole opens. Instead of trying to play battering ram and ither running into his own man or trying to bounce outside too early, he stays in phase with his blockers and takes the easy gain straight ahead. He makes a quick cut right, then lets off the gas so he doesn’t outrun the blocking. It seems simple, but if you watch the league (or the players out of college entering it), it’s much easier said than done. Then there’s the toughness. Who doesn’t want that in a running back? The Rams have built this offense line with the idea that the interior players can use their massive size and strength to overwhelm defensive linemen and linebackers, clearing room for their backs. It led to one of the most efficient rushing attacks in the NFL history last year, statistically speaking. But when your running back can add an extra dash of toughness it only helps matters more. Credit goes to the offensive line here for creating plenty of space for Connors to work with, but once again he sees the correct alley immediately and, most importantly, he finishes the run. He sheds a linebacker and bounces off a pursuing defensive back to gain a couple extra yards, finishing with seven on the play. Again, this is not someone who is going to usurp Williams or Corum on the depth chart. And even if he doesn’t make the initial 53, he’s a no-doubt practice squad candidate and, given the modern elevation rules, it’s fair to assume he’d get some run at some point this season. But when you find an undrafted talent with good vision, quick decision making and plus fluidity, it’s hard to pass that up. For a team that loves to hunt big plays, Connors could be a useful weapon in 2026.

(Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders drafted Fernando Mendoza with plans for him to take the reins as the starting quarterback. John Spytek and Klint Kubiak believe in the young quarterback and what he can do for the franchise in the future. When it comes to putting him on the football field, the team wants to make sure he is ready. During the preseason, Mendoza had ups and downs, which is why they thought Cousins should start early. The question now becomes: when does Mendoza get the starting job? title: Raiders News: Klint Kubiak won’t commit to naming the starting QB
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders just finished their last football game of the preseason with an 18-12 loss. It is now time for the Raiders to cut their roster to the final 53 and get ready for the Miami Dolphins. The biggest part of the 53 is picking the starting quarterback. The Raiders have Kirk Cousins […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders passes against the San Francisco 49ers during the second quarter of a preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders just finished their last football game of the preseason with an 18-12 loss. It is now time for the Raiders to cut their roster to the final 53 and get ready for the Miami Dolphins. The biggest part of the 53 is picking the starting quarterback. The Raiders have Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza vying for a shot at being the starter. After three preseason games, it appears that Kirk Cousins is comfortably in the lead. However, Klint Kubiak has not yet committed to a starter. When asked on Friday, he said he wanted more time to make a decision. “I still don’t think we need to name anybody,” the first-year coach said. “We have a lot to talk about at a lot of positions, so we want to watch the film and talk about everything as a staff.” Kubiak seems to take from his dad, who didn’t like to give too much information until the right time. While it is pretty obvious to fans who the starter is, the Raiders will keep us waiting for the actual decision. Even after the regular season kicks off, we will see plenty of roster moves, especially for Miami who will likely churn the bottom of the roster all season long. The 2026 season is not expected to be a good one for the Dolphins. According to the oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook, Miami has the longest odds to make the playoffs in the AFC at +1500 . The New York Jets have the next worst odds at +700. title: Dolphins roster predictions: Final 53-man projection 2026
summary: The NFL’s roster deadline is 6 p.m. Eastern tonight, requiring teams to drop from the allocated 90-man preseason rosters to the 53-player regular-season limit. The cuts started yesterday all around the league, including with the Miami Dolphins who waived 12 players. The Dolphins open the day with 78 players on the roster and need to […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 28: Miami Dolphins wait to take the field to face the Atlanta Falcons during the first half at Hard Rock Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL’s roster deadline is 6 p.m. Eastern tonight, requiring teams to drop from the allocated 90-man preseason rosters to the 53-player regular-season limit. The cuts started yesterday all around the league, including with the Miami Dolphins who waived 12 players. The Dolphins open the day with 78 players on the roster and need to make moves with at least 25 more. The focus is on the cuts, whether they are players being waived or released depends on service time for each individual, but there are other options that can happen. Miami executed a trade yesterday, sending quarterback Quinn Ewers to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a draft pick, trimming one of the spots on the roster. I predicted the Dolphins’ 53-man roster before the team’s game on Friday against the Jaguars. Today, we make one final projection before the 53-man roster is known. Note: I am only projecting 52 players on the roster right now because I expect the Dolphins to cut Bradley Pinion. I left the roster spot open since they obviously need a punter. There are some other strange moves I made – like only keeping one quarterback – with explanations of why I made those decisions in each position group. Miami Dolphins offense (24) Quarterback (1) Malik Willis Quinn Ewers – Traded to Jaguars 8/29 Cut: Cam Miller, Mark Gronowski Changes: The Dolphins’ trade of Ewers. In this projection, the Dolphins are only keeping one quarterback, not because that is realistic, but because I do not see them keeping either Miller or Gronowski. Maybe the do slide Miller onto the roster, then waive him once they make a waiver claim for someone who is cut by another team, but Miami’s second-string quarterback is not on the roster right now, and I am going to give the team one quarterback as they work to find the right player to backup Willis. Running backs (4) De’Von Achane Jaylen Wright Ollie Gordon II Jarquez Hunter Cut: Coleman Bennett (Waived 8/29), Donovan Edwards (Waived 8/29), Carlos Washington, Jr. Changes: None “That’s a good question,” head coach Jeff Hafley said on Saturday when asked if Miami would keep four tailbacks on the roster. “I think those are still some of the discussions going on, and I think that will clear up between today and tomorrow.” I think they will keep four. Otherwise, why did they trade for Hunter? Fullbacks (1) DJ Herman Changes: Add Herman I go back and forth on Herman. I am back to having him on the roster. I think he brings enough to the offense as a lead blocker and a pass protector that the coaches will want to keep him around. He could slide to the practice squad, then be elevated, but it feels like he is going to make the roster, even with the ugly dropped pass he had in the game on Friday. Tight ends (3) Greg Dulcich Will Kacmarek Ben Sims Cut: Ethan Conner (Waived 8/29), Seydou Traore, Jeremiah Franklin Changes: None. This is where I am going to use the additional spot having one quarterback on the roster gives me. It feels like Sims is going to land on injured reserve, but teams are limited two players that can be directly placed on IR in the roster cuts, and those are going to be used elsewhere. I will keep Sims on the roster here, then place him on IR on Monday when the Dolphins need to create roster space for a quarterback. Conner (waived on Saturday), Traore, or Franklin could land on the practice squad, then be elevated for game day for the first few weeks of the season, giving Miami three tight ends and a fullback active for the games. Offensive lineman (9) Tackles Patrick Paul Austin Jackson Caedan Wallace Charlie Heck Guards Kadyn Proctor Jonah Savaiinaea DJ Campbell Centers Aaron Brewer Andrew Meyer Cut: Gottlieb Ayedze, Jim Bonifas, Kevin Cline (Waived 8/29), Marques Cox, James Ester, Josh Priebe Changes: Add Heck; Cut Priebe I have thought Priebe was going to make the roster as a reserve guard who also provides backup work as a center, a move that could lead to Meyer being cut. After Friday night, I think Priebe played himself off the roster and back to the practice squad for this year. With Priebe coming off the roster, I have the space to put Heck back on the 53. Wide receivers (6) Malik Washington Caleb Douglas Chris Bell Kevin Coleman, Jr. Jalen Tolbert Jalen Reagor Cut: AJ Henning, Donaven McCulley, Terrace Marshall, Jr., Ryan Miller, Theo Wease, Jr. (Waived 8/29) Changes: None I am not positive Tolbert is on the roster by the end of the day on Sunday because Miami could look for a trade partner. He played 24 snaps on Friday night, a high number given the Dolphins sat all of their starters and even Bell, the rookie who was making his debut after being cleared to return from an ACL tear he suffered last year, only played 14 snaps. He would be a good veteran presence in the group, but I am not sure he is in Miami’s plans, given their desire to give the rookies playing time to develop them for the future. Reagor is not a lock, but I have believed his special teams play, especially as a returner, keeps him on the roster and Friday reinforced that idea. Ryan Miller could be a bubble player who steals a roster spot. If the roster math gets ugly, keeping five receivers and having someone on the practice squad to elevate is an option as well. Miami Dolphins defense (26) Defensive ends (5) Chop Robinson Josh Uche Robert Beal, Jr. Max Llewellyn Clelin Ferrell Cut: Cameron Goode, Seth Coleman-Lyles (Waived 8/29), Rodney McGraw, David Ojabo Changes: Cut Goode Goode falls back off the roster; I just do not think he has done enough to clinch a spot on the 53. Ferrell hangs on to a roster spot, but he has been dealing with an injury and he could be a consideration for another player who moves to IR on Monday. Defensive tackle (5) Zach Sieler Jordan Phillips Zeek Biggers Matthew Butler Keith Cooper, Jr. Injured Reserve: Kenneth Grant Cut: Alex Huntley (Waived 8/29), Fatorma Mulbah, Cam Rice (Waived 8/29) Changes: Grant to IR; Add Cooper I moved Butler onto the roster and pulled Mulbah off ahead of Friday’s game, and I think it was the right move. Moving Grant to one of the two direct-to-IR slots opens a roster spot, with Cooper sliding into it. If you want to swap out Cooper and Mulbah, I think that is fine as well. They are both probably practice squad players, but in this scenario I have Cooper on the roster until Grant is healthy. Then the Dolphins can waive Cooper and have him join Mulbah on the practice squad. Linebackers (7) Jordyn Brooks Jacob Rodriguez Tyrel Dodson Kyle Louis Ronnie Harrison, Jr. Willie Gay, Jr. Jackson Woodard IR: Trey Moore Cut: Stephen Dix, Jr. (Waived 8/29), Cam Riley, Jaheim Thomas (Waived 8/29) Changes: Add Woodard I am very heavy at linebacker when you just look at seven names on the roster, but there is some method to it. The group has already had some injury concerns with Brooks and Dodson, plus Moore landing on IR, leading to a need for a deeper group. Louis is listed as a linebacker by the Dolphins, but he has also been working as a safety, which may be where he settles in for this year. Gay is probably the wildcard in the group – it would not be a surprise if he were cut, but for now I have him making the team. As I said on the last projection, the team needs to find a way to keep Woodard, either on the roster or on the practice squad. In this projection, I protect him by moving him to the 53. title: Dolphins trade Quinn Ewers as 2026 preseason ends
summary: The Miami Dolphins are trading quarterback Quinn Ewers to the Jacksonville Jaguars, swapping late-round picks in the 2028 NFL Draft in the deal. The trade was first reported by ESPN and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo. Update: The Dolphins announced the trade Saturday evening, indicating the team was receiving a 2028 sixth-round pick […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - AUGUST 14: Quinn Ewers #14 of the Miami Dolphins looks to pass against the Washington Commanders during the first half of a preseason game at Northwest Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are trading quarterback Quinn Ewers to the Jacksonville Jaguars, swapping late-round picks in the 2028 NFL Draft in the deal. The trade was first reported by ESPN and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo . Update: The Dolphins announced the trade Saturday evening, indicating the team was receiving a 2028 sixth-round pick in exchange for Ewers. Trade | We have agreed to terms with the Jacksonville Jaguars to acquire a 2028 sixth-round pick in exchange for quarterback Quinn Ewers, pending a physical. pic.twitter.com/CkvB3uTzSg — Miami Dolphins (@MiamiDolphins) August 29, 2026 Ewers was selected by Miami in the seventh round of the 2025 NFL Draft out of Texas. He spent much of his rookie season as the third-string quarterback, but he moved into the starting role late in the season when the Dolphins benched quarterback Tua Tagovailoa. He threw for 622 yards on a 66.3 percent completion rate with three touchdowns and three interceptions. He appeared in four games during the season, starting three of them. Miami cut Tagovailoa this offseason, then signed free agent Malik Willis as his replacement. Ewers was expected to assume the second-string position, but his play early in training camp and the preseason was underwhelming. He sustained a groin injury during the first preseason game against the Washington Commanders and, while he finished his time in that game, he was sidelined for about a week. He did not play in the second preseason game because of the injury and was held out in last night’s preseason finale as well. The trade comes a day before the league’s 53-man regular-season roster limit is enforced, dropping from the preseason 90-man limit. Miami has Willis, Cam Miller, and Mark Gronowski at quarterback, but neither Miller nor Gronowski has instilled confidence in their ability to serve as Willis’s backup. The Dolphins will likely be active on the waiver wire and in talks with free agent quarterbacks to join the team and provide a solid option if Willis is injured.

title: Do the Dolphins have a punting problem?
summary: NFL cutdown day is here, with all 32 teams needing to drop from their preseason 90-man roster size down to the regular season’s 53-player limit by 6 p.m. Eastern on Sunday. It is the primary focus for each team and around the league right now, as nearly 1,200 players are waived, released, or placed on […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 22: Bradley Pinion #48 of the Miami Dolphins reacts to a punt against the New York Giants during the first half of a pre season game at Hard Rock Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images NFL cutdown day is here, with all 32 teams needing to drop from their preseason 90-man roster size down to the regular season’s 53-player limit by 6 p.m. Eastern on Sunday. It is the primary focus for each team and around the league right now, as nearly 1,200 players are waived, released, or placed on injured lists. Teams are also looking around the league to consider who may become available for a waiver claim or as a free agent following a release. The Miami Dolphins may have to make a roster move at an unexpected position over the next few days. Miami seems to have a punting problem. Summer-long punting concerns continue after preseason game against Falcons After the first preseason game, a loss to the Washington Commanders, I wrote, “ Punter Bradley Pinion is a concern , with some of his kicks tonight seeming off. He may work off the rust and be ready by the regular season, but his performance tonight didn’t instill confidence.” After the second game, a loss to the New York Giants, I was a little more generalized in my special teams critique, writing, “ The special teams are not good right now . Nothing seems to be working in sync, whether it is kick coverage, punt coverage, field goal attempts, kick returns, or punt returns. The entire special teams unit needs to be a focal point between now and the start of the regular season.” After last night’s game against the Atlanta Falcons, another loss as the preseason schedule closed out for Miami, I added, “[P]unter Bradley Pinion continues to make me nervous for the season. Miami is going to need its punter to be consistent and a field-position-changing weapon, and Pinion has not been that this summer. He has some good kicks, but he shanks them just as often.” The special teams play has been a concern throughout the month, and Pinion is a big part of that concern. Against the Falcons, he had punts of 60 yards, 53 yards, 51 yards, 33 yards, and 36 yards. When he connects cleanly, Pinion can blast the ball. But he seems to have as many misses as he does solid kicks. Field goal holds have not been clean And it is not just the kicking. Field goals were a roller coaster, with Pinion as the holder. On one field goal attempt, he did not field the snap cleanly and had to rush to get the ball in place; kicker Riley Patterson connected on the kick, but it was an awkward-looking kick that knuckled as it flew. Pinion also struggled with another snap on a field goal attempt that wound up being blocked. Long snapper Tucker Addington is also part of the issue, but concern about Pinion’s play continues to grow. Options if Miami make a move The Dolphins have limited options if they are looking to make a move at the punter position. Available free agents include former San Francisco 49ers punter Thomas Morstead, former New York Giants punter Jamie Gillan, the soon-to-be released Mitch Wishnowsky from the Buffalo Bills, and Nik Constantinou who was waived by the Cleveland Browns on Saturday. Morstead was drafted by the New Orleans Saints in the fifth round of the 2009 NFL Draft and would be entering his 18th season. He has a career average of 46.7 yards per kick, including 46.4 yards per kick in 2022 while punting for the Dolphins. Gillan was released by the Giants in March after four seasons with the team. He began his career with a three-year stint with the Cleveland Browns after signing as an undrafted free agent in 2019 out of the University of Arkansas – Pine Bluff. He also had a brief practice squad stint with the Buffalo Bills near the end of the 2021 season after the Browns waived him. He has a 45.2 yards per punt average in his seven seasons. The Bills will cut Wishnowsky as part of the team’s moves ahead of the roster deadline, according to Tom Pelissero . He had been in a training camp battle with drafted rookie Tommy Doman, but appears to be on the losing side of the fight. Wishnowsky spent his first six years in the NFL with the San Francisco 49ers before spending last season in Buffalo. He was drafted in the fourth round of the 2019 NFL Draft by San Francisco out of Utah and has a career 45.5 yard punting average. Constantinou was one of two punters in training camp with the Browns. He was undrafted in 2024, signing with the Denver Broncos, but was waived before training camp. After a two-year stint in the Canadian Football League, Constantinou returned to the NFL on a futures contract with the Browns but was unable to claim the roster spot. The Browns still have a decision to make when it comes to punters. Even after releasing Constantinou, they still have Corey Bojorquez and Wes Phal on the roster at a position where most teams carry only one player. The New England Patriots are also carrying two punters right now. Bryce Baringer has been the primary punter throughout the preseason, but he sustained an injury that, last week, forced New England to sign veteran Matt Haack, who was cut by the Washington Commanders a week earlier. If Baringer is healthy enough to reclaim his spot atop the depth chart, Haack could be an interesting consideration for Miami. He began his career as an undrafted free agent out of Arizona State and signed with Miami. He played the first four of his nine seasons with the Dolphins and has a career 45.0-yard-per-punt average. Do the Dolphins make a move? Pinion has averaged 45.6 yards per punt this preseason, which would have ranked 25th in the league last year. For a team that is going to be having offensive growing pains with rookies and younger players trying to grow together, they need to trust their punter to be able to change the field position game with every kick. Pinion could be that weapon, but the inconsistency is the biggest issue. Miami cannot go into the season not knowing if their punter’s next kick will be over 60 yards or around 30 yards. They cannot worry about the holds on kicks and extra points. They have to trust that the special teams to do their job, and right now they cannot have that trust. If the Dolphins’ coaching staff thinks they can find a more reliable punter, they have to make that move. Pinion not inspired any sense of confidence in his kicks this summer. It seems like it is time to make a move.

title: Falcons vs. Dolphins: Miami players to watch in Preseason Week 3 revisited
summary: The Miami Dolphins lost to the Atlanta Falcons last night, ending a rough preseason schedule for the South Florida franchise. Miami is in the early stages of a rebuild – even if head coach Jeff Hafley does not like to use that specific term – with the roster moving from a veteran-heavy, win-now past into […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - AUGUST 10: Miami Dolphins safety Major Burns (43) runs a play during the Miami Dolphins Training Camp on August 10 2026, at the Baptist Health Training Complex in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Doug Murray/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins lost to the Atlanta Falcons last night, ending a rough preseason schedule for the South Florida franchise. Miami is in the early stages of a rebuild – even if head coach Jeff Hafley does not like to use that specific term – with the roster moving from a veteran-heavy, win-now past into one dominated by young players who will grow together into the nucleus of a (hopefully) consistent winner. It was not the best start, as Miami struggled to score points throughout the summer and were seemingly overmatched nearly every time they faced an opponent – both in preseason games and in training camp joint practices. Before the game, I presented five players to watch. I focused on bubble players who likely needed to make an impact to secure their spot on the 53-man regular-season roster. Teams must drop to the new limit, down from the preseason 90-player tolerance, by 6 p.m. on Sunday. Did any of the players have a performance that locks them onto the roster – or a performance that eliminates them from making it to the 53? We revisit my players to watch this afternoon. Defensive tackle Fatorma Mulbah Pre-game: Mulbah went undrafted out of West Virginia in 2025 and signed with the New York Jets. He did not make the roster out of the preseason and spent time on the practice squad during the year. He signed with the Dolphins at the start of August, and he has made an impact quickly. Mulbah has been a force in the middle of the line, especially against the run. He is not perfect and he has growth that still needs to happen, but with a strong performance against the Falcons, he could force Miami to keep him on the roster rather than risking having him claimed off waivers by another team. Revisit: Mulbah only played eight snaps in the game, and I do not think I noticed him on any of those plays. He is likely fighting for a roster spot with veteran Matthew Butler, who played 31 snaps. It does not look like Mulbah did enough to force his way onto the roster and he is likely headed to the practice squad. Fullback D.J. Herman Pre-game: I have gone back and forth on projecting Herman to make the roster, with him on the wrong side of the cut line in today’s 53-man roster projection . He has been solid as a lead blocker, in pass protection, and as an outlet option in the passing game. A linebacker in college, Herman has made the adjustment to being a fullback and he is doing it well enough to force the Dolphins to at least consider using a roster spot to keep him. Tight end Ben Sims, who is listed as the first team fullback on the depth chart, has missed time and Herman has taken advantage of the opportunity. A strong performance on Friday, especially if he makes a special teams play, could land him on the right side of the cut line. Revisit: Herman was on the field for 24 plays, giving him a fair share of experience in the contest. When you consider that Herman is a fullback, 24 snaps might actually be a decent snap count for a regular-season game. He had an awful drop against the Falcons, one that he has to correct, but he has had a solid training camp and preseason as a whole. He may not have done enough to guarantee a roster spot, but he did not eliminate himself from consideration. The biggest factor in Herman making the roster may be the health of tight end Ben Sims, who was working as a fullback ahead of Herman before a toe injury sidelined him. If Sims is going to miss playing time early this year, Herman makes the roster. If Sims will be ready in Week 1, Herman may be headed to the practice squad. Defensive end Cameron Goode Pre-game: The numbers seem to be against Goode making the roster this year, but the 2022 seventh-round pick could change that tonight. Primarily a special teams player, if he can make an impact during the game, he might force his way onto the roster. He has been fine during training camp, but fine might not be good enough to justify a roster position. Stepping up tonight might be a requirement for Goode to stay with the team another year. Revisit: Goode is likely relying on his special teams play to lock him into a roster spot this year after not really doing much on defense against the Falcons. He was on the field for 17 plays, and, according to Pro Football Focus , had six pass rush opportunities but came away with no pressures. He did have a special teams tackle, but I do not think it was enough to make the roster. Safety Major Burns / Lonnie Johnson / Louis Moore Pre-game: I am absolutely cheating here by putting all three players in one spot on my five players to watch, but it is because there really is not any separation between them at this point. One of the three of them will make the roster as the fourth safety on the depth chart – which one could be determined tonight. Johnson has dealt with an injury this summer, Burns has flashed but may not be as consistent, and Moore is a rookie trying to go from undrafted to the roster. Revisit: This one is a little more direct comparison. One of the three should make the roster, but which one? Burns played 31 snaps, the third-most on the defense for the Dolphins, while Moore was in on 23 plays and Johnson appeared on 17 plays. Burns and Johnson each recorded two tackles while Moore had one. Based on snap counts, Burns might have a slight lead in the race to the roster, but it does not feel definitive. I think Moore is probably headed to the practice squad while I think Burns does make the 53 – but as I said before the game, there is not any separation between the three. Offensive lineman Charlie Heck Pre-game: The Dolphins likely signed Heck as a free agent to serve as the swing tackle and primary game-day backup for both Patrick Paul at left tackle and Austin Jackson at right tackle. He has been inconsistent all summer and he has done everything except claim that role. I do not have him making the roster right now, but a strong performance tonight could change that. Heck could find help in the roster math if guard Josh Priebe sees playing time at center and plays well, that could lead Miami to releasing center Andrew Meyer and open a roster spot for Heck. It might be a backdoor way to make the roster, but it would still land him on the roster. Revisit: I think Heck did enough to push him onto the roster. He played in 19 snaps and, while he was not perfect, he was solid enough while guard Josh Priebe may have played himself off the roster, giving Heck the space needed. Priebe, who played the most snaps on offense for Miami, had a rough outing, both at guard and as a backup center and may now be headed back to the practice squad.

full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 28: Tua Tagovailoa #1 of the Atlanta Falcons throws against the Miami Dolphins during the first half at Hard Rock Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins lost to the Atlanta Falcons on Friday night, bringing to a close the team’s 2026 preseason schedule. The focus over the next two days will be on the roster moves Miami makes to drop its 90-man roster down to the league-mandated regular-season limit of 53 players. The Dolphins, and all 31 other teams in the NFL, must complete the culling by 6 p.m. Eastern on Sunday. Even with the game result fresh and roster cuts looming, Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley took some time in his post-game press conference to address his recent interview with ESPN’s Stephen A. Smith in which the coach said, “Success is not going to be measured in wins and losses this year — and I know nobody wants to hear that.” In a league that is built around wins and losses and with a fan base begging to have their team turned back into the winner it one was, what does the coach mean by that? After the game, the coach’s explanation of his comments was shared by the Miami Herald’s Barry Jackson: “We and I want to win in everything that we do. But success is not just defined by winning. Winning, for sure. That’s why you play the game… But at the same time, we need to make sure this process is built the right way. “The whole key to this year is do everything we can to win football games but making sure we do it right, so the foundation is right and the process is right. I want to make sure we’re doing it the right way with no shortcuts. “It’s important that we move this thing forward and build… because we want to get back on top. To do that, you got to go through some hard stuff, with competing in mind to win in everything we do, but keeping the main thing our process and the detail and the toughness and not taking shortcuts and not flinching along the way, so at the end of the year, we can look back and say, ‘Our foundation is strong. We’re not going away. Look out, ‘We’re coming.’ “That kind of got lost in our conversation [with Stephen A. Smith]. I can look you in the eye and say: We are going to do everything we can to try to win every single game.” You can check out the rest of that story here, and the rest of the day’s round-up below. summary: A claim from last August will be returning to the wire. The New England Patriots have waived defensive tackle Eric Gregory ahead of the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline, as first reported Sunday by ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. Gregory, 25, landed in Foxborough on the heels of the 2025 cutdown deadline after spending his rookie preseason with […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 13: Eric Gregory #95 of the New England Patriots during a preseason game between the New England Patriots and the Indianapolis Colts on August 13, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A claim from last August will be returning to the wire. The New England Patriots have waived defensive tackle Eric Gregory ahead of the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline, as first reported Sunday by ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler . Gregory, 25, landed in Foxborough on the heels of the 2025 cutdown deadline after spending his rookie preseason with the Cincinnati Bengals. The 6-foot-3, 319-pound undrafted free agent out of Arkansas went on to appear in six games before being placed on injured reserve during the playoff run. Across 126 snaps on the interior defensive line, he had a hand in eight tackles. In last week’s preseason finale against the Cleveland Browns, Gregory started and stayed in for 55 percent of the workload, the highest rate among non-linebackers and defensive backs in the fold. The reigning AFC champions went from 91 to 73 reported players on the eve of the NFL’s deadline and acquired running back Corey Kiner in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals. When factoring in designations to return from injured reserve, plus the physically unable to perform and non-football injury lists, active rosters around the league will be down to 53 by 6 p.m. ET Sunday.

title: Sunday Patriots Notes: Defensive depth a concern as cutdown deadline looms
summary: The New England Patriots’ preseason is complete as they now must trim their roster to 53 players by Sunday 6 p.m. ET. The work has already begun for the Patriots, who will then work on filling out their practice squad before turning their attention fully to Seattle. Before the roster movement and Week 1 prep […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: Luke Floriea #81 of the Cleveland Browns scores a touchdown during the first quarter of a preseason game against the New England Patriots at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots’ preseason is complete as they now must trim their roster to 53 players by Sunday 6 p.m. ET. The work has already begun for the Patriots , who will then work on filling out their practice squad before turning their attention fully to Seattle. Before the roster movement and Week 1 prep begins, however, let’s take one final look back at the week that was. Welcome to the latest installment of our Sunday Patriots Notes . Depth concerns The buzzword around 1 Patriots Place continues to be depth. That stems from head coach Mike Vrabel’s comments after the Patriots’ second preseason game. “I do not think we have a very deep team,” Vrabel said. As the Patriots concluded their preseason Thursday night in Cleveland, the lack of depth — specifically on defense — was on display again. Quarterback Dillon Gabriel and the Browns’ backups marched up and down the field against New England’s reserves in a 37-13 win, leaving Vrabel looking for more. “Not good enough,” the coach said. “We got a couple sudden change stops, forced them to kick some field goals which I think is always positive. But not good enough. We couldn’t match the speed of the quarterback in the zone read and some of those things. But we’ll get back to work and figure out who we get back to work with.” The Patriots will now sort through the players on the roster bubble as they cut the group down from 91 to 53 players by Sunday evening. They will also be on the hunt for upgrades on the waiver wire to improve their depth. As for the top spots they might look to upgrade, here’s where we’ll be watching: Defensive line: Entering the summer as one of the deeper groups on the roster, the Patriots’ reserve defensive lineman struggled against the run throughout the summer. New England could be on the hunt for more size at nose tackle behind Cory Durden. Edge: Mike Vrabel left the door open for Harold Landry to be activated off the PUP list before Week 1. What the veteran has left in the tank is TBD. Gabe Jacas, meanwhile, is not ready for a significant role out of the gate, while no other depth option has pushed for a consistent role. Even with free-agent addition Dre’Mont Jones and improvement from Elijah Ponder in Year 2, the edge group remains the weakest overall on the roster. Linebacker: The Patriots do have a strong duo in Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss atop the depth chart, but the depth behind them remains a concern. Rookie Khalil Jacobs was trending upward before suffering an injury, while fellow rookie Namdi Obiazor is likely on the team primarily for his special teams value. Veteran Chad Muma then had significant issues in preseason action while K.J. Britt was inconsistent as well. Cornerback: The Browns picked on Patriots corners Kindle Vildor, Charles Woods, Karon Prunty and Marcellas Dial Jr. Thursday night. The depth behind Christian Gonzalez, Carlton Davis and Marcus Jones remains worrisome, particularly given the injury history surrounding the top of the group. Waiver wire Speaking of the waiver wire, it’s a tool the Patriots used last year claiming both quarterback Tommy DeVito and cornerback Charles Woods, and one Vrabel said they will continue to use moving forward. However, the Patriots will be 31st in the waiver order this go around after holding the 4th spot last year. “When you’re at the back end of the waiver claim, that’s a great thing,” vice president of player personnel Ryan Cowden said. “But it’s also, you know, some good players that become available are going to be gone before you get that opportunity.” Resting starters With the emphasis on health, Mike Vrabel decided not to play the Patriots starters at all throughout the preseason. “I just think that it’s best for us right now to try to start next week with the guys that we have. I know that’s a difficult decision. I don’t think there’s a right or wrong answer,” Vrabel said. “We have to just continue to try to prepare the football team the best that we can. We just wanted to try to get to the regular season with the guys that we had.” That will mean Drake Maye and Co.’s first live snaps of the season will come Sept. 9 against the Seahawks in the opener. Seattle’s starters will also take their first live snaps of the year in that matchup, as head coach Mike Macdonald followed a similar preseason approach to Vrabel. Gonzo’s frustration For the first time this offseason, Christian Gonzalez admitted he’s frustrated that he remains without a contract extension with the Patriots. Asked about his cornerback Thursday night, Vrabel preached patience. “I don’t have a reaction,” Vrabel said. “I have conversations with Christian, and I understand that this is probably something that’s difficult. I’ve never been in that position to this extent. I try to treat it with class, but also, him and I communicate. He’s always free – our players are always free to feel how they want to feel, and you just have to stay patient, and hope that we can continue to work to some sort of degree.” Earlier on Thursday, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported the two sides haven’t “been close” on a contract extension . Gonzalez’s team and the Patriots will work to come to an agreement again this week, but Schefter speculated if no deal is reached before Week 1, the sides may wait until next offseason or then potentially listen to trade offers. Vice president of player personnel was asked if trading Gonzalez is a possibility. “I think we’re continuing to work on the negotiation side of Christian and, you know, I think that’s where that stays,” he said on Tuesday. Van Roten’s memory Before signing with the Patriots, veteran offensive lineman Greg Van Roten visited the team. For veterans, those visits are often an opportunity to get a feel for the team’s environment and determine whether it’s a good fit. It turns out, Van Roten was already impressed by the Patriots from a Week 12 game last season when he was a member of the New York Giants. “I actually told this to Coach Vrabes. When we were getting ready to play [Dec. 1 last season], we were pretty fired up to come here, Monday night, play the Patriots, and everyone was chirping about their schedule and this and that,” Van Roten shared. “There have been a few games in my [12-year] NFL career where you play against a defense and it feels a little bit different. And that was one of those games. “They were flying around. Hitting hard. It was a very physical game very early on. I’ve been a part of a lot of NFL games but that one stood out. So that was another reason why I wanted to come here because they seem to have guys playing football the right way.” Wet mule It’s been an up-and-down summer for rookie Gabe Jacas, which included another poor edge set on a read-option play in the preseason finale. After missing all of the spring and start of training camp, Jacas looks like he’s drinking through a firehose on the field. Still, the coaching staff has high hopes for the rookie’s long-term future. “I’m not a gambler, but I kind of look at maybe anything in life as gambling. You got a kid that’s big like him, that’s athletic like him, that’s meaner than a wet mule, and he loves football. I’m not gonna say he’s gonna be Jason Taylor or LT or any of that stuff, but it’s gonna be very hard for him to fail,” outside linebackers coach Mike Smith said. Forever brother DeMario Douglas and Kayshon Boutte were both drafted by the Patriots in the sixth-round of the 2023 NFL Draft. That’s why Monday’s trade, which sent Boutte to the Houston Texans, was extra hard on Douglas “It was tough. That’s my guy,” Douglas said following Tuesday’s practice. “That’s who I came in [the league] with. That’s my brother, my forever…

title: What their first wave of roster cuts means for the Patriots
summary: The New England Patriots began the process of cutting their roster down to 53 players on Saturday. After starting the day with 91 players, including roster-exempt offensive tackle Lorenz Metz, they currently stand at 73 following a series of releases and acquiring running back Corey Kiner via trade. Let’s find out what it means for […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 22: Marcellas Dial Jr. #27 of the New England Patriots during a preseason game between the New England Patriots and the Philadelphia Eagles on August 22, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots began the process of cutting their roster down to 53 players on Saturday. After starting the day with 91 players, including roster-exempt offensive tackle Lorenz Metz, they currently stand at 73 following a series of releases and acquiring running back Corey Kiner via trade . Let’s find out what it means for the Patriots from a big-picture perspective. No surprises New England’s first wave of cuts did not include any surprises, as the Patriots largely released undrafted free agents who were buried on the depth chart. The harder decisions will come Sunday. Among them: Did rookie Behren Morton do enough to warrant keeping three quarterbacks on the 53-man roster? How will the offensive and defensive depth shake out in the trenches? Did a young pass rusher do enough to stick behind Dre’Mont Jones and Elijah Ponder? And who will emerge as the top backup cornerback in the secondary? Practice squad candidates The Patriots will finalize their initial 53-man roster by Sunday at 6 p.m. ET. The roster movement doesn’t stop as they will need to make space for any awarded waiver claims and then begin the process of putting together their 16 player practice squad. New England’s developmental squad will primarily be built by players they have released over the last two days that clear waivers, which includes wide receiver Kyle Dixon, who impressed in the preseason finale hauling in all eight of his targets for 71 yards. Dixon could be joined by fellow wideouts Nick DeGennaro and/or Cameron Dorner. Among the other players to watch are offensive lineman Jacob Rizy and Mehki Butler, linebacker Riley Wilson and safety Peter Manuma. Lonesome Drake Maye As the Patriots released cornerback Marcellas Dial Jr. on Saturday, Drake Maye is now the only remaining member of the 2024 draft class. The team had previously traded the only other member of that draft class to make it to 2026, offensive lineman Caedan Wallace, to the Dolphins. From the 2022 to 2024 NFL Drafts, the Patriots have just four total players remaining — Maye, wide receiver DeMario Douglas, punter Bryce Baringer, and cornerback Marcus Jones. For a team that lacks depth, as admitted by head coach Mike Vrabel after the preseason game versus the Eagles, that is a the top reason why. Salary cap considerations Saturday’s cuts did little to change New England’s salary-cap picture, as most of the players released or waived were carrying minimum-salary contracts, with several not counting toward the team’s top-51 cap number. Perhaps the most notable change was replacing Hassan Haskins’ $1.145 million cap charge with that of trade acquisition Corey Kiner, who carries a $1.005 million charge. In total, the Patriots still have more than $30 million in cap space, giving them plenty of flexibility moving forward. 20 cuts to go The Patriots released/waived 19 players on Friday night and Saturday, leaving their current roster at 73 players. They must make at least 20 more cuts by Sunday at 6 p.m. ET to get down to 53 players. In order to stay on top of all the latest cuts and releases, please make sure to regularly visit our Patriots roster cuts tracker .

The organization announced the release of Hassan Haskins and have since cut JaMycal Hasty, per a Saturday report from Patriots on SI’s Ethan Hurwitz. Both running backs had signed ahead of […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: Hassan Haskins #26 of the New England Patriots runs the ball during the second quarter of a preseason game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images After acquiring Corey Kiner from the Arizona Cardinals on the eve of the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline, the New England Patriots thinned the backfield. The organization announced the release of Hassan Haskins and have since cut JaMycal Hasty, per a Saturday report from Patriots on SI’s Ethan Hurwitz . Both running backs had signed ahead of the preseason opener after visiting Gillette Stadium for workouts. Haskins, 26, entered the NFL with head coach Mike Vrabel’s former Tennessee Titans in the fourth round of the 2022 draft at pick No. 131 overall. The past first-team All-Big Ten selection out of Michigan was claimed off waivers by the Los Angeles Chargers in 2024 and stands with 76 carries for 229 yards, 18 catches for 119 yards, three touchdowns and one start in his career. Through 371 snaps on offense and 683 snaps on special teams, the 6-foot-2, 228-pound back has handled 30 tackles and 28 kickoff returns. Hasty, 29, broke into the league as an undrafted free agent in 2020. The 5-foot-8, 205-pound Baylor product was picked up by the San Francisco 49ers and climbed from the practice squad to the active roster while in the NFC West. Stops with the Jacksonville Jaguars and Miami Dolphins have been accrued since then. As have stops in Foxborough through three coaching staffs, beginning as a waiver claim in 2023. Now 56 games in, Hasty’s career includes 854 yards and six touchdowns across 181 touches from scrimmage. He has also returned 26 kickoffs. As starters Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson looked on, the pair of vested veterans led the team rushing during the preseason finale against the Cleveland Browns. But the depth chart has gone on to gain a No. 3 option in exchange for a 2028 seventh-round draft pick. The reigning AFC champions made 15 reported cuts to begin the weekend. The NFL’s cutdown deadline is set for Sunday at 6 p.m. ET.

title: What the Corey Kiner trade means for the Patriots
summary: The New England Patriots are in a trade-happy mood. Less than a week after sending wide receiver Kayshon Boutte to Houston, the reigning AFC champions have made another move: acquiring running back Corey Kiner in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals. In New England, the 24-year-old will join a running back group that is settled […]
full_text: CANTON, OHIO - AUGUST 06: Corey Kiner #37 of the Arizona Cardinals carries the ball during the fourth quarter of the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame Game against the Carolina Panthers at Tom Benson Hall Of Fame Stadium on August 06, 2026 in Canton, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The New England Patriots are in a trade-happy mood. Less than a week after sending wide receiver Kayshon Boutte to Houston , the reigning AFC champions have made another move: acquiring running back Corey Kiner in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals. In New England, the 24-year-old will join a running back group that is settled at the top but far less so further down the depth chart. With that said, let’s find out what it means for the Patriots from a big-picture perspective. New RB3 Coming out of their preseason finale in Cleveland, the Patriots had six running backs on their roster. Besides roster locks Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson, they also had the quartet of Lan Larison, Jam Miller, Hassan Haskins and JaMycal Hasty under contract. The expectation, naturally, was that the primary backup behind Stevenson and Henderson would be coming from that second group of players. With Kiner now on the team, that might not be the case. While adding him to the mix is not guaranteed to cost all four of Larison, Miller, Haskins and Hasty their jobs, it certainly muddies the outlook for them. Fact is, after all, that the newest addition to the room is a quasi-lock to be on the initial 53-man roster. The question then becomes just how deep the group will go, especially given the questions about depth elsewhere. When we look at the position solely from a in-and-out perspective, however, Kiner very much is the current RB3: his roster outlook, at least for the moment, is far more settled than that of any other back not named Stevenson or Henderson. Bruiser at running back Standing at under 5-foot-9 and 209 pounds, Kiner is not the most physically imposing running back. That being said, his game is a powerful one that allows him to find success between the tackles. To quote Dan Brugler’s 2025 draft guide , The Beast : Kiner is a leverage-based runner who is more powerful than he looks and consistently makes the first man miss (No. 4 in the FBS with 82 forced missed tackles in 2024). Despite lacking top-tier athletic traits, he has a natural feel for run angles to use his blocking and set up defenders. Overall, Kiner is a compactly built tackle breaker. He won’t impress with speed or burst, but his balance through contact will be his NFL ticket. Proving himself on passing downs will help his chances of making a roster. With seventh-round rookie Jam Miller limited in practice this week and not suiting up for the preseason finale, New England now adds a player with a similar profile — and one who might end up replacing the rookie on the 53-man roster when all is said and done. Of course, that would still potentially leave New England short of a traditional receiving back. Special teams factor A bell-cow runner during his college career, particularly his two seasons as a starter in Cincinnati, Kiner saw only limited special teams snaps. The same has been true since his move to the NFL, with one notable exception: both the 49ers and the Cardinals have opted to use him as a kickoff return option. His output was still limited — one return each in preseason and regular season for 17 and 22 yards, respectively — but it shows that teams see something to build on. The Patriots are not only in need of better running back depth, of course, but also do not have a clear No. 1 kickoff return either. They have tried Lan Larison, Hassan Haskins and wideout Kyle Williams, among others, but nobody seems to clearly edged out the competition thus far. Maybe Kiner’s presence will shake up the group. Kayshon Boutte trade completed We started by referencing the Kayshon Boutte trade, and we’ll close with it as well. Acquiring Kiner, after all, put a wrap on that particular transaction. To recap: the Patriots sent their former starting X-receiver to the Texans and got two assets in return. One was safety Jaylen Reed, a potential foundational piece in the secondary; the other was a seventh-round selection in the 2028 NFL Draft. It was that specific pick that has now changed hands again. After previously already going from New Orleans to Houston and then to New England, it now belongs to the Cardinals. This, effectively, means that the Patriots turned Boutte into two players: Reed and Kiner.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Instant grade for Corey Kiner trade between Patriots and Cardinals
summary: While the New England Patriots are in the process of trimming their roster from previously 91 to 53 players, they also took time to bolster their depth at one position. Corey Kiner, a second-year running back who most recently played in Arizona, has been acquired via trade. To get the 24-year-old aboard, the Patriots are […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - DECEMBER 07: Corey Kiner #37 of the Arizona Cardinals warms up against the Los Angeles Rams during the NFL 2025 game at State Farm Stadium on December 07, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the New England Patriots are in the process of trimming their roster from previously 91 to 53 players, they also took time to bolster their depth at one position. Corey Kiner, a second-year running back who most recently played in Arizona, has been acquired via trade . To get the 24-year-old aboard, the Patriots are sending a 2028 seventh-round draft pick to the Cardinals. Let’s put a grade on the move based on the information we have available. Patriots’ Corey Kiner trade with Cardinals, graded Bernd Buchmasser: It has become quite obvious this summer that the Patriots were not happy with their running back depth. With only so many viable options available, however, using a minor draft choice two years into the future is not the worst investment in the world. Is it a “throw it on the wall and see if it sticks” kind of trade? Yes, but even if he does not pan out there is really no harm done. | Grade: C Matt St. Jean: After months of discussion of who would win the RB3 battle in New England, the answer is apparently “none of the above”. With 2026 seventh-rounder Jam Miller not being the answer, the Patriots moved one of their 2028 seventh-round picks for a former UDFA with 58 career rushing yards. It’s not ideal asset management, but we’re also talking about seventh-round picks and third-string running backs, so this isn’t a high stakes situation. Hopefully, Kiner provides sufficient depth behind what should be one of the top running back tandems in football. | Grade: C- Pat Lane: If you’re wondering, “Who the heck is Corey Kiner?” I hope you didn’t come here for answers. Kiner has bounced around the league after being signed as a UDFA by the 49ers last year. He’s small, at only 5-foot-9 and isn’t very fast, but he is decently powerful. It seems that the Patriots wanted a power back behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson, and they get it with Kiner. Whether or not they keep a fourth back will be interesting to see, but clearly they weren’t happy with the depth they currently had on the roster. I’m not sure if it was bad enough to trade for a guy that no one has ever heard of, but I’ve certainly been wrong before. | Grade: D- What do you think about the Kiner trade? Do you like it? Do you not? Please participate in our poll and head to the comment section below to explain your thinking.

title: Patriots make first reported cuts ahead of 53-man roster deadline
summary: Coming out of their preseason finale and heading into the weekend, the New England Patriots had an active roster of 91 players. With the cutdown deadline looming, they have started trimming that number. The team started by informing 16 players of their release. Wide receivers Kyle Dixon, Nick DeGennaro and Cameron Dorner, tight end C.J. […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Kyle Dixon #83 of the New England Patriots runs against the Philadelphia Eagles during an NFL preseason football game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Coming out of their preseason finale and heading into the weekend, the New England Patriots had an active roster of 91 players. With the cutdown deadline looming, they have started trimming that number. The team started by informing 16 players of their release . Wide receivers Kyle Dixon, Nick DeGennaro and Cameron Dorner, tight end C.J. Dippre, offensive tackle Lorenz Metz, interior offensive linemen Darrian Dalcourt, Jacob Rizy, JonDarius Morgan and Mehki Butler, outside linebackers Xavier Holmes, Amari Gainer and Jesse Luketa, cornerbacks Brandon Crossley and Marcellas Dial Jr., and safety Peter Manuma have all been waived, according to multiple reports. In addition, the team waived safety Eric Butler with an injury designation. Dixon, 25, started his college career as a baseball player before returning to the gridiron with Culver-Stockton in 2024. In two seasons and 22 games with the Wildcats, he caught 143 passes for 2,394 yards and 24 touchdowns. A two-time first-team All-HAAC selection, he went unselected in this year’s draft. Joining the Patriots as a rookie free agent in May, he caught a team-leading 10 passes for 81 yards in the preseason. DeGennaro, 25, played college football at Maryland, Richmond and James Madison. Despite his experience and a 4.40-second 40-yard dash, he took the free agency route to the NFL and New England specifically. A depth option throughout the summer, he ended up playing in three preseason games and caught five passes for 65 yards and a touchdown. Dorner, 22, began his college career at Division II Shepherd University before a one-year stint at North Texas. Despite some solid production in his lone season in Division I, he was not selected in this year’s draft. He joined the Patriots as a UDFA, and in three preseason games caught four passes for 37 yards. Dippre, 24, spent his college career at Alabama before arriving in New England as a rookie free agent last offseason. Initially a practice squad player, he was promoted to the 53-man roster in November to prevent other teams from poaching him. He eventually finished the year on the active team and played a combined 46 snaps on offense and special teams over his two in-game appearances. Dippre started this year’s training camp on the PUP list, and caught two preseason passes for 21 yards after his return. Metz, 29, started his football career at the amateur level in Germany. He later played college football in Cincinnati and through stints with the Bears and Buccaneers found his way to New England in 2025. An exempt practice squad player due to his international status, he was re-signed by the team in the offseason and carried on the roster as a 91st player. Dalcourt, 25, also played college football at Alabama. He joined the Ravens as a rookie free agent in 2024 and via subsequent stints in Washington, Carolina and Cleveland made his way to New England. He played 25 offensive snaps over his two preseason appearances as a Patriot. Rizy, 24, spent his six-year college career at Harvard and Florida State, where he started 27 total games and saw action all over the offensive line. He ultimately did not get selected in the 2026 NFL Draft, but made his way to Foxborough shortly thereafter. Serving as the Patriots’ third-string center, he played 155 preseason snaps and started the finale against the Browns. Morgan, 23, entered the NFL off of college stints at South Carolina and UAB. The rookie free agent signing ended up appearing in three of the Patriots’ preseason games, but was on the field for only 40 combined snaps as a third-string option at guard. Mehki Butler, 25, joined the Patriots as an undrafted free agent in 2025 after attending rookie minicamp on a tryout basis. The guard by way of Iowa Western and Arkansas State had previously been waived at the 53-man deadline last summer. He went on to spend the bulk of the Super Bowl LX run on the practice squad and was retained on a futures contract in February. Holmes, 24, split his college career between Maine and James Madison. He did not hear his name called in this year’s draft and instead joined the Patriots as a rookie free agent two weeks later. While he did show some flashes early in camp, an undisclosed injury has kept him out for the last few weeks and prevented him from appearing in any preseason games. Gainer, 26, played at Florida State and North Carolina before joining the Raiders as a rookie free agent in 2024. He arrived in New England during the 2025 season as a practice squad player and was later signed to a futures contract for 2026. He provided edge depth during the summer and registered one sack in three preseason contests. Luketa, 27, signed a futures contract in Foxborough ahead of the 2026 league year in March. The veteran outside linebacker entered the NFL with the Cardinals in the seventh round of the 2022 draft and spent time last campaign on the Rams’ practice squad. A Penn State product, he has appeared in 31 career games, including three starts, en route to 35 tackles, three sacks and one forced fumble. Crossley, 25, spent six years in college. The Colorado State and SMU product, who was an All-ACC honorable mention in his final season, did not hear his name called in the 2025 NFL Draft. He signed with the Patriots as a free agent shortly thereafter and spent his rookie campaign on and off their practice squad without seeing any game action. He was brought back this year as a depth piece at cornerback. Dial Jr, 25, played college football at Georgia Military and South Carolina. He was then selected in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft by the Patriots and remained the last player from that class alongside Drake Maye. He is being let go with 17 in-game appearances and one start to his name, all coming during his rookie season. This summer, he served as a depth nickel back. Manuma, 24, was named honorable mention All-Mountain West in each of his four seasons at Hawaii. He nonetheless went unselected in this year’s draft, and had to wait until after a tryout at Patriots rookie minicamp to sign a contract. Seeing action on defense and special teams in three preseason games, he registered two tackles. Eric Butler, 23, went unselected in this year’s draft and earned rookie minicamp invitations with the Raiders and Saints. The San Diego State product remained unsigned until arriving in New England in early August, however. If he clears waivers, he will revert to the Patriots’ injured reserve list. With the initial wave now reported, plus a trade , New England’s roster stands in the 70s. The team will have to move below the league-mandated 53-man threshold by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, Aug. 30.

He later spent time on the practice squads in both Minnesota and Arizona, appearing in four games for the Cardinals during his rookie regular season. The 5-foot-9, 209-pound runner has a combined 12 carries for 58 yards on his NFL résumé. He also two passes for 15 yards and has run one kickoff back 22 yards. Now a Patriot, Kiner slots in the third running back spot behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson. The team had looked for a viable RB3 throughout the summer, with Lan Larison, Jam Miller, Hassan Haskins and JaMycal Hasty the options currently on the roster. The trade for Kiner comes in the middle of New England having started the process of trimming its roster . title: Game Recap: Saints visit Cowboys in preseason finale
summary: The New Orleans Saints were looking to bounce back after being shut out by the Los Angeles Rams when they faced the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Friday night. Here’s a recap of all the action from the black and gold’s final preseason game. First Quarter Spencer Rattler started at quarterback for New Orleans […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Spencer Rattler #2 of the New Orleans Saints runs with the ball toward the endzone during the second quarter of the 2026 NFL preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints were looking to bounce back after being shut out by the Los Angeles Rams when they faced the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Friday night. Here’s a recap of all the action from the black and gold’s final preseason game. First Quarter Spencer Rattler started at quarterback for New Orleans and converted each of his first two passes for 15 yards as the Saints quickly entered Dallas territory on the opening drive. But the visitors were soon held to a field goal attempt, which Daniel Carlson converted from 38 yards. With Joe Milton starting at quarterback, the Cowboys quickly had a field goal of their own. Brandon Aubrey converted from 49 yards to level the game at 3-3. Rattler returned and continued to complete passes on the ensuing drive, though the bulk of the work was done on the ground through Audric Estime and Kendre Miller. But it was rookie receiver Barion Brown who ran in for a 7-yard score to cap off a 10-play, 71-yard touchdown drive for the Saints, restoring their advantage at 10-3. Milton and the Cowboys offense found themselves instantly in a third-and-long as they returned to the field. But the quarterback was able to extend the drive with a 27-yard pass to Camden Brown. Second Quarter Dallas was soon in another third-and-long situation, but this time had to settle for a field goal. Aubrey converted from 51 yards. Rattler found Estime for 13 yards as the Saints’ ensuing possession began positively. However, the black and gold were eventually forced to punt. The Cowboys offense responded with another decent possession. The highlight of the drive was Milton’s connection with Marquez Valdes-Scantling for 22 yards. But a 57-yard field goal attempt from Aubrey went wide right, and the score remained 10-6. Despite being sacked on the opening play of the next drive, Rattler and the Saints offense came back with a touchdown. A 4th-down run from CJ Donaldson preceded a 33-yard dash by Estime to set up 1st-and-goal, and it was Rattler himself who ran it in from 8 yards for the score. Milton converted all three of his passes on the next drive as Dallas looked for a quick response, but a holding penalty limited Dallas’ momentum. Aubrey was good from 58 yards this time. Third Quarter Sam Howell entered at quarterback for the hosts, and they went three-and-out to begin the half. Meanwhile, Zach Wilson entered for the Saints and completed his first pass to Ronnie Bell for 23 yards. The Saints’ running backs continued to move the ball effectively, and a 13-yard connection from Wilson to Donaldson set up an 11-yard touchdown run from Zamir White to put the black and gold up 24-9. The teams proceeded to exchange punts. As Dallas’ offense returned to the field, Howell found Jordan Hudson for 52 yards on the opening play of the drive. Fourth Quarter Howell then found Hudson again for a 26-yard touchdown pass, with the extra point pulling the Cowboys within one score of their visitors. The Saints then went three-and-out before Dallas came back with a 12-play, 67-yard touchdown drive highlighted by a 21-yard grab in the end zone by Mitch Van Vooren for the score. A successful two-point conversion attempt levelled the game at 24-24. With 6 minutes to play, Wilson and the Saints offense grabbed their opportunity to restore the lead. Wilson was 4/4 for 38 yards on what turned out to be the game-winning drive, and Carlson nailed his 53-yard field goal attempt after the two-minute warning. Trailing 27-24, Howell threw four straight incompletions as the Cowboys turned it over on downs. Wilson knelt out the clock to secure the win for the black and gold, their first of the preseason. Next up is the regular season, with a visit to Detroit on September 13th kicking things off for New Orleans.
