title: Final Saints 53-man roster prediction
summary: We are finally done with preseason, and less than two weeks away from the beginning of the regular season. For the New Orleans Saints, this was a pretty busy training camp with position battles sprinkled throughout the team. Many of these battles did not have clear winners, but the Saints still must figure out who […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Head coach Kellen Moore of the New Orleans Saints watches action prior to an NFL Preseason 2026 game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are finally done with preseason, and less than two weeks away from the beginning of the regular season. For the New Orleans Saints, this was a pretty busy training camp with position battles sprinkled throughout the team. Many of these battles did not have clear winners, but the Saints still must figure out who they want to bring in for the season, and here is my attempt to do that. QB (2): Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler This was such an interesting position battle because Zach Wilson did look like the better QB in game 1, but it went back to square 1 after game 2. It was such a bad performance by both QBs that any momentum was destroyed. Then, in game 3, Rattler did look like the better QB, and I think the Saints might just go with what they’re comfortable with. RB (5): Travis Etienne, Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller, Audric Estime, and Zamir White Devin Neal on the IR The RBs became such an interesting situation due to the injuries, but hopefully, mostly everyone will be healthy for Game 1. Alvin Kamara’s availability is a bit up in the air, so if he hits the IR, I can see this group only being 4 players, and I do see Devin Neal on the IR. I think, given the injury luck this season, bringing 5 guys makes sense, and all of them did really well in game 3 of the preseason. WR (5): Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele, Barion Brown, Bryce Lance, and Kevin Austin Jr. Jordyn Tyson on IR In this group, I originally had 6 spots filled, but with Jordyn Tyson on IR, I think the Saints are only bringing 5 players as of now. I think the decision comes down to Kevin Austin Jr. or Bub Means, and although Means has done well, the staff really seems to like Austin Jr. TE (3): Juwan Johnson, Noah Fant, and Oscar Delp Nothing really changes here, especially with Moliki Matavao out for the season. OL (9): Kelvin Banks Jr., David Edwards, Erik McCoy, Cesar Ruiz, Taliese Fuaga, Jeremiah Wright, Easton Kilty, William Sherman, and Asim Richards The starters for this group are the same, but the depth is nearly the opposite of my expectations. Jeremiah Wright just kept improving each game and had a really good performance against the Cowboys. Starting might not be out of the question this season. His spot was expected. Behind him, Easton Kilty is a decent depth player with potential, William Sherman took over the backup center role, and Asim Richards is just tackle depth. Although I do think the Saints could move on from Richards, a player would need to be coming in before that happens. DE (6): Chase Young, Carl Granderson, Cam Jordan, Anfernee Jennings, Tyree Wilson, and Michael Heldman Nothing changes for this group in my prediction. I already believed the Saints would bring 6 edge rushers onto the 53-man roster, and I do think that happens. Wilson had a quiet offseason, but made some plays in the last preseason game. For Heldman, he had some shining moments throughout the entire preseason and got some really good pressures/sacks. The Saints should not risk letting him go. DT (6): Christen Miller, Vernon Broughton, Nathan Shepherd, Davon Godchaux, John Ridgeway III, and Myles Cole A lot has changed here due to injuries and some releases, which is why I think the Saints also bring 6 players here. That extra spot was either going to Myles Cole or Jay’Viar Suggs, and it was difficult to choose, but I ended up going with Cole. LB (5): Kaden Elliss, Pete Werner, Danny Stutsman, Isaiah Stalbird, and Jaylan Ford It’s going to be very interesting to see if the Saints bring 5 or 4 LBs onto the 53-man roster, but with how Ford has done in training camp and preseason, he must be in consideration. For my prediction, I do think the Saints bring him, especially with this room being a bit of a worry going into the season. CB (4): Kool-Aid McKinstry, Quincy Riley, Martin Emerson, and Jayden Price Do I like bringing only 4 corners? Absolutely not, but who else has proven themselves to get onto the roster? Price and Emerson have struggled at times, but have also made really good plays. They are good depth to have if an injury occurs and on special teams. The one surprise player on the outside is Isaac Yiadom, but his preseason was not good. S (5): Justin Reid, Jonas Sanker, Julian Blackmon, Jordan Howden, and Lorenzo Styles Jr. Styles is injured, and if he starts on the IR, I could see the Saints bring someone else in this group, but I do think he could be good to go. Styles Jr. has shown the ability to bounce back from injury, and roster-wise, will be a major contributor on special teams. ST (3): Daniel Carlson, Ryan Wright, and Zach Wood Well, I didn’t think Daniel Carlson would be in New Orleans, but here we are. He clearly won the competition against the Cowboys, hitting the game-winning FG and being perfect on the day.

title: Ups and downs: Saints vs. Cowboys
summary: Up: QB2 battle Spencer Rattler and Zach Wilson each had significantly better days on Friday night after, to say it nicely, terrible showings against the Los Angeles Rams. Rattler finished the day completing 8-of-his-10 pass attempts for 79 yards. Rattler also logged an 8-yard rushing touchdown. Wilson had a solid day as well, completing 9/12 […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Spencer Rattler #2 of the New Orleans Saints participates in warmups prior to an NFL Preseason 2026 game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Up: QB2 battle Spencer Rattler and Zach Wilson each had significantly better days on Friday night after, to say it nicely, terrible showings against the Los Angeles Rams. Rattler finished the day completing 8-of-his-10 pass attempts for 79 yards. Rattler also logged an 8-yard rushing touchdown. Wilson had a solid day as well, completing 9/12 passes for 93 yards. The decision on QB2 will be important, but not an easy choice. Wilson looked great in the team’s preseason debut, but Rattler has slowly fought back. No matter who earns the job, strong showings from each of the young passers give the team more confidence heading into the regular season. Up: Run game New Orleans had a better day running the ball in the win against the Cowboys after struggling against the Rams and Jacksonville Jaguars. The Saints ended the day with 169 rushing yards and 3 touchdowns, averaging 5.9 yards per carry. While the running backs did have a good day, it was Rattler and wide receiver Barion Brown who first added to the team’s rushing touchdown total, before newly acquired Zamir White was the first running back to find the end zone. Kendre Miller continued his strong preseason showing, rushing for 42 yards on 9 attempts. Audric Estime continued his push to make the 53-man roster, adding 46 yards on the ground on 4 carries, including a 33-yard rush. Finally, White added 23 yards on 4 carries. The run game will be a big factor for the Saints in the upcoming season, and their lack of a run game during the preseason has been a concern. With Kellen Moore calling plays on Friday, the black and gold’s run game looked significantly better. Up: K Daniel Carlson The Saints added veteran kicker Daniel Carlson to their kicker battle after Charlie Smyth and Tanner Brown struggled and became inconsistent throughout training camp and the preseason. Carlson has been an established kicker in the NFL over the years and looks to be the favorite to win the job for New Orleans. Carlson opened up scoring for the Saints on the opening drive, making a 38-yard field goal. With less than two minutes remaining, New Orleans looked to the veteran kicker on a 53-yard attempt to give the Saints the lead. Carlson nailed the kick and may have locked up the starting job. Down: Pass defense While they started strong, the Saints’ pass defense was poor on Friday. Cowboys quarterbacks finished the day 20/33 for 237 yards and 2 touchdowns. This follows the Saints’ poor performance against the Rams, when they allowed 254 yards. The Cowboys’ passing offense mostly came alive when Sam Howell took over. The veteran passer ended the day 12/18 for 155 yards and 2 touchdowns for a 130.6 passer rating. Saints defensive backs weren’t terrible, and it was usually better throws than it was bad defense, but a consecutive week of failing to stop the passer raises concern for New Orleans’ secondary depth. The Saints also logged just two sacks after failing to take down a quarterback against Los Angeles. With a lack of a pass rush and struggles in the secondary, there remains a bit of a concern over defensive depth going into the regular season. Down: Injuries The injury list grew in Friday’s win, with linebacker Jaylan Ford, pass rusher Michael Heldman, and Estime leaving the game and not returning. New Orleans has dealt with a laundry list of injuries during training camp, and it unfortunately continued in their preseason finale. The most important part coming out of training camp and preseason is remaining healthy, and the Saints haven’t been able to do that. With more Saints being kept out of practices and games, injuries were the black and gold’s biggest enemy throughout the preseason.

title: NFL 2026 Waiver Wire Rules and Order
summary: All NFL teams are now in the process of reducing their rosters to 53 players and while those rosters are never final, the number stands pat at 53. Teams will now play musical chairs with players signing some to their practice squad and claiming some off of waivers. For those unfamiliar with the process, the […]
full_text: METAIRIE, LOUISIANA - JULY 30: A detailed view of a New Orleans Saints Helmet during training camp at Ochsner Sports Performance Center on July 30, 2026 in Metairie, Louisiana. (Photo by Tyler Kaufman/Getty Images) | Getty Images All NFL teams are now in the process of reducing their rosters to 53 players and while those rosters are never final, the number stands pat at 53. Teams will now play musical chairs with players signing some to their practice squad and claiming some off of waivers. For those unfamiliar with the process, the NFL waiver wire is a 24‑hour process for teams to claim players waived from their teams, with priority set by a fixed priority order that decides which team gets a waived player if more than one team submits a claim. In that scenario, the team highest in the waiver order is awarded the player. Waiver order from now through Week 3 is based on that year’s original NFL Draft order. (Any trades that are made in the draft are not taken into account) What are the waiver wire rules? The 53-man cutdown deadline is 5 p.m. CT on Sunday, August 30 after which time every NFL team must be at 53 players. Rosters will be reduced from 90 players to 53 players, which means each team makes 37 cuts. Waiver claims clear at 12 p.m. CT on Monday, August 31. Vested veterans (played four or more accrued seasons) are not subject to waivers and become free agents immediately; players with fewer seasons must clear waivers first. Teams can start signing player to their practice squads, which can hold up to 16 players, or 17 with the International Player designation. What is the waiver wire order? Hodgins, Bankston, Jaimes, and Fotu, in particular are interesting. Hodgins, as Giants fans are well aware, was a key piece for the Giants’ playoff run in 2022. title: Why did the NY Giants trade for C.J. Okoye? John Harbaugh explains
summary: It was clear throughout the preseason that the New York Giants needed additional depth along the interior of their defensive line. The Giants got some on Saturday when they traded a 2028 seventh-round pick for C.J. Okoye, a 6-foot-6, 365-pound 24-year-old who played for Harbaugh last season with the Baltimore Ravens. Why did the Giants […]
full_text: C.J. Okoye | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It was clear throughout the preseason that the New York Giants needed additional depth along the interior of their defensive line. The Giants got some on Saturday when they traded a 2028 seventh-round pick for C.J. Okoye , a 6-foot-6, 365-pound 24-year-old who played for Harbaugh last season with the Baltimore Ravens. Why did the Giants make the deal? “He’s a guy that we got to know recently last year, came in, was with the Chargers actually with my brother [Jim] for a couple years in the international program,” Harbaugh said. “So a guy who had been developmental type guy, learning the game and tremendous physical skills, hard worker, has really dedicated himself over the last few years to learning the game really because he didn’t play it growing up and made great strides, made great strides with Dennis Johnson, our defensive line coach last year. That’s where he kind of broke through and had a really good season.” How will Okoye be used? “We see him as an inside defender, a defensive tackle, A gap, B gap player, run stopper, pocket pusher in terms of the past game and just a really a real big physical player,” Harbaugh said. “So kind of a type of guy we’ve been looking for and we’re really excited to get him up here.” Harbaugh said the Giants are “still looking” for defensive tackle help, but that “I don’t want to rule out anything else either. It’s not like we aren’t looking everywhere.” Harbaugh added that the Giants are both getting and making calls, but called it “the usual due diligence.” NFL teams have to reach the 53-man regular-season roster limit by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

full_text: Bobby Okereke | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Former New York Giants linebacker Bobby Okereke , released by the Giants in March, has finally found a new team. Okereke is signing with the Carolina Panthers . Okereke signed a four-year, $40 million contract with the Giants before the 2023 season. Okereke had a career-year in 2023, with 149 tackles, 10 passes defensed, 2.5 sacks, 2 interceptions, and four forced fumbles in Wink Martindale’s defense. He missed five games in 2024 due to a back injury, and was not nearly as productive the past two seasons. The 30-year-old Okereke is a former Giants team captain and Walter Payton Man of the Year Award nominee. The Giants have rebuilt their linebacking corps with the 6-foot-4, 251-pound veteran Tremaine Edmunds and 6-4, 243-pound No. 5 overall pick Arvell Reese. Okereke, 6-2, 235 is a good player, but not the thumper or physical presence that Edmunds and Reese are. title: NY Giants fans believe Big Blue will surge in 2026
summary: It wasn’t a foregone conclusion that John Harbaugh would choose the New York Giants on the 2026 head coaching carousel. While the Giants were the first and most aggressive team to pursue him, Harbaugh had nearly a third of the NFL as suitors — including several teams that weren’t nearly as bad in 2025 as […]
full_text: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh smiles after the Giants’ victory over the New York Jets. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It wasn’t a foregone conclusion that John Harbaugh would choose the New York Giants on the 2026 head coaching carousel. While the Giants were the first and most aggressive team to pursue him, Harbaugh had nearly a third of the NFL as suitors — including several teams that weren’t nearly as bad in 2025 as the 4-13 Giants. But when Harbaugh agreed to become the Giants’ next head coach, part of the reason was because he believed they were much better than their record suggested. Harbaugh had little interest in a full-blown rebuild after being fired by the Ravens and believes that the Giants have a core of talent that would allow them to compete this year . Most of the national media scoffed at the idea that the Giants could surpass mediocrity and be a real factor in the playoff hunt. But the Giants — and Giants fans — have bought in. After a month of training camp and preseason games, we asked the Big Blue View community how many more games you believe the Giants will win in 2026 than in 2025. It may be Optimism Season speaking, but fans think Harbaugh is right and the Giants could well be in postseason contention this year. A full 88 percent of the Big Blue View community believes that the Giants will win at least 8 games this year, with more than half fans believing that the team will win at least 10 games in 2026. That might seem like wild-eyed optimism considering the Giants have only won 7 games in the last two years put together. However, it’s a more measured improvement if Harbaugh is right that the Giants are a better team than their win-loss total says they are. Earlier this week, Bill Barnwell wrote that the Giants — along with teams like the Ravens, Lions, and Chiefs — are among the five most likely teams to improve this year . His argument is that the way in which the Giants lost last year makes them a historic outlier and their point differential suggests a 7-10 team rather a 4-13 team. That argument mirrors Harbaugh’s assessment from his own tape study before agreeing to terms with the Giants. The Giants had the talent to compete with good teams last year, but situational football, injuries, and poor coaching decisions snatched defeat from the jaws of victory too many times. From that perspective, doubling the Giants’ win total would only constitute a modest 1-game improvement over what they should have been a year before. A 6-game improvement would mean a 3-game improvement over what their point differential suggests they should have been in 2025. And considering all the off-season additions the Giants have made compared to their 2025 season, is an 8 or 10-win season that unrealistic? After all, the Giants will have: HC John Harbaugh and DC Dennard Wilson TE Isaiah Likely (free agent) LB Tremaine Edmunds (free agent) WR Darnell Mooney (free agent) RB Najee Harris (free agent) CB Greg Newsome II (free agent) S Ar’Darius Washington (free agent) FB Patrick Ricard (free agent) P Jordan Stout (free agent) WR Malik Nabers (returning from injury) RB Cam Skattebo (returning from injury) EDGE Kayvon Thibodeaux (returning from injury) LB Arvell Reese (5th overall pick) OG Sisi Mauigoa (10th overall pick) CB Colton Hood (37th overall pick) WR Malachi Fields (74th overall pick) Not to mention another year of development for QB Jaxson Dart , EDGE Abdul Carter , and CB Deonte Banks . We’ll see whether the optimism is borne out in the regular season. But if Harbaugh (and Giants fans) are right, the 7.5-game over/under ( per FanDuel ) is significantly underestimating the Giants. Likewise, if the Giants exceed their expected over/under by that much, John Harbaugh should be the runaway favorite for AP Coach Of The Year — he’s currently the preseason frontrunner at +650 (also per FanDuel). It may be optimism season, but Giants fans might have real reason to be optimistic this year.

title: NY Giants trade for Baltimore Ravens’ DT to bolster run defense
summary: The New York Giants are trading for Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle C.J. Okoye, per a report from Mike Garafolo of the NFL Network. The Giants are sending a 2028 seventh-round pick to the Ravens. It was widely expected that the Giants would make moves to reinforce an interior defensive line that has been a weakness […]
full_text: Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle C.J. Okoye | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants are trading for Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle C.J. Okoye , per a report from Mike Garafolo of the NFL Network. The Giants are sending a 2028 seventh-round pick to the Ravens. It was widely expected that the Giants would make moves to reinforce an interior defensive line that has been a weakness throughout the summer and preseason. It makes sense that their first move would be to acquire a player that not only has rare traits but is also familiar to John Harbaugh. Okoye played for John Harbaugh in 2025 with the Ravens after playing for Jim Harbaugh as an international pathway player (originally from Nigeria) for the Los Angeles Chargers in 2023 and 2024. His experience with John Harbaugh isn’t Okoye’s only link to the Giants, and Okoye came into the International Pathway Program at the insistence of Giants’ great Osi Umenyiora . Okoye, 24, is a massive defensive tackle, listed at 6-foot-6, 365 pounds. That said, he also has impressive physical traits, with surprising movement skills for such an enormous young man. Okoye played in 13 games for the Ravens last season, making 15 tackles in 214 defensive snaps. He’s still learning the game of football, as well as how to use his formidable tools. Okoye’s first organized game of football was his first preseason game for the Chargers in 2023, a game in which he also got his first sack . Former teammate Morgan Fox (Chargers’ defensive tackle) said in 2024 that Okoye was only just “starting to figure out football, which is terrifying.” Okoye had been listed as a second-string defensive tackle for the Ravens, which is significant considering the Ravens have ESPN’s second-ranked defensive tackle group . He’s also been a part of one of the NFL’s best preseason run defenses, and is coming off of a strong game against the Washington Commanders with a tackle, QB hit, and a fumble recovery.

title: New York Giants mailbag: Deonte Banks, roster size, more questions
summary: Adam Jacobs asks: Like all Giants fans, I am very excited about the coming season. I have a question about Banks. Everyone knows about his struggles the past two seasons, as well as the encouraging signs since the start of training camp. Is his (perceived) improvement more about a change back to a press, man-to-man defense, […]
full_text: Adam Jacobs asks: Like all Giants fans, I am very excited about the coming season. I have a question about Banks. Everyone knows about his struggles the past two seasons, as well as the encouraging signs since the start of training camp. Is his (perceived) improvement more about a change back to a press, man-to-man defense, a change in the coaching staff, or something else? I am more than happy if they could get good production out of him beyond returning kickoffs. Do you think this is just trying to impress the coaches, or is this a turning the corner thing? Ed says: Adam, I don’t know what you are getting by asking if “this is just trying to impress the coaches.” Every player who isn’t an established star is always hoping to impress his coaches. In reference to Deonte Banks, the change in both his play and his demeanor have been real. Banks has been playing like the guy the Giants hoped he would be when they used a first-round pick on him in 2023. The change in coaching staffs and schemes has a lot to do with it. Maybe there were things going on in the young man’s life that affected him. We don’t know. Banks doesn’t like to talk to the media. When he does talk, his answers are very short. He isn’t going to tell us much. I don’t know if he will be a starter, but Banks looks like a player who can certainly contribute at cornerback. Joseph Evans asks: I know it’s most likely in the Collective Bargaining Agreement, but why is it you can only dress 45 on game day? With the amount of injuries, that doesn’t make sense to me. Ed says: Joseph, teams can dress 46. If they elevate two players from the practice squad, that number rises to 48. But, your question, of course, regards why there is any type of limit. It really has to do with competitive balance. Say one team has five injured players who cannot dress for a game. The opposing team has only two. The NFL wants each team to dress the same number of players in each game, theoretically so that one team is not at a numerical disadvantage. For me, there is a better way to accomplish this. Let teams dress 53 players for each game. If you have three players who are injured and cannot dress on your 53-man roster, teams should be allowed to activate three players from the practice squad — without needing to pass players through waivers to get them back on the practice squad. To me, full rosters would improve the quality of play. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Bob Donnelly asks: The kickoff (not kickoff coverage) is perhaps the only aspect of a preseason game that is not impacted by the other 21 players on the field. Through two preseason games how do you view this aspect of the kicker competition? Ed says: Bob, it is something we rarely see during practices. Honestly, it isn’t nearly as important as it was prior to the change in the rules that discourages touchbacks. There just isn’t enough to go on for me to say one guy is better at kickoffs than another. Spencer Gross asks: I just read your piece about JC Davis and I found it interesting about him watching and learning from Thomas. My question to you is do you know if Neal ever tried to learn from Thomas? Did Thomas ever mentor him? I’ve read you say Thomas is a stand up guy during interviews but I wonder about that dynamic between the two. Thomas is a captain so it’s evident he has leadership qualities but I’m curious about that relationship. Ed says: Spencer, I don’t really know the nature of the relationship between Neal and Thomas. Neal is in his fifth year in the league now, so he’s pretty much beyond the “mentoring” stage. I would have to believe that over the course of 4+ years that Thomas has tried to help him. Derick Gross asks: Is Nagy allowed to be on the sideline, but watch the offensive plays on a screen with a view from the booth? That way he could get the bird’s eye view of the play unfolding, but still communicate directly with players on the sideline. Ed says: No, Derick. There are tablets on the sideline, but I am not sure how quickly they show photos or replays of plays. Certainly not quickly enough to call the next play. Nagy will end up wherever he and John Harbaugh deem to be the best spot. Kölnerbigblue asks: Ed, Normally, when I hear “noncontact” injury, I think if the cleats gripping too well but Austin’s foot apparently slipped. In Germany, I have to change to winter tires come the snow season. In the grass v turf debate, I never hear people talk about the cleat configuration. Since the cleat is half of the equation, I just wonder if the NFL or NFLPA have looked into it. Is this question ever asked? Ed says: Kölner, you are looking for a problem where one doesn’t exist. It is my understanding that NFL players have about 75 varieties of cleats to choose from. Read this from nearly 10 years ago about how much goes into player footwear. Anthony Viola asks: A friend of mine saw a recent interview with the LBs (Burns, Carter, Reese, and Thibs I believe) and he came away with the impression that they were not a tight knit group of players. I was very surprised to hear this. In your opinion, based on what you see and hear, is there any truth to what my friend said? I did not see the interview so admittedly I am getting this opinion/comment second hand. Ed says: Anthony, I think that’s nonsense. The interview they did was mostly a light-hearted interview with a national media member more or less asking silly questions to get a reaction. The other thing about that interview was that the three edge players insisted that Arvell Reese be included. That’s just looking for an issue where one doesn’t exist. title: NY Giants coach John Harbaugh explains not playing Jaxson Dart vs. Jets
summary: When the New York Giants meet the Dallas Cowboys in their Sept. 13 season-opener, quarterback Jaxson Dart will not have faced live competition in 29 days. Dart played briefly in the preseason opener against the Minnesota Vikings, but has not played since. Head coach John Harbaugh considered having Dart play Friday against the New York […]
full_text: Jaxson Dart watches Friday’s game. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images When the New York Giants meet the Dallas Cowboys in their Sept. 13 season-opener, quarterback Jaxson Dart will not have faced live competition in 29 days. Dart played briefly in the preseason opener against the Minnesota Vikings, but has not played since. Head coach John Harbaugh considered having Dart play Friday against the New York Jets, but decided that playing the second-year quarterback was “not worth the risk.” As he had in the days prior to the game, Harbaugh acknowledged the concern about the layoff for Dart. “I think there is a concern, and the concern is that they won’t have played in a game for a long time,” Harbaugh said. “So, will there be a rust factor, those kinds of things. We’re just going to have to make sure we do everything we can in practice to make sure our guys are sharp and ready to go. But we just decided to go that route and probably take the more conservative route. “We just decided not to take the chance.” Harbaugh pointed out that if Dart had played, other frontline players would also have had to play. “If Jaxson plays, a lot of other guys are going to play too, and then is it worth the risk?,” Harbaugh said. “We got out of the game with no serious injuries, so that’s good, and it probably would have gone that way too, and we’d be happy and they would have gotten some reps. But we chose not to go that way, so I understand. Any criticism of it, I do understand.” Injury updates: Tyrone Tracy has a stinger Running back Tyrone Tracy passed a concussion test, but Harbaugh said he does have a stinger. Cornerback Korie Black suffered a groin injury. Harbaugh said cornerback Art Green suffered an undisclosed “minor injury.” Odell Beckham has ‘done enough’ Harbaugh stopped short of saying that Odell Beckham Jr. would make the Giants’ 53-man roster, but admitted he has “done enough” to be on an NFL team. “I don’t want to like say exactly who’s making it right now and not, what the considerations are. And things can happen,” Harbaugh said. “But I think I would answer the question yes. I mean, I think he has done enough to make an NFL roster for sure. He’s played well, and he’s gotten better as his camp’s gone along. He deserves credit for that. He’s done a really good job with it.” A new play-caller … for one night only Quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan called offensive plays vs. the Jets. No, he is not taking over that job from offensive coordinator Matt Nagy . Harbaugh said this was “standard” preseason preparation. “You never know if something happens. If Nags can’t make it to the game, gets caught in North Jersey traffic or something like that, we might need Cally to do it,” Harbaugh said. “But that was just something different. Last week we had (defensive pass coordinator/secondary coach) Donald D’Alesio call the defenses a little bit, so I think it’s a pretty standard thing to do in preseason.”

summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants get ready to name their 53 man roster. full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants get ready to name their 53 man roster. Giants by the numbers: Just how grueling was John Harbaugh’s training camp? | The Athletic The Giants have held 21 practices from the start of training camp to this point. They held 15 practices over the same stretch last year. Harbaugh’s practices have been longer, with 12 sessions lasting more than two hours. Just four of Daboll’s practices ran over two hours last year. Every coach drills situational football, but Harbaugh dedicates more time to game management — leading late, trailing late, end of half, etc. — than any of the previous four Giants coaches I’ve covered in the post-Tom Coughlin era. No stone has gone unturned by Harbaugh. The Giants have rehearsed everything from their pregame stretching routine to the victory formation. It will be shocking if the Giants aren’t effective at converting on fourth-and-1 because they’ve seemingly drilled that situation as much as any other this summer. Matt Simms impressed by Giants OC NFC East Preview: Is This the Cowboys’ Year? | The Ringer If you are a Giants fan and want to believe that this team can be frisky and compete for a wild-card spot this season, go for it. There’s a scenario in which Harbaugh shows he’s still got it, Dart is an exciting playmaker (and stays healthy), and Carter emerges as a Defensive Player of the Year candidate. But I can’t get there. Harbaugh did not look like a great coach with the Ravens last year. I need to see a lot more from Dart before believing that he can be a real difference maker. This roster still has a lot of holes and lacks depth. And I’m not sure that the offensive coaching staff will be able to do more with less. This feels more like a transition year in which Harbaugh figures out which guys he wants to build with going forward. Projected record: 6-11 How every 2026 NFL draft pick has looked in the preseason | ESPN.com Round 1 (No. 10): Francis Mauigoa, G. Mauigoa fits in nicely on the Giants offensive line. He has been the starter at right guard since Day 1 of camp, where he has proven to be a big help with his nasty style of play, specifically in the run game. New York seems to have big plans for Mauigoa. The only downside is he missed some time this summer with a stinger, which comes after he was diagnosed with a herniated disc in his back earlier this year. It’s something to keep an eye on moving forward. Round 2 (No. 37): Colton Hood, CB. It has been an up-and-down summer for Hood, but he is still competing with Deonte Banks, Greg Newsome II and Paulson Adebo for playing time at one of the two outside spots. It’s likely that Hood starts the season as a backup, but he’ll get a chance at some point. His competitiveness has flashed, which has made life difficult for receivers but also led to some penalties. 10 First-Round NFL Rookies Blowing Away Expectations at Training Camp | SI.com Arvell Reese, LB, New York Giants. When Arvell Reese was drafted No. 5 overall by the New York Giants, the premier question became whether he’d be staying at off-ball linebacker, or making the rumored transition to edge rusher. With the Giants loaded at defensive end, they decided to keep him at his college position. Reese has looked very comfortable at linebacker throughout camp. The former Ohio State standout has been displaying his athleticism and sideline-to-sideline ability. summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … One potential first-time Pro Bowler from each NFC team heading into the 2026 NFL season – NFL.comA.J. full_text: Jul 30, 2026; Philadelphia, PA, USA; Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith (6) during training camp at Jefferson Health Training Complex. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … One potential first-time Pro Bowler from each NFC team heading into the 2026 NFL season – NFL.com A.J. Brown’s exit opens a trove of opportunities for DeVonta Smith. Yes, the Eagles drafted Makai Lemon in the first round and buffered the unit with veterans, but Smith is the alpha. The sixth-year pro boasts route-running ability and can generate separation with the best of them. Smith is a WR1. There will be no question now. [BLG Note: Isn’t it wild how DeVonta hasn’t made a Pro Bowl already? He’s certainly that caliber of player.] A thought on all 90 Eagles leaving 2026 training camp – NBCSP WR DeVonta Smith: The Eagles were without Smith for a good portion of this training camp as he healed from a hamstring injury but they’re very excited to see him take over as their WR1. A.J. Brown was a great player in Philly but his absence will open the door for Smith to have a huge season in an expanded role. When he has been on the field, we’ve seen how good Smith can be. What really stood out this summer was his ability to bring in contested catches against some really good cornerbacks. Smith should shine in Sean Mannion’s offense. Eagles-Bengals snap counts: Cole Payton saw some special teams action – BGN The Eagles experimented with using Cole Payton on punt coverage. He finished the summer with just 21 preseason snaps, 15 of which came in his encouraging NFL debut. Weird and disappointing that the Eagles didn’t make a better effort to get him more experience after that, unless they’re just trying to prevent other teams from poaching him? But maybe just play him and then keep him on your roster? Seems like a wasted developmental opportunity. NFL Rookie of the Year 2026 predictions, including one 3rd round sleeper – SB Nation Makai Lemon, WR — Philadelphia Eagles. Lemon is sitting at WR3 on the Eagles depth chart, which is the role he was drafted for. Working out of the slot in this offense will give him a lot of opportunities, and Philly brings the exposure needed to build a campaign. Lemon is also in a position where he could get a lot of targets from Jalen Hurts, and is in a rare situation among the rookie receivers where he’s landing on an elite offense. There’s a chance he could become a key touchdown scorer this season, and I’m not entirely sure that being on an offense with DeVonta Smith will really hurt him. Eagles worked out an intriguing edge defender; Cowboys made a weird trade – PhillyVoice Reiger was a priority undrafted free agent who signed with the Miami Dolphins. Leading up to the draft, most analysts thought he would be selected. For example, he was Mel Kiper’s 140th-ranked (4th/5th round) prospect, and Dane Brugler’s 197th-ranked (5th/6th round) prospect. But, Reiger had a complicated evaluation because of a worrisome injury history, as noted in Brugler’s scouting report. Preseason Football – Iggles Blitz Na Brown. Paul Turner. And now Carson Steele. He was released by the Eagles and that confused more than a few people. You can argue he was the best Eagles player over the past two games. But that was in terms of results, not process. Steele has the right combination of size, athleticism and effort that helps him shine in August. He’s done that with multiple teams. KC put him on the roster in 2024. He ran for 183 yards and averaged 3.3 yards per carry. He caught 7 passes and averaged 3.7 yards per reception. Not ideal. He’s just not quite good enough to make plays against starters. Steele is great in the summer when he’s going against future car salesmen, insurance employees or welders. He’s not the same when going against guys like Zack Baun. 12 NFL teams did not play their starting quarterbacks in the preseason – PFT The growing trend of NFL teams keeping their quarterbacks out of the preseason has reached the point where more than one-third of starting quarterbacks did not take a single snap in this year’s preseason. [BLG Note: Jalen Hurts was obviously one of these 12.] Eagles’ Cooper DeJean attends Red Bull Championship Run in Philadelphia – CBS News At the Red Bull Championship Run, 120 contestants tried to retrieve a flag at the end of a 30-foot greased pole over the Delaware River. Falcons 2026 roster cut tracker – The Falcoholic [Former Eagles UDFA signing] G Jaeden Roberts Carolina Panthers 2026 roster cuts tracker – Cat Scratch Reader [Former Eagle] Elijah Cooks, wide receiver Pittsburgh Steelers 2026 live cut tracker – Behind The Steel Curtain [Former Eagle] TE Jaheim Bell BREAKING: Cowboys trade with Steelers for OT Broderick Jones – Blogging The Boys Jones was not regarded well by Steelers fans, so this is something that they are celebrating with vigor. The Cowboys needed help at tackle as noted, but did they need help this badly? 2026 NFL offseason trade grades: Gervon Dexter, Broderick Jones – ESPN The Steelers got a solid return for a player they could have feasibly cut on Sunday — that’s always good business on cut-down day. Though, it is a little scary to walk into Week 1 with poor tackle depth behind Iheanachor and left tackle Troy Fautanu, both of whom have injury histories. The Cowboys take a big swing on a talented athlete at a position in which they have had some instability, and returning Jones to the right could help him return to his previous form of play. The Cowboys have yet to confirm which side is the plan for Jones, as left tackle Tyler Guyton started the year in a camp competition but reportedly impressed with a great summer, while right tackle Terence Steele — a long-time starter under contract through 2028 — hasn’t had the best play in past seasons. Ostensibly, Jones is better on the right and has a better path to reps on the right … but the recent film and injury history is scary to buy into, no matter the side. Commanders vs. Ravens preseason Week 3: Mark Tyler’s Studs and Duds – Hogs Haven OL Julian Good-Jones. Living up to the moniker I have bestowed upon him, “Bad-Jones” was every bit as bad as you could expect. It’s absolutely crazy to think that if Washington had a regular-season game tomorrow, this man may be our starting center. Shame, SHAME on Adam Peters! Giants-Jets winners and losers: Odell Beckham makes his case – Big Blue View Odell Beckham Jr. — Is anyone still questioning whether or not Beckham is making the 53-man roster? Beckham nearly had a 73-yard touchdown reception, but Jameis Winston slightly overthrew him and the ball fell incomplete. Beckham still had an outstanding night. He caught three passes for 53 yards, an average of 17.7 yards per catch, with the longest being a 23-yard grab. He has enough juice to be a useful player for this Giants team. John Harbaugh said after the game that Beckham has done enough to make a roster, but stopped short of anointing him as part of the Giants’ 53-man roster. … Social Media Information: BGN Facebook Page: Click here to like our page BGN Twitter: Follow @BleedingGreen BGN BlueSky: Follow @bleedgreennation.bsky.social BGN Instagram: Follow @BleedingGreenInsta BGN Manager: Follow Brandon Lee Gowton on Twitter | BlueSky | Threads BGN Radio Twitter: Follow @BGN_Radio The Feed post of the day Each day, we highlight a BGN community post here in this space. title: Eagles host rookie free agent on tryout
summary: News of the Philadelphia Eagles waiving players has already begun to leak out but the team did not officially file any roster cuts today, according the NFL’s August 29 personnel notice. There were two Eagles transactions listed, however. Here’s an overview: Let’s sort through these items on a player-by-player basis. TARIQ CASTRO-FIELDS TCF was having […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - AUGUST 14: Athan Kaliakmanis #16 of the Washington Commanders is tackled by Mason Reiger #90 of the Miami Dolphins during the second half of a preseason game at Northwest Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images News of the Philadelphia Eagles waiving players has already begun to leak out but the team did not officially file any roster cuts today, according the NFL’s August 29 personnel notice. There were two Eagles transactions listed, however. Here’s an overview: The Eagles terminated CB Tariq Castro-Fields from injured reserve with an injury settlement. The Eagles hosted EDGE Mason Reiger on a tryout. Let’s sort through these items on a player-by-player basis. TARIQ CASTRO-FIELDS TCF was having a decent summer before suffering a heel injury that landed him on injured reserve on August 21. Now he’s leaving Philly after reaching an injury settlement with the team. MASON REIGER Reiger, who turned 24 earlier this month, played college football for Louisville and Wisconsin before signing with the Miami Dolphins as an undrafted rookie free agent following the 2026 NFL Draft. Here’s a scouting report on him from NFL.com’s Lance Zierlein , who tabbed him as a potential fifth-round pick: Reiger is a tall, linear edge rusher with a slender frame. He doesn’t look like a pro pre-snap, but he certainly plays like one after the snap. He lacks the size/anchor to consistently set the edge and can be controlled when tackles latch on, but he’s unusually talented to work off contact for quick wins at the point of attack. He’s a short-striding rusher who takes similar tracks at similar speeds and is more pressure-creator than sack-finisher at this time. However, altering his approach (tempo and angles) and adding a better inside counter could create a bump in his sack production. Reiger needs more mass and refinement but could become a good rotational odd-front edge in time. Reiger played 23 snaps in the Dolphins’ first preseason game, logging one sack and one TFL. There was also talk of him impressing in practice before Miami abrupt waived him with an injury designation on August 18. The Eagles might’ve wanted to take a look at Reiger to check in on his medical situation. Could be a good addition to the practice squad or they could look to stash him at the bottom of their roster?

full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Myles Hinton #78 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the national anthem prior to an NFL preseason football game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles waived 2025 sixth-round pick Myles Hinton on Saturday, according to a report from NFL insider Adam Schefter . Hinton’s departure doesn’t come as a surprise ; he really struggled this summer. The Eagles originally experimented with moving the 24-year-old to guard earlier this offseason before putting him back at offensive tackle, where he didn’t play well. Perhaps the Eagles will bring Hinton back on the practice squad if he clears waivers but I tend to think he might look for a fresh start. It’s worth noting that Jeff Stoutland, who left the Eagles earlier this year, seemed to be a big fan of Hinton when he was drafted. Hinton is the third member of the Eagles’ 2025 NFL Draft class to be dismissed by the team. They previously cut Kyle McCord and Antwaun Powell-Ryland Jr. (who made some plays against the Birds for the Cincinnati Bengals on Friday night) last year. The following 2025 Eagles draft picks are still currently on the roster: LB Jihaad Campbell S Andrew Mukuba DT Ty Robinson CB Mac McWilliams LB Smael Mondon Jr. OL Drew Kendall OT Cameron Williams Robinson looked to be in trouble earlier this summer before rebounding to likely make the team. McWilliams and/or Williams could be in danger of getting cut. Of course, the Eagles did sign standout Darius Cooper in undrafted free agency last year in addition to claiming Willie Lampkin off waivers as a rookie. title: Eagles vs. Bengals Preseason: The good, the bad, and the ugly
summary: If the Eagles wanted to keep everything hidden this preseason, they certainly did a good job of it. They could not really be that bad after three preseason games. It’s possibly the only conclusion that could be made, after the Eagles went winless in three preseason games, losing to the Cincinnati Bengals Friday night, 30-13, […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - AUGUST 15: Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the first half of the preseason game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images If the Eagles wanted to keep everything hidden this preseason, they certainly did a good job of it. They could not really be that bad after three preseason games. It’s possibly the only conclusion that could be made, after the Eagles went winless in three preseason games, losing to the Cincinnati Bengals Friday night, 30-13, at Lincoln Financial Field. The Eagles were outscored this preseason, 78-41. They were outgained, 1,248 to 670. They gave up 77 first downs, while achieving a scant 38. It makes you wonder just how deep this team is. First-round draft pick Makai Lemon saw his first action, getting a nice round of applause after he made his first catch. His night, however, was an utter disappointment: three catches on five targets for three yards, and a catchable ball that deflected off his hands that led to an interception. At least Andy Dalton redeemed himself from what had been so far a bad summer. The 38-year-old completed 12 of 19 passes for 104 yards, and one touchdown. Tanner McKee we will get to (see ugly). There was a continued slew of ugly, some bad and some comforting good in the Eagles’ 30-13 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. The Good Carson Steele looks like he will make the Eagles , after another strong performance in which he had eight catches for 52 yards and a TD against the Bengals. He has a knack for doing something each time he is on the field. His Friday night follows the six passes he caught on seven targets—one for 28 yards—for 84 yards and a touchdown, while rushing for 33 yards on 12 carries against New England in the second preseason game. The bad is that Steele was the Eagles’ leading receiver through three preseason games, while Lemon did little in his preseason debut and the starting receivers did not play at all. [UPDATE: Steele was reportedly waived.] Kicker Jake Elliott nailing field goals of 45 and 56 yards. It was good to see, considering the Eagles have shown considerable faith, as they should, in the Super Bowl-winning kicker who has a history of more clutch kicks than bad—though last season was uneven at best. It was encouraging to see Elliott kicking like Jake Elliott . Cornerback Mac McWilliams did a decent job tackling and little else, making a team-high seven tackles—six solo—but he was the best of a bad situation on a defense that gave up 420 yards of total offense, 25 first downs, an average of 6.6 yards a play, and allowed seven of 13 third-down conversions. McWilliams had problems in coverage, and that could mean a demotion to the practice squad. A strange one here, but the good for these guys who did not play. The human bowling ball with knives, Willie Lampkin, and linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr., who had two super preseason games and little to prove that he deserves to be an NFL starter. Defensive tackle Ty Robinson, who received limited playing time Friday night, impressed this entire preseason with three sacks in three games. Quarterback Andy Dalton may have reversed his course from the No. 3 to the prime backup. He completed 12 of 19 passes for 104 yards, and one touchdown. More so, he looked in control, was steady and he looked better than McKee. The Bad Lemon was sketchy. He is undersized to begin with, and his hamstring has been causing him problems this entire offseason. His debut did not go well. His three catches on five targets for three yards were disappointing. The defense. As stated above, the Eagles have given up 1,248 yards, allowing an average of 416 yards and 26 points a game. They allowed their three opponents to convert 21 of 41 third downs, which translates into 51.2-percent. The receiving corps. Lemon is still getting himself in playing shape, hampered by the hamstring injury, while starters DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks did not play at all this preseason. So, the Eagles are left with Hollywood Brown, Darius Cooper, who had an inconsistent preseason with five catches for 65 yards, and Elijah Moore, who caught two passes for 10 yards this preseason. The receiving corps, and iffy area of the field to begin with after the A.J. Brown trade, looks like a weakness entering the season. Much will depend on Smith emerging as a quality No. 1 NFL go-to receiver, which he is very capable of doing. The Eagles will be hoping for the 6-foot, 170-pound Smith to hold up the entire season. Will he, considering the additional pounding he will take in Brown’s absence? The Ugly The Eagles’ coaching staff. Okay, okay, it is preseason, but Nick Sirianni and his coaching staff are expected to coach up everyone, starters, backups, and future practice squanders. The futility of the offense and how porous the defense showed that they did not do a very good job of it. The 0-3 record and the inability of the offense and defense was proof. Performance counts, regardless of who is on the field. Part of that is the inability of the players in the game, part of that is positioning those players to make plays. Sirianni would probably give himself a poor grade after the preseason. Quarterback Tanner McKee did not help his case. He had looked better than Dalton in the first two preseason games, and with more time, starting the game, seemed to expose himself. He completed 12 of 22 passes for 55 yards, and an interception. With 1:11 left in the first half, McKee had Britain Covey open down the sideline for what should have been a touchdown—and missed him. Friday night’s performance comes after a solid showing against New England, when he completed 16 of 22 passes for 173 yards and two touchdowns. At the time, McKee seemed to be the leader in the backup race, considering how poorly Dalton looked in his first two preseason games. The backup job seems not so certain now. Cornerback Ambry Thomas did not have a good two weeks. With and Eagles stop in the fourth quarter, they could have taken a lead. Instead, an Eagles’ fumble recovery was overturned by a Thomas’ holding call. The very next play, the Bengals converted a third-and-four to the man Thomas was covering. This follows the New England preseason game in which Thomas was beaten bad on a Tommy DeVito 69-yard, second-quarter touchdown pass.

title: Eagles-Bengals snap counts: Cole Payton saw some special teams action
summary: The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ preseason loss to the Cincinnati Bengals are in. TAke a look, y’all. OFFENSE DEFENSE SPECIAL TEAMS DID NOT PLAY
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Cole Payton #10 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the national anthem prior to an NFL preseason football game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ preseason loss to the Cincinnati Bengals are in. TAke a look, y’all. OFFENSE Micah Morris played the second-most offensive snaps of any Eagles player this preseason, just four behind Jake Majors. Good to see for the rookie blocker’s development since he won’t be getting any snaps in the regular season (unless things have gone horribly wrong). On a side note, Majors might sneak onto the roster? He spent all of last season on the practice squad. Not unlike Majors, John Ojukwu has felt like a dark horse roster candidate. Tend to think he’s off, though. Is Carson Steele going to make the roster? He’s made a case for himself. But the fact that he played a lot might not bode well for his chances. Quez Watkins played the most preseason snaps of any Eagles skill player with 108. And yet he had just two receptions for seven yards. At least he got a lot of cardio in by running all of those routes. Tanner McKee played the entire first half on Friday night and he sure didn’t look good. Not really sure what the point of playing Andy Dalton, who is entering his age 39 season, for 25 snaps in the second half of a preseason finale was. Like, we didn’t already know what he is/isn’t at this point? This entire Eagles backup quarterback battle has been weird at every step of the way. Fred Johnson played in this game while rookie Markel Bell did not. Of course, Bell is banged up. Still, notable that Johnson was not rested. But at least it’s not like he played the entire night. Elijah Moore played in this game while Darius Cooper did not. Moore is on the bubble. I have him making my final 53-man projection but I don’t feel awesome about it. He’s earned a spot and the coaches have talked him up … but he’s also a vested veteran who isn’t subject to waivers. Really second-guessing myself here. Stone Smartt is tied with Maximus Pulley for the second-most special teams snaps played this summer. They’re behind Deontae Lawson in the top spot. Smartt is a practice squad contender. Makai Lemon logged 17 special teams snaps and one special teams snap in his NFL debut. It didn’t go so great for the rookie wide receiver . Myles Hinton didn’t see much playing time and it’s not like the Eagles were resting him. He’s just fallen off of roster consideration. Tough. Dameon Pierce had some nice flashes but he hasn’t done enough to make the roster. The Eagles experimented with using Cole Payton on punt coverage. He finished the summer with just 21 preseason snaps, 15 of which came in his encouraging NFL debut. Weird and disappointing that the Eagles didn’t make a better effort to get him more experience after that, unless they’re just trying to prevent other teams from poaching him? But maybe just play him and then keep him on your roster? Seems like a wasted developmental opportunity. Tahj Washington got a little playing time after only signing with the Eagles two days ago . DEFENSE Kapena Gushiken had a rough game. Unlike last week, when he exclusively played slot cornerback, the Eagles split his snaps between nickel CB and safety. The Eagles may have never had a better preseason Peanut Puncher than Shaun Wade. Three forced fumbles in three games. The Eagles took a long look at Deontae Lawson this summer. Seems like he’s on the roster bubble. Andre’ Sam led the Eagles in defensive snaps this preseason despite getting carted off in this game. Shame to see. Zion Wilson logged the third-most snaps of any Eagles preseason defender this summer. Good to get him a lot of reps for his development. He at least belongs on the practice squad, if he doesn’t sneak onto the roster. This was probably the last chance for Joshua Weru and Uar Bernard to play until next preseason. Keyshawn James-Newby notched a sack in his NFL debut. After splitting snaps between outside corner and slot corner in his first preseason game, Mac McWilliams was exclusively used at outside corner in the last two games. It seems like slot corner might be his better position, though. Smael Mondon Jr. not playing too much makes me believe he’s on the team, in case that was in question at all. Interesting to see that Michael Carter II suited up again. Marcus Epps did not play a preseason snap despite Vic Fangio’s insistence that there’s an ongoing safety competition. Kelee Ringo not playing too much makes me believe he’s on the team. Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa got the start before quickly calling it a night. I bet you didn’t realize the Eagles had a player named Jaylen Mahoney on their roster. No relation to Dick Mahoney , as far as I know. SPECIAL TEAMS Jake Elliott made his only two field goal attempts of the preseason, one from 45 and another from 56. DID NOT PLAY Eli Stowers, Markel Bell, Grant Calcaterra, Jakorian Bennett, and Cole Wisniewski did not participate in the Eagles’ most recent practice, so, they were likely not healthy enough to play. Jonathan Jones was limited in the Eagles’ most recent practice but he’s also a veteran so he might not have played even if he was healthy. Willie Lampkin suffered a stinger in the Eagles’ last preseason game before returning to practice this week. It did seem like he may have tweaked something on Wednesday, so, maybe the Eagles were being extra cautious by not playing him here. Darius Cooper being rested is a good sign for his standing on the team. Ditto for Drew Kendall, Will Shipley, and Jeremiah Trotter Jr.

title: Eagles News: “The QB2 battle has been weird this summer”
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Final Roster Prediction – Iggles BlitzQB – 3 – Jalen Hurts, Tanner McKee, Cole Payton. The QB2 battle has been weird this summer. Whatever the Eagles plan was, it didn’t work. Neither McKee nor Dalton was good. I don’t think anyone is trading for either […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Andy Dalton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on before the preseason game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Final Roster Prediction – Iggles Blitz QB – 3 – Jalen Hurts, Tanner McKee, Cole Payton. The QB2 battle has been weird this summer. Whatever the Eagles plan was, it didn’t work. Neither McKee nor Dalton was good. I don’t think anyone is trading for either guy. If Howie can find a taker for Dalton, go ahead and put him in Canton. I don’t have a lot of confidence in what the team will do here since things were so weird this summer. Nothing will shock me, including a trade to add a QB. Handing out 10 awards from the Eagles-Bengals preseason game – PhillyVoice 2) The ‘When You Have Two QB2s, You Really Don’t Have Any’ Award 👎👎: Tanner McKee and Andy Dalton McKee had a rough game. He finished 12 of 22 for 55 yards (2.5 YPA), 0 TDs. and 1 INT. Most of those yards were on checkdowns to Carson Steele. McKee made several bad throws along the way, including a missed opportunity to hit a wide open Britain Covey for what should have been a TD after Covey smoked a Bengals DB on a stutter-go. Meanwhile, Dalton is 38 years old with 173 career starts and he was playing with a lot of guys who aren’t going to make the team in the second half of the final preseason game. Dalton looked better than McKee at least, finishing 12 of 19 for 104 yards, 1 TD, and 0 INTs. He had one good drive, and otherwise looked a lot like a 38-year-old playing in the second half of a preseason game. Eagles lose to the Cincinnati Bengals: From the peculiar QB2 competition to Makai Lemon’s debut, five takeaways – PHLY The next chapter in a peculiar QB2 battle. Full disclosure: I originally had written that Friday night was the final chapter in the Eagles’ awkward battle for the backup quarterback job, but the performances from both Tanner McKee and Andy Dalton left things all the more uncomfortably unsettled going into cut-down day Sunday evening. McKee looked like a shell of his former self in a half of preseason action against the Bengals defense, going 12-for-22 for 55 yards and one interception with a handful of errant passes. The outing served as a direct contrast from one of McKee’s brightest moments: Exactly 386 days prior when the 26-year-old went 2o-for25 for 252 yards and two touchdowns. The discussion after that game was whether a Day 2 pick would be enough for a quarterback-needy team to pry him away from the Eagles at some point, but now it’s hard to envision McKee garnering anything near that on the trade market. Dalton, who came in at the beginning of the second half after starting each of the previous two games, was slightly better. He went 12-for-19 for 104 yards and a touchdown, although it’s still hard to argue he clears the bar as the No. 2 quarterback for a team that has valued the role so highly for more than a decade. It’s also hard to know whether the Eagles can recoup draft assets for the 38-year-old in a trade between now and Sunday at 6 p.m., which beckons the question: If the Eagles can’t find a trade partner for Dalton or McKee, will general manager Howie Roseman be willing to keep four quarterbacks on the roster to regain leverage? And if not, which of the four will fall victim to the crowded room? Cole Payton has been encouraging enough this summer to argue he’s shown enough be on the initial roster, but it’s at least worth mentioning just how limited his exposure to the rest of the league has been in each of the last two preseason games as a somewhat-unfair byproduct of the quarterback competition lingering this long into the summer. The sixth-round rookie was utilized as a personal protector on the punt unit Friday night, but took his first snaps under center until after the five-minute mark of the fourth quarter. Could the Eagles been trying to hide him as a way to get him through waivers? It’s unlikely, but there’s no impossibilities in this summer’s strange quarterback carousel. Eagles-Bengals preseason: Makai Lemon debuts, no clear victor in QB2 competition – The Athletic The Eagles split reps between Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee throughout training camp practices and preseason games to determine their backup behind starting quarterback Jalen Hurts. Neither quarterback played well enough to be considered a clear winner. McKee started Friday night against the Bengals; he underwhelmed by completing 12 of 22 passes for 55 yards and an interception. He was also sacked twice. His passes seemed to have too much juice in the backfield, too little on deeper throws along the sideline, and he overthrew Britain Covey on a deep pass toward the end zone. Dalton led an 11-play, 76-yard touchdown drive against the third-team defense, but McKee had similar success against the bottom end of the depth chart last week. The Eagles are likely displeased with what the QB2 competition produced. It is also unclear what the Eagles will do. Coach Nick Sirianni said McKee needed extra reps to get more comfortable in a new system. Last year, McKee completed 20 of 25 passes for 252 yards and two touchdowns in the preseason opener against the Bengals, and the coaching staff saw enough to sit him for the remaining two exhibitions. If the Eagles bet on the 26-year-old McKee’s potential over Dalton’s 16 years of experience, they will enter the 2026 season in the precarious position of knowing Jalen Hurts’ backup is not yet comfortable with this scheme. Philadelphia Eagles 53-man roster prediction: Final edition – BGN Now that the Philadelphia Eagles’ preseason schedule is over, the team’s focus shifts to cutting their roster down to the regular season 53-player limit before the 6:00 PM Eastern deadline on Sunday, August 30. Here’s our best effort at projecting what the INITIAL roster is going to look like. The Birds will likely make some tweaks (injured reserve placements, trades, waiver claims, etc.) before they actually play the Washington Commanders in Week 1. Note that this activity is about predicting what the Eagles WILL do as opposed to what we necessarily think they should do. From benched, doubted and overlooked, to Super Bowl MVP – SB Nation It’s easy to simply say Jalen Hurts stinks. Not like a smelly person or anything, but bad at football. Which is a bit of a lazy read. In recent years, he hasn’t exactly fit the mold of a traditional QB and could maybe fairly be called a tush-push merchant, but those labels massively overshadow one of the league’s more unique journeys. 2026 NFL Preseason, Week 3: What We Learned from Friday’s games – NFL.com Lemon drop mars debut. First-round pick Makai Lemon saw his first preseason action after missing most of training camp with a hamstring injury. He was targeted right away by Tanner McKee, getting free on an out route for an easy 3-yard gain. A deep shot to Lemon two plays later was deflected by the defender. Then, on his fourth target, Lemon couldn’t corral a dart from McKee on a slant, the ball deflecting off his hands for an interception. After Lemon saw 17 offensive snaps (three catches on five targets for 3 yards), Philly oddly tossed him back out there for a third-quarter punt return. The former Trojan played half of snaps out wide and half in the slot, perhaps providing a glimpse at the versatility he’ll provide Jalen Hurts alongside DeVonta Smith in the starting offense. For a player who thrived in college at playing in the middle of the field, Lemon’s big drop and little gains were letdowns, but any action is better than no action. title: Philadelphia Eagles 53-man roster prediction: Final edition
summary: Now that the Philadelphia Eagles’ preseason schedule is over, the team’s focus shifts to cutting their roster down to the regular season 53-player limit before the 6:00 PM Eastern deadline on Sunday, August 30. Here’s our best effort at projecting what the INITIAL roster is going to look like. The Birds will likely make some […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Uar Bernard #93 of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts against the New England Patriots during an NFL preseason football game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Now that the Philadelphia Eagles’ preseason schedule is over, the team’s focus shifts to cutting their roster down to the regular season 53-player limit before the 6:00 PM Eastern deadline on Sunday, August 30. Here’s our best effort at projecting what the INITIAL roster is going to look like. The Birds will likely make some tweaks (injured reserve placements, trades, waiver claims, etc.) before they actually play the Washington Commanders in Week 1. Note that this activity is about predicting what the Eagles WILL do as opposed to what we necessarily think they should do. OFFENSE QUARTERBACK: Jalen Hurts, Tanner McKee, Cole Payton (3) [3] Hurts threw a lot of interceptions this summer, yes, but I challenge you to find a daily practice observer who feels like he had a bad camp. On the whole, the good outweighed the bad. It seems like he’s embracing the new offensive direction. The Eagles are hoping Hurts doesn’t get, well, hurt … because the depth behind him is very uninspiring. There was no clear winner from the Eagles’ training camp backup quarterback battle. McKee somehow looked worse than ever after previously showing encouraging signs in previous years. Dalton looks somewhat physically diminished, which tracks for a quarterback entering his age 39 season. Maybe he gets traded … but what price is he even fetching at this point? I wonder if the Eagles might trade both Dalton (for very meager draft pick compensation) AND McKee (included in a deal for another team’s quarterback, such as Anthony Richardson or J.J. McCarthy)? Payton has shown some promise but the Eagles didn’t really do a good job of getting him more action in the preseason. Utilizing him on special teams in the final preseason game points to them trying to find a role for him. This is a tough position to figure out. OUT: Andy Dalton RUNNING BACK: Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley (3) [6] Barkley looks poised for another big season and he might actually be involved as a pass-catcher more than ever this year, no, for real, I mean it this time?! Bigsby’s role is obviously limited with Barkley blocking his path to playing time but he’s simply too good to be a total afterthought in this offense. Shipley finished training camp strong and did enough to earn his RB3 role, which was evident by the team resting him in the third preseason game. Carson Steele was basically the entire Eagles’ passing offense in the preseason but I don’t think they need to keep him on the roster; he spent all of last year on the Kansas City Chiefs’ practice squad. Dameon Pierce looked good early in camp, got hurt and missed a lot of time, and then looked good upon returning … before maybe getting banged up again? Steele and/or Pierce will be on the practice squad. Jordan Mims was recently added to the roster to help fill practice reps/preseason snaps. OUT: Carson Steele, Dameon Pierce, Jordan Mims WIDE RECEIVER: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore (6) [12] As the Eagles’ undisputed top receiving option, Smitty is going to have his first career Pro Bowl season. There’s every reason to believe in him. In a more perfect world, Wicks might ideally be WR3 … but he’s clearly WR2 in this configuration. Hurts was not scared to throw to him over and over while Smitty and Lemon missed most of camp. Lemon doesn’t look ready to be a starting receiver in Week 1 after missing most of the Eagles’ offseason practices but it seems like they’re going to try to make it work anyway. Brown didn’t have a great summer and Hurts threw a number of interceptions when the ball went his way … but his guaranteed money signals the Eagles holding onto him, unless he exits in a trade. The Eagles do seem to value Brown’s deep threat ability. Cooper proved that he deserves playing time on offense but it remains to be seen if the Eagles will actually give it to him. Moore is firmly on the bubble and I could see the Eagles cutting him since he’s a vested veteran who could be brought back on the practice squad. But the coaching staff has spoken favorably of Moore and he’s had a good summer and Hurts has thrown to him a lot. Plus, with Lemon looking a bit shaky, the Eagles could afford to go heavier here. Britain Covey is a contender to be temporarily elevated from the practice squad to help out at punt returner. OUT: Britain Covey, Quez Watkins, Danny Gray, Samori Toure, Erik Ezukanma, Tahj Washington IR: Johnny Wilson TIGHT END: Dallas Goedert, Johnny Mundt, Grant Calcaterra, Cameron Latu (4) [16] Goedert is the Eagles’ top tight end, which is fine-to-good. The depth behind him is not great. Mundt has built a reputation as much more of a blocker than a pass-catcher. He’s consistently been TE2 in the Eagles’ 12 personnel packages. Calcaterra is currently dealing with a back injury and the severity is unclear. I wouldn’t keep him and I know Eagles fans won’t want to see him on the roster. But I think the team likes him more than you do. Latu is a special teams standout. E.J. Jenkins and/or Stone Smartt are practice squad considerations. I have Eli Stowers, who is currently dealing with a hamstring injury, beginning the season on injured reserve/designated to return. He’ll be required to miss four games before being eligible to return. Using this mechanism also avoids the likelihood of him being a healthy scratch, at least early in the season. Stowers showed nothing this offseason to suggest that he’s ready to significantly contribute in 2026. OUT: E.J. Jenkins, Stone Smartt IR (DESIGNATED FOR RETURN): Eli Stowers OFFENSIVE LINE: Jordan Mailata, Landon Dickerson, Cam Jurgens, Tyler Steen, Lane Johnson, Markel Bell, Drew Kendall, Willie Lampkin, Micah Morris, Cameron Williams (10) [26] The starting offensive line is set. Dickerson appears to be less than 100% physically, which is something to monitor this season. By contrast, Jurgens looks healthier than he did in 2025. Steen looks like he’s better than he was last year. Johnson is entering his final NFL season, according to him (though there’s plenty of time for him to change his mind). Bell is currently banged up and the severity of his injury is unclear, so, maybe the Eagles need to keep Fred Johnson. But we have Big Fred off because he’s had a bad summer and he could be brought back on the practice squad; we’ve already seen that the league doesn’t really value him. Also, Bell has looked good and deserves to be the swing tackle. Kendall has emerged as this year’s Brett Toth, meaning that he’s poised to be the top interior backup. Lampkin earned his roster spot by having an impressive offseason; he could be active as the eight offensive lineman on game day. Morris showed developmental potential and the Eagles might not be ready to give up on the 22-year-old Williams. Jake Majors is a strong practice squad contender and John Ojukwu might return in that capacity as well. Myles Hinton played his way out of practice squad contention and Jeff Stoutland, who seemed to be high on him, is no longer around. The Eagles don’t need Michael Jordan now that the Sixers have LeBron James. OUT: Fred Johnson, Michael Jordan, Jake Majors, John Ojukwu, Myles Hinton, Zeke Correll DEFENSE EDGE RUSHER: Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith, A.J. Epenesa, Arnold Ebiketie, Josh Weru (6) [32] There’s concern that Greenard won’t be ready for Week 1 but the Eagles might have hope he can at least return by Week 4, which would justify not having him begin the season on the reserve/PUP list. But I wouldn’t fault the team for keeping him on PUP in an effort not to rush him back and instead try their best to get him right. Hunt was the star of the summer for the Eagles; he looks ready to…

full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Broderick Jones #77 of the Pittsburgh Steelers in action during the game against the Green Bay Packers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have traded Broderick Jones to the Dallas Cowboys. The trade comes on the evening before final 53-man rosters are due around the league. Per ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, the Cowboys sent Pittsburgh a third- and sixth-round pick in exchange for a fourth-round pick and Jones. The Cowboys are sending third- and sixth-round picks to the Steelers for a fourth-rounder and OT Broderick Jones, per source. — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) August 29, 2026 The Steelers traded up to select Jones 14th overall in the 2023 NFL Draft. Jones suffered a brutal neck injury during Week 12 of the 2025 season against the Chicago Bears. The injury required Jones to receive spinal fusion surgery. After little to no updates on the injury through the offseason, Jones was surprisingly activated from the PUP list just one day before training camp began. Jones’ availability seemed to come as a shock to everyone, including the Steelers. Pittsburgh selected their third offensive tackle in four years in April by selecting Max Iheanachor out of Arizona State. This move allowed the Steelers to have Troy Fautanu switch back to his primary position of left tackle, while almost certainly meaning that Jones’ time as a starter had come to an end. Just last week, Jones expressed frustration with all of the moving around he has done during the summer. Jones was playing about 15 pounds underweight throughout training camp. A fresh start for Jones seemed to be in the best interest of both sides. Now the Steelers have an extra roster spot available, and future draft capital to continue to build with.
