title: Jamel Dean says Steelers are capable of winning Super Bowl
summary: Confidence is growing inside the Pittsburgh Steelers locker room as the team prepares for the 2026 season, and veteran cornerback Jamel Dean believes the roster has what it takes to make a serious run at the Super Bowl. Dean, who won a Super Bowl with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers following the 2020 season, drew a […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 21: Jamel Dean #35 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on during the game against the New York Jets at Acrisure Stadium on August 21, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Confidence is growing inside the Pittsburgh Steelers locker room as the team prepares for the 2026 season, and veteran cornerback Jamel Dean believes the roster has what it takes to make a serious run at the Super Bowl. Dean, who won a Super Bowl with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers following the 2020 season, drew a comparison between his current Steelers team and the Buccaneers squad that ultimately captured the Lombardi Trophy. “This team right here reminds me of that team we had in Tampa, when we won the Super Bowl,” Dean said. “Like, we got all the pieces that we need,” he told El Podcast Immaculado , the Steelers official Spanish podcast. The Steelers have emphasized experience while also adding younger talent to a roster that is expected to carry significant expectations this season. Dean believes that combination could prove to be one of the team’s biggest strengths. “We got veteran guys that understand the game, that knows what it takes to get there,” Dean said. “And we also got younger guys that’s bonding to the system, and they’re also coming along to make plays too.” Dean’s perspective carries added weight given his experience with a championship team in Tampa Bay. The Buccaneers entered the 2020 season with a mix of established veterans and emerging talent before putting together a postseason run that culminated in a dominant Super Bowl victory over the Kansas City Chiefs. Pittsburgh is hoping its own blend of veterans and young players can produce a similar result. The Steelers have made significant investments in their roster, particularly on defense, while also adding veteran pieces and young talent on the offensive side of the ball. With expectations rising around new head coach Mike McCarthy and a veteran-led roster, the team’s ultimate goal is no secret. Dean, however, believes the foundation is already in place. For a player who has experienced firsthand what it takes to go from a talented roster to a championship team, his assessment is notable: the Steelers believe they have the pieces to make a Super Bowl run. full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 28: Running back Emmett Johnson #10 of the Kansas City Chiefs carries the ball as linebacker Patrick O'Connell #52 and linebacker Aidan Hubbard #93 of the Seattle Seahawks defend during the 1st half of the preseason game at Arrowhead Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. Of course, there’s an emphasis on initial , because the roster is almost certainly going to change several times over before opening night against the New England Patriots. Seattle is typically a team that waits until cutdown day itself (which, this year, is Sunday) before all of the cuts get reported, so I think there’s enough time to squeeze out a last roster projection. With Terrion Arnold signed and Derrick Graham waived in a corresponding move , that bit of news will be reflected in my projections. O ffense (25) Quarterback (3): Sam Darnold, Drew Lock, Jalen Milroe Cut: N/A Notes : I think Friday night put to bed any notion that Milroe wouldn’t make the team. There was some legitimate nonzero concern after the Tennessee Titans outing, but he bounced back in a big way. Running Back (3): Jadarian Price (R), Emanuel Wilson, George Holani Cut: Jacardia Wright, Velus Jones Jr PUP: Zach Charbonnet Notes : If Emanuel Wilson’s hamstring is still an issue, then I think Wright ends up on the roster as a fourth back. He was in warm-ups and in pads on Friday so I guess he’s fine. Otherwise, keep three, have a couple of people on the practice squad for a few weeks, and Zach Charbonnet should be back in October. Fullback (1): Brady Russell Cut: Brock Lampe Already on IR: Robbie Ouzts Notes : Lampe showed some good stuff on film but he might be a practice squad player for the time being. Wide Receiver (5): Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp, Rashid Shaheed, Tory Horton, Montorie Foster Cut: Emmanuel Henderson Jr (R), Cody White, Ricky White III, Irv Charles, Rashad Rochelle (R) Already on IR: Jake Bobo Notes : Foster may not be on the regular season roster the whole year. I think that WR5 could almost be rotational given Cody White and Emmanuel Henderson Jr are viable candidates. Cody White always clears waivers, so White will probably get waived and be an immediate practice squad signing. Henderson is another PS signing, I believe. You can make a case for any of them, at this point. Irv Charles played no preseason snaps and his special teams value needs to be Matthew Slater level to make up for zero offensive productivity in his career. Horton’s injury is supposedly not long-term so I consider him good for Week 1. Tight End (4): A.J. Barner, Elijah Arroyo, Eric Saubert , Nick Kallerup Cut: Nick Vannett Notes : Same grouping as last year. Vannett can be a practice squad veteran option. Offensive Line (9) : Charles Cross, Abe Lucas, Josh Jones, Anthony Bradford, Olu Oluwatimi, Jalen Sundell, Grey Zabel, Christian Haynes , Beau Stephens (R) Cut: Federico Maranges, Bobby Hart , Amari Kight, Logan Brown, Bryce Cabeldue , Derrick Graham (already waived), Already on IR: Mason Richman Notes : If Haynes is let go then Cabeldue takes his spot. I think the Seahawks’ last guard spot is down to Haynes and Cabeldue and Haynes has had his best camp and preseason to date. Cabeldue could be a practice squad stash. Defense (25) Defensive Line (6): Byron Murphy II, Leonard Williams, Jarran Reed, Rylie Mills, Mike Morris , Brandon Pili Cut: J.R. Singleton, Bubba Thomas , Uso Seumalo (R) , Deven Eastern (R) , Aidan Hubbard (R) Notes : Mike Morris sitting out the Chiefs game means that, unless he’s a trade candidate, he’s probably safe for the roster. Pili might be borderline depending on their want of a nose tackle on the 53, but that’s about it. Seumalo and Eastern generally underwhelmed in preseason, whereas Singleton I anticipate will be back on the PS. Outside Linebacker (4): Derick Hall, Uchenna Nwosu , Dante Fowler Jr, DeMarcus Lawrence Cut: Jared Ivey, Connor O’Toole , Marvin Jones Jr (R), Jamie Sheriff, Jalan Gaines Notes : Ivey had his best game of preseason versus Kansas City, including early on when the Chiefs had starters in for a hot minute. I think it’s probably a little too late. O’Toole might sneak in for special teams value and maybe that comes at the cost of letting go of someone at another position. Sheriff and Gaines and Ivey all figure to be PS candidates. Inside Linebacker (4): Ernest Jones IV, Drake Thomas, Tyrice Knight, Patrick O’Connell Cut: Aaron Smith , Power Echols IR: Chazz Surratt (designated for return) , Chris Paul Jr (out for season) Notes : My IR line with Surratt is based off of Gregg Bell’s observations that Surratt was not suited up for play ; not even a helmet on. His own projection had Surratt on IR-designated for return. We’ll roll with four inside backers at the moment. Cornerback (6): Devon Witherspoon, Josh Jobe, Nehemiah Pritchett , Julian Neal (R), Noah Igbinoghene , Andre Fuller (R) Cut: Jordan Washington (R), Michael Dansby (R) , Trevon Diggs Exempt list: Terrion Arnold Notes : Arnold is signed but he won’t be on the 53-man roster any time soon. I think either Fuller or Dansby will find a way onto the 53, and I lean toward Fuller slightly. One of Igbinoghene or Diggs will be released and then signed to the practice squad or brought back later. My argument in favor of “cutting” Diggs is that, unlike Igbinoghene, he’s not had a proper training camp and barely played any NFL football over the past year. Igbinoghene could play a normal snap count in Week 1. Diggs might be someone who gets practice squad elevations and then permanently signed later in the season, but he’s definitely on this team to contribute throughout the season. Safety (5): Julian Love, Ty Okada, Nick Emmanwori, A.J. Finley , D’Anthony Bell Cut: Maxen Hook, Rodney Thomas II , Tysheem Johnson Already on IR: Bud Clark Notes : I’m not sure Emmanwori is Week 1 ready, which means D’Anthony Bell could at least be signed for Week 1. Thomas spending as much time as he did with the third-team in the first preseason game and at times with the threes in camp has me wondering what’s going on there. If you swapped Bell for Thomas I don’t really think there’s much argument from me. Special Teams (3) Kicker (1) : Jason Myers Punter (1) : Michael Dickson Long Snapper (1) : Chris Stoll Cut: No one Notes : They’re not cutting Jason Myers despite a horrific preseason. As a reminder, do not overestimate how many waiver claims are actually made during roster cuts weekend. It’s usually in the 2-3% percent range across the whole league, so if one of your preseason favorites is let go then he’s probably going to clear waivers. My only complication this year is how much the Minnesota Vikings under former Seahawks assistant GM, Nolan Teasley, might have an eye on Seattle’s cuts.

title: Terrion Arnold officially signs with Seahawks, is placed on commissioner’s exempt list
summary: The Seattle Seahawks have officially signed former Detroit Lions cornerback, Terrion Arnold. It was announced earlier this month that Arnold would be joining Seattle. However, considering the off the field issues that Arnold is dealing with (eight felony charges, including armed robbery and kidnapping), there remained questions as to the exact timing of his signing […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks have officially signed former Detroit Lions cornerback, Terrion Arnold. It was announced earlier this month that Arnold would be joining Seattle . However, considering the off the field issues that Arnold is dealing with ( eight felony charges, including armed robbery and kidnapping ), there remained questions as to the exact timing of his signing – or whether he would sign at all. Well now, those questions can officially go to rest. It was also announced that once the league receives Arnold’s contract from Seattle, that he will be placed on the commissioner’s exempt list . While on this list, Arnold will be paid, however he cannot practice or play. As long as Arnold is on the commissioner’s exempt list, he will not count against the Seahawks 53-man roster . The Seahawks have had questions about their depth at the cornerback position this training camp. Those questions remained even after the news of Arnold joining Seattle earlier this month. Perhaps that is what led the team to sign another veteran cornerback, Trevon Diggs. The signing of Diggs, as well as Arnold going on the exempt list, makes Saturday’s signing appear to be a move for later on in the season and perhaps after 2026. For those curious about the timing of this signing, and why the Seahawks waited so long, ESPN’s Brady Henderson explains it well . Arnold would count against the 91-man roster for at least one day, until he’s placed on the commissioner’s exempt list. Since he would be unable to practice or play in any games (including preseason), it made more sense for Seattle to leave that roster spot available for someone who could practice and play. This means that it would make sense for Seattle to make this move after the preseason games finished up, but before the 53-man roster cut down day. In other words, today. To make room on their roster, the Seahawks released offensive tackle, Derrick Graham.

title: NFL roster cuts, explained: Why these 25 Seahawks aren’t subject to waivers
summary: The 2026 NFL preseason is over for the Seattle Seahawks, and now the focus for this weekend is to trim their roster from 91 players to 53 by Sunday at 3 pm PT. For the bulk of players who are let go, they will have to go through the waiver wire, during which period they […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 15: Noah Igbinoghene #17 of the Seattle Seahawks looks on during the first quarter during the NFL preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lumen Field on August 15, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 NFL preseason is over for the Seattle Seahawks, and now the focus for this weekend is to trim their roster from 91 players to 53 by Sunday at 3 pm PT. For the bulk of players who are let go, they will have to go through the waiver wire, during which period they can be claimed by another team and placed on their active roster. But not everybody is subject to waivers during cutdown day. The ‘vested veteran’ rule For NFL players with at least four accrued seasons in the league, they are considered vested veterans and can be released outright and immediately hit free agency. They are NOT subject to waivers until after the trade deadline. How accrued seasons are calculated An accrued season is earned for any player who is on full pay status for at least six games in a single season. This includes being on the 53-man active roster, injured reserve, or the PUP list. For roster cuts, that means a team like the Seahawks could, say, “release” a vested veteran in order to get someone who is subject to waivers safely onto the active roster. Then they would be free to bring the vested veteran back at a later date and let someone else go. There are 25 vested veterans on the Seahawks who would not hit the waiver wire if let go by Sunday. Seattle Seahawks vested veterans who won’t go through waivers if cut QB Sam Darnold QB Drew Lock WR Cooper Kupp WR Rashid Shaheed TE Eric Saubert TE Nick Vannett OL Charles Cross OL Abraham Lucas OL Bobby Hart OL Josh Jones DL Leonard Williams DL Jarran Reed EDGE DeMarcus Lawrence EDGE Uchenna Nwosu EDGE Dante Fowler Jr ILB Ernest Jones IV ILB Chazz Surratt CB Trevon Diggs CB Noah Igbinoghene CB Josh Jobe S Julian Love S D’Anthony Bell S Rodney Thomas II P Michael Dickson K Jason Myers Of course, most of these listed Seahawks are firmly on the roster and are in no danger of being released. The players who could be released (either for musical chairs reasons or just to part ways) are Nick Vannett, Bobby Hart, Chazz Surratt, Trevon Diggs, Noah Igbinoghene, D’Anthony Bell, and Rodney Thomas II.

title: Seahawks Droppings: Jason Myers meltdown cements Seattle’s winless preseason
summary: Well, the 2026 preseason is finally over with the Seattle Seahawks tying the Kansas City Chiefs 9-9 on a missed 52-yard field goal by Jason Myers. Actually, the reason the game was tied in the first place was because of a missed extra point by Myers earlier in the game. More on that later. I […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 28: Place kicker Jason Myers #5 of the Seattle Seahawks misses a field goal as time expires in the fourth quarter of NFL preseason game action against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, the 2026 preseason is finally over with the Seattle Seahawks tying the Kansas City Chiefs 9-9 on a missed 52-yard field goal by Jason Myers . Actually, the reason the game was tied in the first place was because of a missed extra point by Myers earlier in the game. More on that later. I wouldn’t say that Seattle was impressive by any sense of the imagination against Kansas City, but they played well enough to win the game. Once again, there were no starters to be found on the field for the Seahawks while the Chiefs had a number of their first string get snaps including Travis Kelce, and Chris Jones. Maybe the best news of all was that there were no major injuries considering the shitshow that encompassed the trip to face the Tennessee Titans. Seahawks Droppings Jalen Milroe looked the best he has as a Seahawks QB throwing for over 200 yards and 1 TD . It would’ve looked even better if some of his teammates had made routine plays – a trend that’s been going on throughout this preseason. Milroe was credited with a fumble on a backwards pass to Jacardia Wright. Sure, the throw was a little low at waist high, but Wright needs to catch that. The next time Julian Hicks catches a pass will be the first time. I was impressed with Milroe’s decision making and accuracy overall tonight as he made some beautiful explosive passes of 40, 30, and 24 yards. Milroe also had an easy rushing TD on a read option that was (surprise, surprise) called back on a holding call. He followed that up with a TD pass to Nick Vannett. Milroe is still a work in progress, but definitely one that deserves to stick around on the roster. Yes, it is officially time to be concerned with Jason Myers. I touched on the subject last week, and Myers missed two more kicks tonight. The worst part was that neither was particularly close with a miss both wide left and wide right. All he needed for a hat trick was another one that came up short. Five missed kicks in three games is scary. Kickers are weird, man. It seems like they’re good until all of a sudden they aren’t and there’s no coming back from that. The rushing game was poor for Seattle on both sides of the ball . They were only able to manage 54 yards rushing on offense while giving up 155 rushing yards on defense. Seattle’s backup offensive lineman have played quite poorly all preseason blowing blocks and getting penalized. The game against the Chiefs was no different. Nehemiah Pritchett had a good game again tonight. He seems clearly set as the third CB behind Devon Witherspoon and Josh Jobe. Newcomer Trevon Diggs had an INT after only two practices with the team. Not too shabby. I’m not entirely convinced that Montorie Foster Jr has locked up a roster spot . Fans fret every year that the guys they cut will get scooped up by someone else, but every team has their own version of Foster. Cody White and Emmanuel Henderson Jr played well in this game and are just as deserving of a roster spot. At least the Seahawks had less than 100 penalty yards finishing with 90. This whole preseason it seems like Seattle has shot themselves in the foot on two thirds of their drives with a stupid penalty. It’s hard to dig out of a hole when you’re sitting at 1st and 20. I expect that to get cleaned up when the starters are on the field. Jamie Sheriff had two great special teams tackles while also getting some pressure off the edge . I don’t know if it was enough to get him a spot on the roster, but no one has really pulled away in that EDGE competition. I’m guessing it was just because of the lack of depth at safety, but seeing D’Anthony Bell playing into the 4th Quarter was surprising considering it seems like he’s a lock for the roster. Rodney Thomas II was back in action after an injury which was good to see. He’s still in the mix for a spot due to the Bud Clark injury. Honestly, I wouldn’t be surprised if Clark’s replacement is not yet on the roster. Maybe it’s time for a Jerrick Reed II reunion in a trade with TEN or a Nino signing after Week 1? Despite the Myers fiasco, I came away pretty encouraged with this game. The stream I was watching was the Chiefs broadcast so it was interesting to hear some of their analysis. Former Chiefs QB and current NFL Analyst Trent Green was on the broadcast and came away quite impressed with Milroe. Sometimes it’s good to get a different perspective from someone who doesn’t religiously follow the team. We can have such high expectations as fans that it colors our view of how some of the players are actually progressing. No, the Seahawks didn’t win any preseason games this year which we would’ve all liked to see. Their young players, however, did get vital reps to aid in their progression should they be called upon in the regular season. Real ball is up next, and I couldn’t be more excited!

Luter doesn’t play nickel so whose spot could he take?” Unranked and unloved by scouts, Jaden Dugger might be 49ers’ new late-round find (paywall) “On Jan. 23, 2023, his brother, Dajuan, the oldest of five siblings, died in his sleep. He was 24. Dajuan had been a quarterback at Division II Lock Haven University, setting the example for his football-playing brothers, Jaden, Dalen and Julian, a sophomore quarterback at Washington State….“Time makes it easier, but you never forget,” Dugger said. “Some days are harder than others. … Something like that is terrible, but I feel like it taught me a lot about myself. I kind of feel like I’m not playing the game for myself anymore. I definitely was before.” …[KJ] Wright was convicted by Dugger’s feel for the position. While studying video, Wright was impressed by how Dugger reacted to a reverse — taking off as if he had heard the play in the opponent’s huddle. Wright made it the second play of a highlight reel presented to head coach Kyle Shanahan. To Wright, it was evidence that the former wide receiver, cornerback, safety and pass rusher was, unquestionably, a linebacker — one who was raw but could become a star with seasoning. “He’s going to be a guy that will anticipate plays and see them before they happen,” Wright said. “That’s just a gift he has. It’s hard to coach. You just have to have the gift.” Dugger admits he once viewed another of his assets — his versatility — as a curse. When he was moved from the secondary to the defensive front after arriving at Louisiana, he was frustrated. “It was like, ‘Dang, I’m a safety. Why are they switching me?’” he said. But his mindset shifted. And his fortunes changed. Now, after overcoming Division I rejection, personal tragedy and skepticism from scouts about what, exactly, he was, he has a shot to become more than anyone imagined.” Matt Maiocco’s 53-man 49ers roster projection 4.0 ahead of the 2026 NFL season “And the medical reports will determine how the 49ers piece it together ahead of their trip to Melbourne, Australia, to face the Los Angeles Rams on Thursday, Sept. 10. “That’s why you want as long as possible,” Shanahan said. “They’re moving it up this year on Sunday with us leaving for Australia so soon. So it just makes it a little bit harder to guess where those guys are going to be. “Most of our guys, besides Ricky, are going to be all right. How good are they going to be Week 1? How good are they going to be Week 2? Those are things we’ve got to balance out.” 4 Winners and 2 losers: Is the 49ers’ defensive line depth good enough? “This kid is worth investing in. On Dinkins’ second play, the team trusted him to stay in and pass protect. He ended up helping right tackle Brandon Parker on a defensive lineman. On the next play, Dinkins drove the safety about seven yards from where he started. On the play where Jordan James ran for 17 yards, Dinkins worked to the linebacker and secured him, paving the way for James. Who knows if Dinkins ever turns into a viable pass catcher, but he is the exact type of prospect the team has drafted in the sixth round under this regime. Dinkins is a keeper. The aggression he plays with is palpable. Dinkins blocks with the intent that George Kittle would admire. He should stick on the practice squad.”

summary: The San Francisco 49ers have made a decision on their No. 3 quarterback, as they are releasing quarterback Adrian Martinez, paving the way for 2025 seventh-round pick Kurtis Rourke to make the 53-man roster as the team’s third quarterback. Martinez, 26, had thrown for 346 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions during the preseason, seeing […]
full_text: Aug 20, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; San Francisco 49ers quarterback Adrian Martinez (4) throws the ball against the Los Angeles Chargers in the second half at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The San Francisco 49ers have made a decision on their No. 3 quarterback, as they are releasing quarterback Adrian Martinez, paving the way for 2025 seventh-round pick Kurtis Rourke to make the 53-man roster as the team’s third quarterback. Martinez, 26, had thrown for 346 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions during the preseason, seeing action in all three games. He had been a long shot to make the 53-man roster after a solid offseason and initial preseason outing from Rourke, who completed 12 of 14 passes for 101 yards as the starter in the 49ers’ first preseason game. Martinez had been on the 49ers practice squad last season, being signed in August and serving as the No. 2 quarterback to Mac Jones when Brock Purdy was hurt for parts of 2025. The team signed him to a futures contract in January, and he had been competing for the No. 3 role this offseason. But the 49ers had shown interest in Rourke, who missed his entire rookie year after recovering from a torn ACL sustained in the final game of his collegiate career at Indiana. They drafted him in the seventh round last year, and he now jumps into the No. 3 quarterback role and will be the emergency quarterback on game days. Rourke’s impressive preseason start also paves the path for him to eventually be the 49ers backup once Mac Jones’s deal expires next offseason. As for Martinez, he could return to the 49ers practice squad following the 53-man roster cutdown period if no other opportunities arise.

title: How would you split the 49ers’ RB workload in 2026?
summary: There are two good things: Christian McCaffrey will be available in Week 1 of 2026, and the 49ers have a nice rookie to try out in Kaelon Black. Brian Robinson Jr., the running back behind McCaffrey last year, was a significant upgrade, and Black might be even better. Behind those two, well, whoever doesn’t get […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JULY 27: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers works out during training camp practice at SAP Performance Facility on July 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images There are two good things: Christian McCaffrey will be available in Week 1 of 2026, and the 49ers have a nice rookie to try out in Kaelon Black. Brian Robinson Jr., the running back behind McCaffrey last year, was a significant upgrade, and Black might be even better. Behind those two, well, whoever doesn’t get cut. Probably Jordan James, maybe Sincere McCormick . Black has been impressive in the preseason. So much you could overreact that he might be an heir apparent to McCaffrey—because McCaffrey isn’t going to play forever. That said, he has a lot of football left in him, but maybe, just once, the 49ers have an option that isn’t 80 percent of McCaffrey’s snaps. If anything, Black should quickly give Kyle Shanahan confidence that pulling McCaffrey for a play or two isn’t a hindrance. Something he said he finally was able to do last year when I asked this same question: “[When] Christian goes out,” Shanahan said during his segment on KNBR’s Dirty Work , “Whether it’s a run play or pass play, it’s tough. Because you know he’s such a good runner and such a good receiver. But now, when you have a really, really good back behind him, and we take Christian out and things like that, you’re not so upset on all these plays because you know you’ve got a guy coming in there who you shouldn’t miss a beat on.” Of course, McCaffrey played nearly 83 percent of the offensive snaps during the 2025 season . So apparently those plays off came few and far between. Black is a rookie; Robinson wasn’t. So the first order of business is Black getting Shanahan’s trust and holding onto it. That means holding onto the ball when he gets it. Unlike last year, snaps for a third running back might not be as necessary—if they are, something has gone horribly wrong. I remain convinced McCaffrey should get 65 percent of the snaps. Give 30 percent to Black, provided all that optimism he’s shown in the preseason doesn’t go “poof” in Weeks 1 and 2, and the remaining five to Jordan James. I’m basically saying Black should get a larger role so McCaffrey can rest, and it’s not like the 49ers offense is down a player when he takes the field. They might not miss a beat. That’s obviously asking a lot since Shanahan tends to run McCaffrey way more than many armchair GMs think he should. More likely than not, McCaffrey will be going 90 percent of the time this year simply because he’s CMC and he’s that good. That said, if we’re being logical about it, what is your pitch count between what most likely will be the 49ers’ running back room?

Yes, there was a whiffed tackle, but besides that, he’s made […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 20: San Francisco 49ers linebacker Jaden Dugger (53) gets set prior to a play during the game between the Los Angeles Chargers and the San Francisco 49ers on August 20, 2026 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood. (Photo by David Dennis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images San Francisco 49ers rookie linebacker Jaden Dugger has had a bit of talk around these parts—and all of it has been positive. Most recently, he had an impressive performance on Thursday night against the Las Vegas Raiders with 10 tackles and two quarterback hits. Yes, there was a whiffed tackle, but besides that, he’s made his case to make the 53-man roster. It’s not just linebacker either. Dugger was seen mixed in with the pass rushers earlier in August and even beat Trent Williams. 49ers linebackers coach K.J. Wright even praised Dugger’s versatility. Now, he has the eye of a Hall of Fame linebacker. 49ers legend and Pro Football Hall of Famer Patrick Willis: #53 is going to be good player. I’m seeing what Coach KJ saw. It’s subtle! Potential ↗️ — Patrick Willis (@PatrickWillis52) August 28, 2026 Getting praise from one of the best linebackers to put on the red and gold certainly helps Dugger’s case to make the 53-man roster. So do plays like this torpedo play he had on Thursday: Jaden. Dugger. 🤯 📺: KPIX pic.twitter.com/EYBqoRvmc4 — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) August 28, 2026 The 49ers have reunited Fred Warner with Dre Greenlaw. The latter has a one-year deal, and maybe Dugger is the guy to take Greenlaw’s role. The 49ers also have Tatum Bethune, who was used as Warner’s backup last year. Dugger doesn’t seem like a guy for either role. Dugger seems like the defense’s version of Deebo Samuel. A guy whom they can move around to play every position. Are we going to see plays like the one above with the Raiders in 2026? Probably not. NFL starting offensive lines during the regular season are not like the ones in the preseason. The good thing is Dugger has two great people to learn from in Dre Greenlaw and Fred Warner while he learns the NFL game. Given he’s caught the attention of the best linebacker to do it in San Francisco, maybe he can learn a bit from Willis as well.

title: Buccaneers Preseason Week 3 Winners and Losers
summary: It was a preseason finale to forget in Jacksonville Friday night, as the Buccaneers faltered to a 19-0 shutout at the hands of the Jaguars. The offense, even with dynamic undrafted rookie QB Jalon Daniels starting, could not muster even 100 total yards…all game. Preseason or not, that’s pretty gross, and in fact it was […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 28: Jack Pyburn #58 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers lines up on the line of scrimmage during their preseason matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was a preseason finale to forget in Jacksonville Friday night, as the Buccaneers faltered to a 19-0 shutout at the hands of the Jaguars. The offense, even with dynamic undrafted rookie QB Jalon Daniels starting, could not muster even 100 total yards…all game. Preseason or not, that’s pretty gross, and in fact it was the lowest total any team has posted all preseason as of this article. Nevertheless, the exhibitions end and the real festivities begin soon enough. Final cuts are due by Sunday, so we’ll do a recap of who helped themselves and who did not. Winners Ayden Garnes As if he hadn’t shown enough already, but UDFA Ayden Garnes produced some noteworthy snaps and showed how useful he can be in a reserve role. The 23-year-old out of Arizona notched 4 tackles and a pass breakup, which should more than solidify his place on the 53-man roster. Another quality UDFA find from Jason Licht’s scouting crew. Jack Pyburn College eligibility fiasco aside, Jack Pyburn has shown some serious pass-rushing chops throughout this preseason. With 2 sacks against the Jags, Pyburn leads all of the NFL with 4 total, and he also made a splash play in the run game with a tackle for loss. In what looks to be a completely remade edge rushing group (for the better), Pyburn might just force his way into the EDGE6 role behind Rueben Bain, Yaya Diaby, Al-Quadin Muhammad, David Walker, and Anthony Nelson. Losers Elijah Klein Sometimes you just need to admit defeat. The Bucs have a established an excellent draft record when it comes to finding offensive linemen, but former sixth-rounder Elijah Klein simply has not shown enough. The coaches stuck him at right tackle Friday in an effort to keep expanding his versatility, but is flexibility really that valuable when you’re not particularly good at anything you’re being asked to do? He got whipped for two sacks, displaying a clear lack of functional athleticism to hold up there. He was not the only one who struggled, far from it in fact, but Klein has not been very noteworthy on the interior this preseason or in his prior seasons either, so you have to seriously wonder if there’s any merit in trying to continue this experiment. Receiver Depth In an opportunity to make good final impressions, not many receivers made much of an impact. Garrett Greene, a converted college QB, has generated both of the team’s biggest catches all preseason (his lone catch Friday went for 18 yards) and showed promise last preseason too, but the fundamentals of the position are still a work in progress. He’s had multiple drops as well, along with route running snafus. The practice squad remains the best place for him. Kam Johnson had a bad drop as well, and it was a reminder that he’s explosive but not always a quality passing option. Dean Patterson made some highlight reel grabs in the previous two games but couldn’t put a ribbon on it, catching 2 passes for only 2 yards. It will be interesting to see how the final receiver spot and practice squad spots shake out. Devin Culp After the Bucs drafted Bauer Sharp, the writing felt on the wall for Culp, who has athletic chops but could never seem to carve out a bigger role. The last two games, Culp received 3 total targets, so either but the Bucs don’t really see the need to play him or they want to possibly stash him on the practice squad. Either way, it feels more of inevitable parting at some point or another.

title: Buccaneers preseason finale was a disappointment for many
summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers closed out the preseason Friday night with an offensive performance they will quickly want to put behind them, falling 19-0 to the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium. With Tampa Bay sitting its starters, rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels received an extended opportunity to make his case for a roster spot. But after […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 28: Bryan Thomas Jr #57 of the Jacksonville Jaguars sacks Jalon Daniels #10 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during a preseason game at EverBank Field on August 28, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers closed out the preseason Friday night with an offensive performance they will quickly want to put behind them, falling 19-0 to the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium. With Tampa Bay sitting its starters, rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels received an extended opportunity to make his case for a roster spot. But after leading five scoring drives over the first two preseason games, Daniels and the offense never found a rhythm. He completed eight of 15 passes for 57 yards, was sacked three times and finished with nine rushing yards as Tampa Bay managed just 87 total yards. The struggles went well beyond the quarterback position. The Bucs had trouble protecting Daniels, failed to establish the running game and committed a costly botched snap that handed Jacksonville possession deep in Tampa Bay territory. Head coach Todd Bowles did not sugarcoat the performance afterward. “Not good enough,” Bowles said . “Anytime you get shut out, you know. I didn’t think we protected the quarterback enough. We couldn’t run the ball. We gave up a special teams touchdown. The defense fought; they made some mistakes but at least they fought. I thought two out of the three phases didn’t show up.” Tampa Bay’s defense provided several bright spots, including sacks from Anthony Nelson and Jack Pyburn, but the headlines belong to an offense that failed to score as the Bucs finished the preseason 2-1. Several players will look at Friday’s night game as one they wish they can have back. Offensive linemen played poorly and receivers dropped pass which made the rookie quarterback’s stats look worse than what they should have been. Daniels should still make the roster. Whether he is named QB2 remains to be seen.

summary: Once the roster cut deadline of 5:00 PM Central passes on Sunday, players with less than four years of service time will be subject to waivers. All 32 teams have the chance to claim every player who falls under this category. The waiver order through week 3 of the regular season is the same as […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - AUGUST 13: A Tennessee Titans helmet is on a Gaterade cooler during a preseason NFL game between the Tennessee Titans and the San Francisco 49ers on August 13, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Once the roster cut deadline of 5:00 PM Central passes on Sunday, players with less than four years of service time will be subject to waivers. All 32 teams have the chance to claim every player who falls under this category. The waiver order through week 3 of the regular season is the same as the 2026 NFL Draft order. That means the Tennessee Titans have the 4th spot. If more than one team claims a player, the player will be awarded to the team with the highest priority waiver spot. If a player has 4 years or more of service time, they do not have to go through waivers. They are free to sign with a team as soon as they are released. Once a player clears waivers, they are free to sign with whatever team they choose. The Titans will start to fill out their practice squad from players that have cleared waivers over the next few days. Of course, if the Titans claim a player, they will have to waive a player who made the initial 53-man roster. For the player who is waived, if they have less than 4 years of service time, they will then be subject to the waiver process. The Titans are +12500 to win the Super Bowl at FanDuel Sportsbook . Anybody put any money on that?

full_text: The Daily Slop – 30 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles The Athletic (paywall) Commanders’ shaky preseason requires immediate fortification before the regular season The Commanders sat 41 players before a 41-3 loss to the Ravens, capping an ugly end to training camp which started with Baltimore’s first-team defense dominating Washington’s available starters for most of last Wednesday’s joint practice. The Ravens’ third- and fourth-teamers then smacked Washington’s around at M&T Bank Stadium for four quarters. Dan Quinn had clarified going into the week that Wednesday would be the last bit of preseason business for not just Jayden Daniels, but almost everyone on the two-deep chart. Almost no one Friday made a case for making the team that hadn’t already done so, leaving Quinn miffed. The Commanders’ OTAs and (most of) training camp point to a team that should be more competitive than last season’s 5-12 version — though a brutal schedule the first eight weeks may render that preparation moot. They point to an offense that first-year offensive coordinator David Blough spun up that could put points on the board behind a more balanced attack around Daniels. Though the long-term triceps injury to star tackle Laremy Tunsil has shaken the offensive line’s depth and potential. Still, amid the finite disappointment of this last week, alongside a mistake-filled outing in Detroit a week ago, there’s hope for a turnaround once the games start to count. The staff, including new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones, threw a lot at this group. They absorbed much of it, but there is much to clean up. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Ringer NFC East Preview: Is This the Cowboys’ Year? What’s at Stake for the Commanders I’m not saying for sure that Dan Quinn is on tilt about saving his job. But if he were on tilt about saving his job, this is what that would look like: Fire both coordinators. Hire two new coordinators who have no experience doing the job. And implement spelling bees and friendship quizzes to improve team morale. Quinn seems like a nice enough guy. And I think he can be (and has been) a good coach in the right situation. But we all know the score here. If the Commanders underperform like they did last season, Quinn will be gone, and they will try to find a young, offensive-minded head coach who can maximize Jayden Daniels’s talents. How I See It If you squint, you can see some upside for this team. But there are a lot of ifs. And the Commanders are facing the NFL’s ninth-hardest schedule . The truth is that there are as many unknowns here as there are for any team in the NFL. If some bounces go the Commanders’ way, they could be a little sleepery and compete for a playoff spot. But I think that the most likely scenario is a season stuck in mediocrity. Projected record: 8-9 To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Washington owns the No. 7 waiver priority as it works toward its initial 53-man roster The Washington Commanders officially have until 6 p.m. Sunday to cut their roster from 91 down to 53 players , a process they started Saturday night . One thing to keep in mind: no matter who is on the original list, it can and likely will change frequently before the team kicks off the season in Week 1 against the Philadelphia Eagles. Currently, Washington owns the No. 7 position in the waiver order, meaning Commanders GM Adam Peters has the priority to claim players before 25 other teams get a chance. Through the third regular-season game, the waiver wire order will reflect the 2026 NFL Draft order. The six teams that can claim players before Washington are the Las Vegas Raiders, New York Jets, Arizona Cardinals, Tennessee Titans, New York Giants, and the Cleveland Browns. For a Washington claim to succeed, none of the six teams ahead of them can put in a claim for that same player. The waiver order gives the Commanders’ front office leverage over the teams at the bottom of the stack as Washington continues working to improve the bottom of its roster. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Commanders must resist glaring waiver-wire trap from Dan Quinn’s past According to reports, the New York Jets have waived defensive lineman Mazi Smith following a brief yet underwhelming stint with the AFC East club. He was part of the trade package that sent Quinnen Williams to the Dallas Cowboys, but he didn’t do enough to make any sort of impact. Commanders should not entertain Mazi Smith waiver claims after Jets exit Of course, Quinn was the defensive coordinator in Dallas when Smith was selected No. 26 overall in the 2023 NFL Draft. His lack of consistency and effort led to his failings, and the Cowboys were only too willing to give him away in their quest to acquire a legitimate difference-maker in Williams. Quinn is extremely loyal to his players, old and new. The Commanders also have some depth concerns in the defensive trenches after losing 2024 second-round pick Johnny Newton to a torn pectoral muscle . However, they should not remotely consider Smith as a viable option. The Michigan product just doesn’t look interested in playing football most of the time. Quinn gave him countless chances as a rookie in Dallas, but he almost always fluffed his lines. Things didn’t get much better once the coach departed, and the Jets were signing guys off the street rather than giving him game time over the second half of 2025. Hinton’s departure doesn’t come as a surprise ; he really struggled this summer. The Eagles originally experimented with moving the 24-year-old to guard earlier this offseason before putting him back at offensive tackle, where he didn’t play well. Perhaps the Eagles will bring Hinton back on the practice squad if he clears waivers but I tend to think he might look for a fresh start. title: How it works: NFL Practice Squad rules, eligibility, salary, waiver wire, and more
summary: The Washington Commanders have to trim their roster down to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET today. The roster cuts will start before then, and many of those players will be signed to the team’s 17-man practice squad. Every team has to trim down from 90 or 91 players, 16 player squads Practice squads were […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - AUGUST 14: Ricky Barber #50 of the Washington Commanders reacts during the NFL preseason football game against the Miami Dolphins at Northwest Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Washington Commanders have to trim their roster down to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET today. The roster cuts will start before then, and many of those players will be signed to the team’s 17-man practice squad. Every team has to trim down from 90 or 91 players, 16 player squads Practice squads were limited to 10 players in 2019, but that was set to change with the new CBA signed in 2020. The number was going to 12 players for 2 years, and then was going to be increased to 14 players in 2022. That all changed when the uncertainty of COVID-19 hit, and the league increased practice squads to 16 players, which will once again be the limit in 2026. International Player Pathway Program Teams participating in the International Player Pathway(IPP) program can have 91-man rosters during the offseason. They can also have a 17th practice squad member for the season, but if signed to the practice squad, that player can’t be signed to the regular season roster; however, starting in 2024 he can be elevated for up to three games. If the player is kept on the 53-man roster, he is subject to waiver rules. The Washington Commanders currently have DE T.J. Maguranyanga on the roster, and he is eligible to be signed to their practice squad as the 17th member if he is waived and clears waivers. He is unlikely to be part of the 53-man roster. Practice squad players moving up to the main roster Like the last three seasons, teams have more flexibility with using practice squad players on game day. PS players can be activated on game day before the team announces their inactives (90 minutes before game time). Teams are allowed to elevate players from their practice squad to the game day roster without having to cut a member of the 53-man team. Accordingly, clubs can increase from the standard 53 to 55 players while game day active squads expand from a previous 46 to 47 players (or 48 if a team carries eight offensive linemen). Any practice squad player can be elevated and automatically reverts back to the practice squad after a game. Each practice squad player is now able to be elevated up to three times per season. To be activated a fourth time requires the player to be signed to the regular roster. During the playoffs, practice squad players have unlimited elevations. This makes it easier for teams to have players they know and trust on game day, and also not have to subject them to waivers when they are signed to the main roster and cut to get back to the practice squad as was true in the past. Veteran players Another change is the eligibility requirements for veteran players. Previously teams could have up to 4 players who had two years of NFL experience. Now teams can have 6 veterans with no limit on the amount of accrued seasons they have in the league. A player must have been on full-play status for at least six regular-season games in a given season to gain an accrued season. This includes being on the active/inactive list, injured reserve or reserve PUP. Weekly payment Practice squad players make $13,750 per week or $247,500 for 18 weeks. Veteran players with over two years of experience make a minimum of $18,350 per week or $330,300 for 18 weeks, and a maximum of $22,8590 per week or $411,300 for 18 weeks. Signing with the practice squad Teams must complete their roster cuts by Sunday August 30th at 6 p.m. ET, meaning that almost 1,200 players will be released or placed on an injury list. Teams have until Monday at noon to claim unvested players that have been waived. Vested veterans (players with a minimum of 4 accrued seasons) become free agents immediately and are able to sign with any team. Starting at 12:00 p.m. ET on August 31st, teams can begin signing players to their practice squads. Practice squad basics Practice squad players practice with the team. They do not play in games, unless they are elevated (see above) Practice squad players are paid per week and can be released at any point during the season. Practice squad players are free to sign with other NFL teams, but they have to be signed to the 53-man active roster of the acquiring team. A practice squad player cannot be signed to another practice squad unless he is first released or waived. A practice squad player cannot sign with his team’s upcoming opponent unless he does so six days before the upcoming game, or 10 days if his team is currently on a bye week. If a practice squad player is signed to the active roster, he will receive a minimum of three weekly paychecks, even if he is released before spending three weeks with the new team. In order to be signed to a practice squad after being released, a player who is not a vested veteran must first clear waivers, and is subject to waiver claims by other teams. Waiver wire The Washington Commanders had the No. 7 overall pick in this year’s draft, which means they have six teams in front of them that could potentially claim a player Washington wants. There should be plenty of players available, and Washington will be on the look out for some offensive line help next week. The waiver order goes by original draft order not counting trades. Teams maintain their places on the waiver priority list through Week 3 of the regular season. After Week 3 the waiver priority order is determined by reverse order of wins. Teams don’t lose their spot on the priority list like in fantasy football. Teams can put in as many waiver claims as they want, and will be awarded the player(s) if they are the highest-ranked claiming team. Any player added through waivers will need a corresponding roster move to make room for him on the roster. The claiming team picks up the player’s contract, not including any signing bonuses that his original team already paid. Vested veterans (on an NFL roster for at least 6 games per season, for at least 4 seasons) aren’t subject to waivers until after the trade deadline, which will be after Week 9 this season. Players who are waived/injured, and not claimed on waivers, return to their team and are placed on injured reserve unless an injury settlement is made.

title: Commanders vs. Ravens preseason Week 3: Mark Tyler’s Studs and Duds
summary: A beautiful late-summer evening in Baltimore turned into a nightmare performance for Dan Quinn and his Commanders roster hopefuls. With most of the starters and key reserves sitting this one out, there were still plenty of guys hoping to make an impact in the game for either Washington, or one of the 31 other teams […]
full_text: A beautiful late-summer evening in Baltimore turned into a nightmare performance for Dan Quinn and his Commanders roster hopefuls. With most of the starters and key reserves sitting this one out, there were still plenty of guys hoping to make an impact in the game for either Washington, or one of the 31 other teams in the league. Unfortunately, many guys may have played themselves right out of the league with bad performances… This was one of the most poorly played football games in all three phases I have ever seen from a Washington football team. They looked completely unprepared, out-coached and lacked “juice” for all four quarters. I’ve watched a lot of Washington football games in my life – preseason, regular season and playoffs. I can honestly say there was nothing about this game, with the exception of a few plays by Tyler Owens, that I enjoyed watching. This was incredibly painful to watch. — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 29, 2026 Quinn commented on how great a camp this group had in his post-game presser but lamented the fact that these last two games left a lot to be desired in terms of preparation, discipline and execution. With what looks like a plethora of roster questions still left unanswered, fans have now gone into full panic-mode just two weeks before the season opener against the Eagles . It’s just the preseason though – right? Below are my Studs and Duds of the game, followed by some notes. Studs DB Tyler Owens Owens was the lone bright spot to an otherwise embarrassing evening. The imposing safety was playing like his job was on the line, and, in my opinion, secured a spot on the 53-man roster. Playing from a deep half, he read plays correctly, covered ground quickly and arrived with violence — exactly what you want to see from a safety. He was also a standout on special teams. Tyler Owens is certainly showing he deserves to make this team! Another big hit from his safety position pic.twitter.com/8uxfj2od7T — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 28, 2026 GREAT hit right at the goal line by Tyler Owens who denies the ball carrier💪🏻 pic.twitter.com/Te4rMbsVHx — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 28, 2026 Duds WR Luke McCaffrey McCaffrey being active for this final preseason game says a lot about his potential spot on the 53-man roster. While Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs, Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown, Jaylin Lane and Antonio Williams all sat this one out, Luke was active and seemed VERY much on the bubble. Unfortunately, he did nothing to stand out. He had a drop on a slant and failed to come back to a ball on a hitch that allowed a Ravens defender to break up the pass. Although he does have return value, that may not be enough to keep him on the roster. 2nd and 10. Bunch formation – McCaffrey drops the slant. pic.twitter.com/5pVx0JKh6v — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 28, 2026 McCaffrey needs to work back to this ball. He sits and allows the defender to make a play pic.twitter.com/2TB0BgnU6y — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 28, 2026 RB Kaytron Allen Rookies fighting to make the roster need to practice good ball security. Allen’s fumble on Washington’s first offense play set the tone for what would be an incredibly rough evening for the Commanders. Fatman fumbles on Washington’s first offensive play 😡 pic.twitter.com/zViPWZOoQU — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 28, 2026 WR Jaden Bradley For the second week in a row, a rookie fighting to make the team has fumbled a kickoff. Bradley fumbles a kickoff. You won’t make the team doing this pic.twitter.com/yBBrrfY1hT — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 28, 2026 OL Julian Good-Jones Living up to the moniker I have bestowed upon him, “Bad-Jones” was every bit as bad as you could expect. It’s absolutely crazy to think that if Washington had a regular-season game tomorrow, this man may be our starting center. Shame, SHAME on Adam Peters! title: WR Diggs signing seen as most critical to 2026 success – survey results
summary: In this week’s Reacts survey conducted here at Hogs Haven, we asked readers to identify which of six high-profile free-agent acquisitions would deliver the most significant positive impact on the upcoming 2026 season. Visit our partners at FanDuel Wide receiver Stefon Diggs led the field with 47% of the total vote. Edge rusher Odafe Oweh […]
full_text: ASHBURN, VA - AUGUST 12: Stefon Diggs #18 of the Washington Commanders shares a laugh during a joint practice at BigBear.ai Performance Center on August 12, 2026 in Ashburn, Virginia. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images In this week’s Reacts survey conducted here at Hogs Haven, we asked readers to identify which of six high-profile free-agent acquisitions would deliver the most significant positive impact on the upcoming 2026 season. Visit our partners at FanDuel Wide receiver Stefon Diggs led the field with 47% of the total vote. Edge rusher Odafe Oweh drew the second-most support at 29%. A deeper look into the survey results reveals nuanced viewpoints regarding roster construction, financial investments, and how these acquisitions position the franchise to defy lackluster national narratives about the 2026 Washington Commanders. The wide receiver room: ceiling & floor The 47% support for Stefon Diggs confirms that many fans view having a true perimeter weapon as a key catalyst for offensive improvement and team success in 2026. However, the fact remains that he drew less than half the votes in our survey. Some of those who didn’t vote for Diggs argued against the receiver’s prime importance on the grounds of diminishing marginal returns. In other words, with Terry McLaurin firmly established as the primary target in Washington’s passing game, some fans felt that adding another high-volume receiver yields a lower incremental impact than addressing other roster deficiencies. Certainly, in a fully healthy offense, Diggs and McLaurin will naturally eat into each other’s target shares, potentially flattening the statistical ceiling of the individual investment. But one of the driving forces behind the signing of Diggs a week into training camp was rooted in the lessons of the 2025 season. When McLaurin missed 7 games last season due to injury, the offense’s lack of receiving depth was exposed. With Scary Terry missing and a injured Noah Brown out for 13 games as well, the passing game stagnated and opposing secondaries easily suffocated Washington’s remaining pass catchers. Signing Diggs is as much a floor-raising insurance policy as it is a ceiling-raising luxury. The presence of two 1,000-yard receivers ensures that if injury strikes the receiving corps again, the offense will still likely be able to field an elite route-runner capable of sustaining the passing game. When both are on the field, it forces defensive coordinators into a schematic bind, preventing them from consistently shading safety help toward the team’s only real passing game threat. Re-making the defense: Oweh and the $96 million mandate While Diggs received more support in our survey, Odafe Oweh represents the franchise’s largest financial commitment of the offseason. Oweh signed a four-year, $96 million contract, making it the most lucrative contract executed by the Commanders with an external free agent since Albert Haynesworth was inked to a disastrous 7-year, $100m deal in 2009. As expensive as it might be, per Over the Cap, with an average annual value of $24m, this deal ranks only 17 th among edge rushers and falls far short of the league’s top-6 contracts in the position group, each of which is valued at between $40m and $50m per year. Yet, evaluating Oweh’s impact solely through individual box-score metrics like sacks may miss the broader strategic picture. Under new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones, Washington is transitioning to an aggressive, pressure-heavy defensive scheme. His system is expected to rely on dictating matchups and using multiple fronts to create internal and external confusion for opposing offensive lines. Oweh is not being asked to carry an otherwise barren pass rush; rather, he is expected to serve as the “lead dog” of a deep and talented rotational group. By pairing Oweh’s elite athletic profile with a wave of fresh situational rushers, Jones can maintain a relentless standard of pressure throughout four quarters. Oweh’s value will be measured by how his pressure off the edge frees up interior gap shooters, stressing the quarterback and creating opportunities for his teammates. Oweh’s contract reflects the premium placed on a foundational edge setter – but not an elite one-man wrecking crew — who can trigger the tactical components of Jones’s new scheme. Defying the national calculus Beyond the individual impact of Diggs and Oweh, the survey results reflect an undercurrent of optimism among Commanders fans that stands in stark contrast to national projections. Across major sportsbooks and national media previews, the Commanders are largely being discounted, with win totals and power rankings that reflect memories of Washington’s disappointing 2025 record, and which take little or no notice of the significant coaching changes and dramatic roster upheaval that took place this offseason. For sophisticated fans looking at these underlying factors rather than relying on outdated prior year standings, there are at least three reasons to believe the national consensus is projecting the wrong trajectory for Washington in 2026: A complete conceptual overhaul: The arrival of two new coordinators completely resets the schematic identity of the team. The predictable, easily countered schemes of 2025 – particularly on defense — have been replaced by modern, adaptable systems on both sides of the ball. National models frequently struggle to quantify the statistical jump that occurs when a roster is invigorated by fresh approaches in coaching. Defensive roster metamorphosis: Looking at last year’s defensive metrics to project 2026 performance is fundamentally flawed. Due to tectonic offseason changes, the defensive coordinator and aggressive scheme, along with more than half of the defensive starters, will be new to the organization this season. Washington has systematically replaced low-ceiling depth with proven or high-potential scheme-specific veterans and draft picks. Regression to the (injury) mean: In 2025, Washington was one of the NFL teams most severely impacted by adjusted games lost due to injury. NFL history demonstrates that extreme injury luck—good or bad—is rarely sustained from year to year. By simply regressing to the league average in health, the Commanders would be positioned to experience an organic boost in continuity and performance. Outlook The Reacts survey demonstrates that the fan base recognizes the strategic logic behind the Commanders’ offseason roster haul. Diggs provides critical stability and redundancy to the perimeter, while Oweh gives Daronte Jones the elite chess piece required to unlock his defensive vision. While national analysts remain anchored to the results from 2025, the critical changes in coaching, health, and personnel suggest that Washington has built a new and different team, still fueled by its franchise quarterback, Jayden Daniels, that is likely to surprise the disbelieving broader universe of NFL media, analysts and fans in 2026. Jean-Baptiste missed much of last season due to a pectoral injury and didn’t show much in the early going of camp. If Washington’s outside linebackers finished camp healthy and available, Jean-Baptiste may have been hard-pressed to get a spot, but Armstrong’s suspension and injuries to Oweh (calf) and Chaisson (knee) — Quinn has not provided a timetable for their return — make it worth keeping him. Cornerback (5): Mike Sainristil, Amik Robertson, Trey Amos, Rasul Douglas, Fabian Moreau There are a number of outstanding questions about this group, none bigger than the availability of Amos. The 2025 second-round pick was Washington’s most consistent corner last year, but a fractured fibula cut his season short and cost him the entire offseason. He returned two weeks into camp but suffered an ankle sprain in his second practice. It’s unclear if he will be available for Week 1. Washington added Douglas and Moreau to give the team more veteran experience and depth, and both proved their worth. Whenever Amos returns, it’ll be interesting to see whether Robertson or Sainristil shifts inside to the slot. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Bullock’s Film Room Washington Commanders Initial 53-man Roster Projection [There are] two factors in deciding to keep three quarterbacks for me. The first is the injury Marcus Mariota suffered in the preseason opener against Miami. It’s expected he’ll be back in time for the opening game of the season, but if there’s any sort of setback or delay in that return, then you need a third quarterback. Even if he is healthy enough to play, he hasn’t practiced in weeks so he might be lacking sharpness. So it feels wise to keep a third quarterback on the roster just in case. But the second and more prominent reason to keep a third quarterback is Kaliakmanis’ performances. He’s played so well so far in the preseason that I think he’s earned a spot on the 53. I know a lot of fans will speculate about another team claiming him if they cut him and try to stash him on the practice squad, but I don’t think that would be so much of a risk. If you’re looking for a quarterback during roster cut down day, it’s either because your starter or back up is injured. If you need a starter, you’re searching around the NFL for a more established player than Kaliakmanis and probably trying to trade for him. If you need a back up, you’re likely looking for someone with familiarity in your system that can come in and be ready to go right away. It’s pretty rare that you see teams claim a rookie quarterback that they could have drafted with any pick higher than 223rd overall pick a few months ago. So I do think if Washington really wants to save a roster spot and stash Kaliakmanis on the practice squad, where he can still be designated as the emergency third quarterback on game day, then I think they’d probably manage to do it without anyone claiming him. But based on his preseason performances so far (obviously he could have a terrible outing against Baltimore tonight and change the equation here), I think he’s earned his spot on the 53. If you subscribe to the theory of just keeping your best 53 players, I think Kaliakmanis has been one of their best 53. That would lead me to rewarding that performance level with a roster spot. Friday’s showing dropped the number of wide receivers from seven to six, though whether Washington does ultimately find a trade suitor as some have speculated could be worth tracking. TE (4): Chig Okonkwo, John Bates, Ben Sinnott, Colson Yankoff Skinny: the top of the room is clear with Okonkwo now anchoring the room while Bates returns as the in-line blocker and Sinnott as a secondary receiving threat. Yet with an offense that’s expected to feature two tight end sets, coupled with a strong offseason, Yankoff could be another piece in the room. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Commanders’ final 53-man roster prediction after intense preseason battles Defensive Line (5): Daron Payne, Javon Kinlaw, Tim Settle Jr., Charles Omenihu, Ricky Barber The Washington Commanders were dealt another blow on their defensive front after Johnny Newton suffered a torn pectoral muscle that required surgery, ending any hopes of his breakout campaign. Daronte Jones will have to make the best of a bad situation, and it places even more pressure on the starting trio to stay healthy. Daron Payne, Javon Kinlaw, and free-agent signing Tim Settle Jr. have the scope to be productive. Charles Omenihu offers versatility and proven production. Deatrich Wise Jr. would have been the call, but he hasn’t practiced all summer and could land on the physically unable to perform list to start the season, paving the way for Ricky Barber to make the team. Linebacker (4): Sonny Styles, Frankie Luvu, Leo Chenal, Jordan Magee Washington’s linebacking corps will be a real strength, or at least it should be. But that doesn’t make it any easier to figure out who’ll be on the team to start the campaign. Frankie Luvu is moving back to his off-ball role in a contract year. Free-agent signing Leo Chenal fits the athletic, explosive prototype Daronte Jones is looking for. No. 7 overall selection Sonny Styles has all the makings of a franchise cornerstone, even if he is coming in for some extremely harsh criticism on social media right now. Behind them is the intriguing part. Jordan Magee and Kain Medrano both offer special-teams value, but Ale Kaho has also made a strong push for roster consideration. full_text: The Washington Commanders have to cut their roster down to 53 players by Sunday’s 6 p.m. ET deadline. That means 38 players will either be released, traded, or placed on an injury list as the team prepares for the start of the 2026 regular season, a division game against the Eagles in Philadelphia. FanDuel Week 1 Odds Washington +5.5 , 46.5 O/U Commanders +134 Eagles -235 Most spots on the roster are already known, with only a few left to determine by depth needs and special teams contributions. The Commanders played the Ravens Friday night in the preseason finale and had 41 players inactive . If a player is waived but not claimed by another team after 1 p.m. ET on Monday, they are eligible to be a part of Washington’s 16-man practice squad, though that group can reach 17 players if it includes someone from the International Pathway Program . The NFL’s waiver system can be complicated, so let’s break it down for you: Which Washington Commanders are subject to waivers? Johnson S Quindell Johnson WR Jacoby Jones DE Joshua Josephs LB Ale Kaho QB Athan Kaliakmanis S Qwuantrezz Knight WR Jaylin Lane LB Jordan Magee DE T.J. Maguranyanga S Quan Martin DT Jeffrey M’ba WR Luke McCaffrey TE Tre’ McKitty LB Kain Medrano TE Quentin Moore WR Nick Nash DT Jer’Zhan Newton S Tyler Owens OL Nicholas Petit-Frere CB Darius Rush CB Mike Sainristil TE Ben Sinnott K Drew Stevens LB Sonny Styles OL Tanoa Togiai CB Car’lin Vigers WR Antonio Williams TE Colson Yankoff How waivers work in the NFL When a player is ‘waived,’ he is subject to the waiver wire, where any team can claim him and assume his current contract. Currently, the waiver wire order (listed below) is dependent on the NFL Draft order from this past April, but without any trades. Every team that is interested in acquiring a player will file its waiver claim in the same time window, but only the team with the highest spot in the order will successfully ‘claim’ the player and his current contract. Which NFL players are subject to waivers? Whether or not a player is put on the waiver wire or becomes a free agent depends on a player’s NFL service time. Six games active in a season earns a player an accrued season. Players with at least four years of accrued NFL service time are released outright (not subject to waivers). In this case, upon release, the player’s contract ends and he immediately becomes an unrestricted free agent who is eligible to sign with any team. However, as described above, if a player has less than four years of service time, he is subject to waiver wire claims. Any player who is not claimed after being waived is eligible to sign wherever he’d like, including his former team’s practice squad. Mainly, the group of players who get waived comprises those who are currently not eligible for unrestricted free agency status entering the year — Exclusive Rights Free Agents (less than three years of service) or Restricted Free Agents (three years of service). What is the NFL waiver order right now? The NFL waiver order during the preseason and the first three weeks of the regular season mirrors the 2026 NFL Draft order (absent trades). Once we get through three games, the waiver order resets weekly to the current NFL standings. So, until Week 4, the Raiders have first crack at every player on waivers. The Washington Commanders had the No. 7 pick in this year’s draft, selecting Ohio State linebacker Sonny Styles. They are also seventh in the waiver wire list, meaning there are six teams ahead of them to claim any eligible players that get released over the next month.
